In particular, we establish implications among these conditions and identify cases in which the implications are strict, thereby clarifying their relative strengths. Our results provide a unified perspective on existing regularity assumptions and offer guidance for selecting appropriate conditions in the complexity analysis of first-order methods.

papers.title: 3D Neural Rendering for Automated Ultrasonic Laser Scans
papers.abstract: Laser doppler vibrometer (LDV) scans can be used to detect defects and cracks in manufactured parts before they are deployed. This work presents a method for reconstructing the steady-state surface wavefield of a three-dimensional part by combining automated robotic manipulation with neural rendering. A six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) robotic manipulator (UFactory xArm6) with an embedded piezoelectric transducer presented an acoustically excited test article to a stationary LDV at a sequence of known orientations, yielding a set of complex-valued 2D scans with poses derived analytically from the arm kinematics rather than from image-based pose estimation. These scans were used to train a novel complex-nerfacto model, a modified Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) pipeline that replaces the standard three-channel RGB output head with a two-channel output. Complex-nerfacto represents the real and imaginary velocity components of a wavefield, preserving the complex measurement without quantization. Reconstructions of a welded aluminum cylinder and a welded T-bracket were evaluated against measured scans using Z-normalized cross-correlation (ZNCC). The complex-valued pipeline achieved a mean ZNCC of 0.60 at held-out viewing angles, compared with 0.28 for a baseline RGB nerfacto model trained on rendered images of the same data. The resulting surface wavefield reconstructions supported defect detection and characterization on complex components. We identify geometry reconstruction from sparse LDV scans as the remaining obstacle to practical deployment.

papers.title: Physics-informed X-ray tomography of magnetization and material parameters
papers.abstract: Three-dimensional spin textures are stabilized by microscopic interactions within their host materials. X-ray vector tomography can image these nanoscale structures, but weak magnetic contrast and a limited range of viewing angles often leave parts of the magnetization poorly determined. Here we show that a reconstruction constrained by the micromagnetic energy recovers the three-dimensional magnetization from such data and gains sensitivity to the underlying material interactions. Applied to the chiral magnet Co$_8$Zn$_9$Mn$_3$, the method resolves the three-dimensional helical texture even from a small fraction of the dual-axis projections typically required for a successful tomographic reconstruction, or from a single tilt axis alone. By testing which ratio of exchange to Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction in the reconstruction best reproduces the measured projections, we obtain a value for the sample that differs by about 10 % from the literature value derived from the helical winding period. Taken together, our findings suggest a way to reduce the time needed for vector tomography and to extend it to determining fundamental magnetic interactions in a material.

papers.title: Estimating cosmogenic backgrounds in nEXO at SNOLAB using Geant4 and FLUKA
papers.abstract: The nEXO experiment was designed to search for neutrinoless double beta decay in the isotope $^{136}$Xe, using a five-tonne, isotopically-enriched liquid xenon time projection chamber (TPC). To meet nEXO's sensitivity goal, significant effort is placed on background mitigation strategies. Here, we evaluate the expected cosmogenic background rate for nEXO if placed at its preferred underground host site, SNOLAB. A comparison of results from Geant4 and FLUKA Monte Carlo simulations are presented. We perform detailed Monte Carlo simulations of muons reaching the underground SNOLAB environment using both Geant4 and FLUKA to study the production of radioactive isotopes from both direct spallation reactions or subsequent neutron-induced reactions. We find that, of the isotopes produced, the only one of concern for nEXO is $^{137}$Xe, produced by neutron capture on the xenon target. We develop a veto strategy that achieves an anticipated 92\% \xe{137} rejection efficiency while keeping dead time to less than 1 day over a 10 year exposure.

papers.title: WeSearch: A Unified Model-Centric Retrieval Framework for WeChat Search
papers.abstract: We present WeSearch, a unified, model-centric retrieval framework for large-scale, continuously evolving content search. Prevailing methods assign documents fixed hierarchical Semantic IDs, implicitly assuming each document follows a single coherent semantic path-an assumption that often breaks down for multi-topic documents. WeSearch instead retrieves query-relevant clusters and then ranks atomic documents within the resulting query-specific candidate space, decoupling candidate pruning from fine-grained relevance modeling. Combined with relevance-aware training, compact document representations, and incremental index updates, this design enables weekly-or daily when needed-model refreshes. Deployed as the primary semantic retrieval path in WeChat Search alongside a lexical syntax tree, WeSearch shows consistent one-week A/B gains on corpora from hundreds of millions to billions of documents, and a one-month full-traffic A/B test confirms stable improvements of +0.68% CTR and +2.27% per-user article clicks, together with a 41% reduction in retrieval resource cost and a 19 ms reduction in graphic-text retrieval latency. WeSearch is now fully deployed in WeChat Search, serving 100% of production traffic.

papers.title: A closed formula for the Poisson cohomology of scalar Dubrovin-Novikov brackets in arbitrary dimension
papers.abstract: The structure of the Poisson cohomology groups for scalar Poisson brackets of Dubrovin-Novikov type with $D$ independent variables has been first described in arXiv:1512.05744 ; in that work, a complete dimensional counting was provided for $D=2$, and some numerical results exhibited for $D=3$, $D=4$. Here, we prove a formula for the dimensional counting of the Poisson cohomology for arbitrary $D$. Moreover, we show how to obtain canonical representatives for each cohomology class.

papers.title: When Does Spatial Cooperation Help? Contamination Regimes in Decentralized Online Spectrum Anomaly Learning
papers.abstract: Learning-based spectrum monitors adapt online to benign propagation changes, but persistent rogue transmissions can gradually become incorporated into the learned background. Spatially distributed receivers provide additional evidence for detecting such anomalies, while decentralized model mixing can also spread contamination to receivers with clean measurements. We study this tradeoff using a decentralized online learner with sample gating and model sharing. We show that, without defenses, contamination propagation is governed by the occupancy rate and is independent of cross-receiver correlation. In contrast, the benefit of spatial fusion depends strongly on correlation and the detector operating point, so cooperation can either improve or degrade detection. We also show that fragmented transmissions can evade gating based on temporally smoothed statistics. Combining smoothed and per-sample gating substantially improves robustness to such intermittent contamination.

papers.title: Machine Learning Aided Computational Discovery of Boride Substrates for Borophene Synthesis
papers.abstract: Borophene, a monolayer of boron, is distinctive among two-dimensional materials owing to its unique properties, including polymorphism and potential applications in quantum technologies and energy conversion and storage. Nevertheless, its applications are hindered by the strong binding of borophene to metal substrates, which impedes the realization of freestanding borophene. Alternative substrates with tunable binding to borophene are therefore highly desirable. Since boride layers arise during borophene synthesis on metals, borides provide potential alternative substrates for borophene synthesis. In this work, we investigate the binding energies and interactions between borophene and 1356 boride surfaces for two borophene phases (v1/6 and v1/9), using density functional theory (DFT) calculations and machine learning (ML). Importantly, incorporating ML-predicted charge transfer as an input feature to a subsequent ML model enables physics-informed predictions of binding energies. Additional DFT calculations on four representative cases were performed to validate the ML predictions. SHAP analysis reveals that the majority of key descriptors are associated with delocalized electrons, highlighting the role of electronic properties in governing binding strength. Combined DFT and ML screening identifies 65 and 73 promising boride surfaces for the v1/6 and v1/9 phases, respectively. Al- and Ag-based borides, including AlB2 and AgB2, emerge as predominant candidates for both phases. The computationally predicted candidate substrates and the deduced design guidelines provide a charge-transfer-informed ML strategy for substrate selection and represent promising steps toward the experimental realization of freestanding borophene.

papers.title: Nodeless $d$-wave superconductivity driven by charge fluctuations in monolayer FeSe on SrTiO$_3$
papers.abstract: Monolayer FeSe and Fe(Te,Se) grown on SrTiO$_3$ exhibit some of the highest superconducting transition temperatures among iron-based superconductors, yet their pairing mechanism and symmetry remain elusive. Motivated by the recent surprising discovery of nodeless $d$-wave superconductivity using scanning Josephson tunneling microscopy (SJTM) [T. Wei et al., arXiv:2610.38421 (2026)], we investigate superconductivity in monolayer FeSe/SrTiO$3$ (1L-FeSe/STO) within an extended Hubbard model incorporating both onsite and intersite Coulomb interactions among Fe $3d$ and Se $4p$ orbitals. We show that Fe-Se intersite Coulomb repulsion strongly enhances small-momentum $p$-$d$ charge-transfer fluctuations, which mediate attractive intraorbital spin-singlet pairing interactions. These electronic fluctuations may be further enhanced by forward-scattering optical phonons of the SrTiO$3$ substrate. The resulting intrapocket attraction, together with residual repulsive interpocket interactions, stabilizes a mirror-odd, nodeless $B_{1g}$ ($d$-wave) superconducting state with opposite gap signs on the two electron pockets. Both Fe $t_{2g}$ and Se $4p$ orbitals contribute substantially to this multiorbital superconductivity. The calculated superconducting gap and density of states exhibit a two-peak structure, while the Josephson tunneling conductance displays a half-lattice-period modulation, in excellent agreement with experimental observations. Our results establish electronic charge-transfer fluctuations as a viable pairing mechanism for unconventional nodeless $d$-wave superconductivity in monolayer FeSe/STO.

papers.title: Dynamic programming principle for controlled systems driven by fractional Brownian motions and related backward stochastic Riccati equations
papers.abstract: This work aims to study the stochastic optimal control problems of controlled stochastic differential systems driven by both Brownian motions and fractional Brownian motions via dynamic programming principle. The stochastic Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation is obtained. Different from the classical case, the obtained stochastic Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation is a backward stochastic partial differential equation driven by both fractional Brownian motions and standard Brownian motions, whose solution is a pair of random fields. For linear quadratic optimal control problem this backward stochastic partial differential equation is explicitly solved by relating it to a backward stochastic Riccati equation.

papers.title: Dual-Axis Policy Entailment: A Benchmark for Policy-Change Reasoning
papers.abstract: Whether a policy shifts domains and, by extension, continues, broadens, narrows, or reverses previous policy is of paramount importance to the study of public policy. We propose Dual-Axis Policy Entailment (DAPE), which evaluates an ordered pair of policy directives on both dimensions at once: a binary judgment determines whether the two directives govern the same policy domain, and a five-way judgment determines whether the later directive continues, broadens, narrows, or reverses the earlier policy, or governs a different domain altogether. Read together, the two judgments form one five-category label, our primary metric. The two-axis design captures two central dimensions of policy change without conflating errors on either dimension into a generic "irrelevant" label, and it makes annotation more rigorous: a coder cannot dismiss a difficult pair as domain-irrelevant without an explicit, checkable decision. We introduce an expert-annotated benchmark of 1,000 ordered directive pairs drawn from a large corpus of Chinese government policy, together with an annotation-calibration protocol (an adjudication packet with pre/post agreement measurement) that we contribute as a methodological artifact. Fourteen open-weight models and four frontier API flagships fail the task zero-shot: even the best frontier flagship's chance-corrected agreement with expert labels is far below the human ceiling (Cohen's $κ\approx 0.29$ vs. $0.53$). A fine-tuned open-weight model (LoRA SFT of Qwen3-14B, five-fold cross-validation) closes this gap, reaching the coder-mutual human ceiling ($κ= 0.524$ vs. $0.527$). Finally, we apply our method to China's AI policy (1980-2024) and map the direction of policy change across eras.

papers.title: Gravitational Capture of Large Interstellar Planetesimals by Collapsing Prestellar Cores
papers.abstract: We investigate the capture of free-floating planetesimals by the time-varying gravitational potential of a collapsing prestellar core. We use one-dimensional collapse models to estimate the volume of space from which planetesimals are captured. We combine this calculation with an estimate of the size distribution and velocity dispersion of the free-floating planetesimal population to determine the largest planetesimal that is typically captured, as well as the total mass of all planetesimals captured by a given protostar. We consider two cases: one in which the free-floating planetesimal population comes from the birth cluster of the star, and one in which the planetesimals are captured from the Galactic population of free-floating planetesimals. We find that the details of the collapse matter substantially, with the predicted diameter of the largest captured body from the Galactic population ranging from $2.8$ km to $6.4$ km depending on collapse model, and the largest body from our model birth cluster environment ranging from $70$ km to $1200$ km, for assumed velocity dispersions ranging from 0.7 to 8.5 km/s. The total solid mass captured by this mechanism does not exceed 0.07 Earth masses in all cases. We discuss the effect of these captured objects on the planet formation process, and argue that while the total solid mass captured is likely not significant, the largest captured bodies may grow to planet size via accretion of pebbles present in their host disks. This process may accelerate planet formation, or enable it in disks that have difficulty in forming their own planetesimals.

papers.title: Robust Inference for Spiked Eigenspace under Elliptical Distributions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study two eigenspace testing problems under high-dimensional elliptical spiked models: whether the spiked eigenspace equals a given subspace, and whether a given vector is a spike eigenvector. We propose a \textbf{Robust Functional Projection} (RFP) test and a \textbf{Robust Spike Direction} (RSD) test for these two problems, respectively. Based on the spatial-sign covariance matrix $\bm C_n$, both tests achieve robustness by remaining invariant to the radial distribution without moment conditions and allowing the background level to be unknown. To construct and analyze both tests, we establish central limit theorems for \textbf{G}eneralized \textbf{E}lliptical \textbf{S}patial-sign \textbf{S}pectral statistics (GESS) $\operatorname{tr}\{f(\bm C_n)\bm B_n\}$. The results cover a general class of deterministic weighting matrices $\bm B_n$ whose ranks are either comparable to the dimension or of smaller order, providing a common theoretical foundation for both tests. The central idea in constructing both tests is to avoid the need for consistent estimations of individual spike eigenvalues by working directly with GESS. Simulations illustrate the finite-sample performance of the procedures, and an analysis of LOCATA acoustic data demonstrates their use in assessing a signal subspace and a steering direction, both constructed from measured source and array geometry.

papers.title: Faster Imitation by Re-timing Demonstrations Within the Controller Limit
papers.abstract: Imitation policies inherit the operator's pace, and re-timing the demonstrations to run faster works only until success collapses at two to three times demonstration speed. Recent methods attribute that collapse to distribution shift and answer it with finer rules for which segments may be sped up; we show it has a mechanical cause that segment selection cannot address. A low-level controller realises only a bounded displacement per control period, so merging consecutive commands produces sums outside that bound: training pairs that promise a transition the plant cannot deliver. The share of such pairs in the re-timed data, which we call the exceed share, tracks where the retrained policy collapses. The rule that follows has a single parameter: merge greedily while the sum stays realisable. Every command is then realisable by construction, the demonstrated geometry is preserved, and the speed-up lands only where the demonstrator left slack. On four simulated robomimic tasks, 200 held-out seeds per cell, a merge cap of two is at or above the frozen policy's success on all four, by 14 points on Square, and shortens the successful episodes. At matched tempo, uniform re-timing loses 9 and 16 points on Can and ToolHang, is within noise on the other two, and reaches zero on the hardest at 2x. Placement also matters: no shuffled, entropy-guided or speed-conditioned alternative beats the rule on three of the four tasks, by margins the exceed share alone does not explain; on the fourth, at a tempo the task absorbs, every placement lands in the same band. The same principle carries to a simulated humanoid whole-body tracker: re-timing 429 reference motions within its velocity envelope succeeds on 71% of clips at 2.3x, against 51% for uniform time scaling at 2x.

papers.title: RIXS study of strain-tuned coupled valence and spin-state transition in epitaxial $(\mathrm{Pr}_{0.85}\mathrm{Y}_{0.15})_{0.7}\mathrm{Ca}_{0.3}\mathrm{CoO}_{3}$ films
papers.abstract: Strain-tuned $(\mathrm{Pr}_{0.85}\mathrm{Y}_{0.15})_{0.7}\mathrm{Ca}_{0.3}\mathrm{CoO}_{3}$ thin films provide a model system for controlling coupled valence, spin-state, structural and metal-insulator transitions (VSSTs) in perovskite cobaltite materials. Here, we use Co $L_{2,3}$ and Pr $M_{4,5}$ X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy (XAS), along with Co $L_{3}$ edge Resonant Inelastic X-ray Scattering (RIXS), to probe the local electronic structure across the strain-controlled VSST in epitaxial (Pr,Y,Ca)CoO$_{3}$ thin films. In compressively strained films on YAlO$_{3}$ (YAO) substrates, cooling through the transition produces Pr$^{4+}$-like spectral weight, suppresses Co$^{4+}$-like character, and favors predominantly low-spin Co$^{3+}$. The changes at the Pr and Co edges are quantitatively consistent with a reduction of approximately 0.15 holes per Co in the Co--O network. By contrast, tensile-strained thin films on La$_{0.18}$Sr$_{0.82}$Al$_{0.59}$Ta$_{0.41}$O$_{3}$ (LSAT) substrates have nearly temperature-independent spectra. Multiplet calculations reproduce the principal XAS lineshapes and local $dd$ excitations at high energy loss. Additionally, low-energy RIXS intensity recovered above the transition is consistent with a combination of Co$^{4+}$-like local excitations and a broader particle--hole continuum associated with the metallic phase. These results provide element-resolved evidence for charge compensation between the Pr and Co--O sublattices and support cooperative coupling among charge-transfer, spin-state, and lattice structure at the strain-controlled VSST.

papers.title: Exact scalarization thresholds and onset laws for a nonminimally coupled scalar field on the Ellis wormhole
papers.abstract: We study a real scalar field nonminimally coupled to curvature on a fixed Ellis wormhole background. The scalar perturbation decouples at linear order, and the substitution $ x=a \tan z $ reduces its static radial equation to a trigonometric Pöschl-Teller problem. This yields the exact threshold spectrum $ ζ_{n\ell}=(n+\ell+1)^2/2 $, closed-form Gegenbauer profiles, and an exact count of negative radial eigenvalues in each angular sector. The s-wave thresholds are zero-energy resonances at which the growth rate rises linearly, whereas the $ \ell \geq1\ $ threshold states are square integrable and the growth rate rises as a square root. At the first threshold we also obtain the next-order term, $ σa=(π/4)g-(3π/16)g^2+O(g^3) $ with $g=2ζ-1 $. For a probe field with quartic self-interaction, we show that no nontrivial spherical static solution exists for $ζ\leq1/2 $ and derive local branch expansions near the s-wave thresholds. Numerical evolutions are consistent with saturation on the nodeless branch. These nonlinear results refer to the probe-field model; they do not establish the existence or stability of fully backreacted scalarized wormholes.

papers.title: Multiplicity and Uniqueness of Stationary Expected Payoffs in Coalitional Bargaining
papers.abstract: I study uniqueness of stationary expected payoffs in random-proposer coalitional bargaining with transferable utility. Proposer independence of coalition surplus does not guarantee uniqueness, even when the surplus is strictly monotone and every equilibrium features immediate agreement. For $M^\natural$-concave characteristic functions, including non-monotone ones, I show that stationary expected payoffs are unique and continuous in the primitives, provided that every equilibrium features immediate agreement. To prove uniqueness, I identify an equitable grouping property of maximizing coalitions and show that $M^\natural$-concavity implies it at every no-delay candidate payoff vector. Using equitable grouping, I show that every no-delay equilibrium payoff vector is isolated and has positive local index. For parameter changes that preserve immediate agreement in every equilibrium, a uniform increase in a player's contribution to every coalition containing her strictly increases her expected payoff, while an increase in her discount factor weakly increases it. I apply these results to joint ventures with coordination costs and government formation with ministerial expertise.

papers.title: FIXP-Completeness in Second-Price Auctions
papers.abstract: Computing equilibria is a fundamental algorithmic problem in game theory and economics. Although general frameworks are available for proving membership in FIXP, the class capturing exact fixed-point computation, establishing FIXP-completeness often remains challenging. We prove FIXP-completeness of exact equilibrium computation in three second-price auction models: (1). pacing with return-on-investment constraints, with multiplier cap $1+δ$ for every fixed rational $δ>0$ [Filos-Ratsikas, Hansen, Høgh, and Hollender (2024)]; (2). budget-constrained generalized second-price sponsored shopping [Hansen, Li, and Nie (2026)]; (3). budget-constrained throttling [Liu (2026)]. These results resolve open questions on the exact complexity of automated bidding. Our technical ingredient is a FIXP-complete generalized-circuit problem using only clipped affine gates and the reciprocal $x\mapsto1/(1+τx)$, for any fixed positive rational $τ$. This gate basis provides a common framework for the three auction reductions: simulating these gates in each model establishes FIXP-hardness without directly implementing multiplication or squaring.

papers.title: Skill++: Towards Lifelong Agents via Routing-Aware Skill Refinement
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents extend their capabilities with skills, each with a name, a description, and a body. Under progressive disclosure, an LLM router selects skills by name and description alone and loads only the selected bodies. Skill libraries grow continually as users and agents add new skills. Because the router relies on this metadata, a similar new skill can displace an earlier one, breaking previously correct routing even though the earlier skill and the router are unchanged. This routing interference is aggravated for public skills, whose descriptions may not match their bodies. We formulate the problem as lifelong skill routing, a class-incremental continual learning problem. A solution must keep earlier skills selectable without suppressing new ones. Existing approaches fall short, since continually retraining the router risks catastrophic forgetting and rewriting methods either ignore similar skills or require per-skill feedback. We therefore propose Skill++, which rewrites only the name and description of each incoming skill, without router training or labeled data. The new description states what the body supports, how the skill differs from its closest predecessor, and what related work it excludes. As a library grows to 731 skills over ten sessions, Skill++ selects all required skills for 76.3% of queries, versus 36.4% under the original metadata. Across three benchmarks and five LLM routers, it outperforms all compared approaches, and its gains carry over to the Codex CLI agent harness.

papers.title: The Fluctuation-Dissipation Theorem and Dynamical Love Number in Schwarzschild Black Holes
papers.abstract: We study the real-time response of a Schwarzschild black hole in the Hartle-Hawking state to an external massless scalar field. Using a complexified radial contour to represent the Schwinger-Keldysh closed time path, we describe dissipation, thermal fluctuations and conservative tidal response within a common framework. Before performing tidal matching, we derive the equilibrium fluctuation-dissipation relation directly from the radial construction for every scalar multipole at arbitrary real frequency. In the low-frequency tidal expansion, we recover the known relation between the logarithmic running of the conservative dynamical Love coefficient at order $ω^2$ and the leading dissipative response at order $ω$. We explain how the same leading absorptive coefficient enters both relations at low frequency and trace the unit coefficient of the running relation to the Schwarzschild horizon slope. In the Hartle-Hawking state, this common coefficient relates the logarithmic running directly to the zero-frequency thermal noise. Kubo-Martin-Schwinger analyticity determines the thermal noise from the dissipative response, whereas the near-zone radial equation and tidal matching determine the conservative logarithmic running.

papers.title: Low-Margin Branch Points in Deterministic LLM Deliberatio
papers.abstract: Deterministic multi-agent LLM deliberation can exactly re- play a fixed transcript, yet exact replay alone does not test local resistance to controlled internal interventions. Because each response becomes context for later agents, a changed greedy token can redirect a transcript-mediated execution. We present a white-box audit of this local failure mode in a five-agent committee under greedy decoding. We prospectively select low- and high-margin token positions, require exact no-op re- play, inject norm-relative residual displacements, and measure first transcript divergence within ten generated tokens. Low- margin positions are more branch-sensitive than high-margin controls, while matched margin-reducing gradient directions branch substantially more often than margin-increasing con- trols. We then continue selected realized branches through the committee to distinguish textual persistence from preference and final-decision changes. The contribution is a controlled audit for local branch susceptibility in this specified protocol, not an estimate of deployment frequency, decision correct- ness, or a phenomenon unique to multi-agent systems.

papers.title: BitLLM: Efficient Low-Bit, Conversion-Hiding LLM Decoding on Mobile GPUs
papers.abstract: The rapid scaling of large language models (LLMs) has unlocked remarkable capabilities across various domains. However, deploying LLMs on mobile devices remains challenging because of their high computational and memory requirements. Low-bit quantization (e.g., 4-bit weights, 8-bit activations) can reduce model size while preserving accuracy, but its practical efficacy on mobile GPUs has been limited so far. In this paper, we identify that the performance gap stems primarily from frequent data type conversions between quantized and floating-point values, and dynamic and inefficient memory access patterns caused by the growing Key-Value (KV) cache during autoregressive decoding. We introduce BitLLM, a mobile inference engine that addresses type conversion overhead and suboptimal memory accesses in quantized LLMs. Our approach features an adaptive layout and packing strategy for the KV cache that ensures efficient memory access throughout LLM decoding. This is coupled with an integer-native execution pipeline that defers and overlaps type conversion outside the compute hot path, keeping the critical MatMul stages in the integer domain. Implemented on off-the-shelf mobile GPUs, BitLLM outperforms leading engines, i.e., LLAMA.CPP, MNN-LLM, LiteRT-LM, and MLC-LLM, achieving average speedups of 1.78$\times$, 1.73$\times$, 1.58$\times$, and 1.47$\times$, respectively, across various models and quantization levels. Under long-context generation, BitLLM reduces average energy consumption (per token) by up to 88.9%.

papers.title: Elucidating the topological nature of molecular beam epitaxy grown high Curie temperature (Mn1+ySb2-yTe4)x(Sb2-yMnyTe3)1-x using angle resolved photoelectron spectroscopy
papers.abstract: Angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES) is used to elucidate the band structure of (Mn1+ySb2-yTe4)x(Sb2-yMnyTe3)1-x, a new magnetic quantum material grown using molecular beam epitaxy that has a Curie temperature (TC) above 100K, much higher than those reported for other materials of the MnxSb2-xTe4 class. Conflicting and sparse theory and experiments, as well as the complex disordered structure of the materials make it difficult to establish their topological nature. Here we explore this question by performing ARPES studies for two samples with x=0.65 and x=0.92, respectively. Images of the band structures of these two samples were acquired using photon energy dependent studies. The bulk and surface states of this complex material system, and the effects of composition on the band structure were investigated. Evidence of surface state features as well as bulk related ones were obtained, supporting their non-trivial nature. No signature of Fermi-arcs consistent with Weyl semimetals were seen. A shift in the Fermi level of the two samples due to different carrier densities allowed observation of the onset of a Dirac point in the surface states. Temperature dependent ARPES suggests possible band splitting as the materials undergo magnetic transitions, helping to understand the magnetic interactions. Our results point to their likely magnetic topological insulating nature.

papers.title: Spectral Dynamics and Fuglede--Kadison Determinants for Wreath Products
papers.abstract: We investigate connections between operator spectra, complex dynamics, and determinants for wreath product groups. For a nontrivial finite abelian group $G$, the natural action of $G\wr\mathbb Z$ on a rooted tree produces a family of operators with a recursive structure. Applying Schur complements to this family yields a rational map on complex projective space. We determine the projective spectrum--the parameter values for which the operator pencil fails to be invertible--as the union of the Julia set of this map and an explicitly described subset of its Fatou set. We also prove that the associated Koopman representation and the left regular representation are weakly equivalent and therefore give the same projective spectrum. We then compute Fuglede--Kadison determinants for a family of operators on more general wreath products. These formulas yield injective operators with zero determinant for wreath products $K\wr\mathbb Z$, where $K$ is a discrete group admitting a nontrivial projection $e\in\mathbb C[K]$. This answers negatively a question of Li and Thom about whether injectivity implies positive determinant for operators defined by matrices over complex group rings of amenable groups. For $G_{tf}\rtimes_σ\mathbb Z$, where $G_{tf}$ is any countable torsion-free abelian group and $σ\in\operatorname{Aut}(G_{tf})$, we prove that injectivity does imply positive determinant in every matrix size.

papers.title: Characterizing Estimator-Regime Transitions in Adaptive Enrichment Trials
papers.abstract: Adaptive enrichment trials that identify responsive subpopulations allocate a fixed sample across them and estimate each one's effect from the resulting data. For a synthetic control design with adaptive recruitment and borrowing of control outcomes, we ask whether a doubly robust family of targeted maximum likelihood estimators should replace its sample mean; the choice can be made largely at the design stage. A crossing condition weighs the bias removed and the efficiency gained by the doubly robust family against the finite-sample inflation of nuisance estimation; an equal-error boundary, located by simulation, separates the families in the plane of sample size and bias. A consistency principle prices recruiting with the wrong family's variance functional. With three and eight simulated subpopulations the boundary's sign prediction for the mean squared error difference holds in $99.6\%$ of $10{,}302$ comparisons decided at two standard errors. A pre-specified selector commits to the doubly robust family where the squared anticipated bias exceeds the net variance term. Recruiting along that family's path costs up to $0.035$ in the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve; recruiting with the sample mean functional and routing only the analysis removes this cost and about nine tenths of its error excess.

papers.title: Governing Equations of Human Sleep Macro-Structure:Symbolic Discovery from 1,106 Nights
papers.abstract: Human sleep is organized into a small number of cycles per night: deep sleep dominates early cycles, REM lengthens toward morning, and light sleep clusters at cycle boundaries. These regularities have long been described qualitatively but never distilled into closed-form laws from large-scale data. A total of 1,106 nights (Sleep-EDF 153 + SHHS 953) are segmented into REM-anchored cycles, and four cycle-indexed statistics follow simple closed-form equations: cycle length declines nearly linearly (R^2=0.996), REM duration follows an inverted U (R^2=0.873), deep-sleep (N3) run length decays exponentially (R^2=0.987) with a time constant of 2.94 cycles, consistent with the homeostatic Process S of the two-process model, and light-sleep (N1) run length follows a U shape (R^2=0.956), confirming a "long-short-long" pattern across the night. The laws are reproduced by per-night differentiable fitting (142/142 and 773/773 nights converge), by unconstrained symbolic regression (PySR), and by a 500-night generative synthesizer built from them. Their robustness is established against the two main methodological threats: bootstrap CIs computed by resampling whole nights (1,000 replications) exclude zero for every shape term, and a five-level scan of the REM-merge segmentation threshold preserves every qualitative form. These appear to be the first closed-form laws governing the macro-structure of sleep, distilled and tested across an age-mixed sample (healthy young adults and community-based older adults).

papers.title: RATR: Training-Free Material Rebinding via Role Assignment and Temporal Routing
papers.abstract: Material rebinding aims to transfer the material appearance from a reference image while preserving the target object's geometry and identity. Existing methods typically struggle to balance material fidelity with structural preservation due to the coupled influence of structural and appearance cues in their visual conditions. We identify role entanglement in the target and reference conditions as a contributing factor the target condition carries both geometry and its original appearance while the reference condition contains material cues alongside object-specific structure. To address this issue, we propose RATR, a training-free material rebinding method built on a diffusion-based image editor that assigns complementary roles to the two conditions and coordinates their influence during denoising. To make the target condition primarily convey structure, we introduce an albedo-resolved surface release mechanism, which suppresses the target's original surface appearance while retaining geometric cues, yielding a structure-oriented condition for material transfer. On the reference side, the designed material evidence isolation mechanism emphasizes material cues while reducing interference from object-specific structure, yielding a complementary material-oriented condition.

papers.title: A comparison of parallel iterative methods for ILU triangular solves
papers.abstract: Exact triangular solves parallelise poorly, limited by the size and number of the level sets, so on GPUs the factors from incomplete LU (ILU) factorisations are often solved approximately with parallel iterative methods. We compare four such methods: a Jacobi method, an Incomplete Sparse Approximate Inverse (ISAI), GMRES polynomials, and AIRG, a reduction multigrid built on GMRES polynomials, for which we introduce a parallel coarse/fine splitting that bounds the diagonal dominance ratio of the fine-fine block. We test them with ILU(0) and ILU(1) factors of canonical PDE problems and 91 SuiteSparse/Matrix Market matrices, the latter on a single GPU. AIRG is the most robust on the PDE factors, with nearly flat iteration counts under refinement and no per-problem tuning, but has the largest setup and memory costs. GMRES polynomials are more robust than the Jacobi method at a similar cost. As the inner solve of an ILU preconditioner with tuned inner iteration counts, ISAI gives the largest median speedups over a hipSPARSE exact triangular solve (4.5$\times$ and 6.8$\times$ for ILU(0) and ILU(1)), though this was dominated by smaller problems; on the largest ILU(1) problems all four methods give similar median speedups of 2.1-2.6$\times$.

papers.title: Efficient Causal Survival Inference under Limited Surrogate Monitoring
papers.abstract: Post-treatment surrogate endpoints can improve the efficiency of causal survival effect estimation, but their monitoring may end before follow-up for the primary outcome. We investigate the impact of limited recurrence monitoring on semiparametric efficiency when mortality follow-up continues. We derive the efficient influence function under limited monitoring and establish an exact expression for the efficiency gain from extending monitoring between any two durations. Our framework encompasses the absence of surrogate information and the usual shared-censoring scheme as boundary cases, and allows comparison with fully observed surrogates. We develop a doubly robust estimator under limited surrogate monitoring and establish asymptotic normality and semiparametric efficiency for its cross-fitted version under suitable conditions. Simulations and an application to breast cancer data illustrate the proposed method.

papers.title: From Weeks to Hours: Fast and Principled SFT Data Generation for Reasoning LLMs
papers.abstract: Reasoning-oriented post-training enables large language models (LLMs) to solve complex tasks via multi-step inference. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) on high-quality reasoning traces is a particularly efficient approach, but its effectiveness depends critically on careful data curation. Existing pipelines rely on a costly generate-then-filter paradigm: large pools of long reasoning traces are produced by multiple teacher models and subsequently filtered for difficulty and diversity using additional LLMs, often requiring weeks of computation. In this work, we propose SFTProbe, a fundamentally different approach that bypasses this pipeline by directly predicting the quality of reasoning data. We show that a brief LoRA-based adaptation, combined with evaluating loss on only 5% of each reasoning trace, suffices to estimate both difficulty and diversity. SFTProbe is grounded in a geometric view of post-training, where pretrained LLMs lie in a low-rank, anisotropic loss basin. By probing this basin via low-rank perturbations, we construct compact loss signatures whose clustering captures diversity, while loss at curvature inflection points provides a robust proxy for difficulty. We also provide a simple criterion for teacher selection. Empirically, our approach reduces data curation time from weeks to hours while maintaining or improving performance. Remarkably, on mathematical reasoning, 5k generated examples match the highly filtered 89k-example in OpenThoughts-Math dataset, and 7.5k generated examples outperforms it by 2.5% in accuracy. We further introduce a high-quality physics reasoning dataset, and use it to train a model that outperforms an IPhO 2025 silver-medal-winning model. The code and the dataset are released at https://bigml-cs-ucla.github.io/SFTProbe-page/.

papers.title: Distinguishing among reasoning levels of GPT 5.5 Pro via a grammar lens benchmark
papers.abstract: Does the level of test-time processing effort affect a language model's computational capability? A formal grammar-lens benchmark method, derived from the theory of computation, generates novel data at specified levels, each successively more computationally powerful than the levels below. Using this data, we tested GPT-5.5, and GPT-5.5-Pro-Medium, -High, and -XHigh, showing incrementally increased acceptance of test data: 16, 40, 43, and 52\%, respectively, illustrating the benchmark's ability to discern fine-grained differences among models' added test-time reasoning levels. Additionally, as test-time compute effort increases, model responses diverge from human responses to the same data. This increasing disagreement may turn out to be broadly characteristic of more capable language models, introducing the potential of a general capability-versus-alignment conflict.

papers.title: Spatial-Spectral Interactive POCS Network for Large-Gap Seismic Data Interpolation
papers.abstract: Large gaps in seismic acquisition disrupt reflection events and hinder spectral recovery. Existing seismic interpolation deep unfolding networks primarily rely on localized spatial priors, limiting their ability to aggregate the global context necessary for reconstructing these extensive missing regions. We propose a spatial-spectral interactive projection-onto-convex-sets network (SSI-POCS) to tackle this severely ill-posed problem. By unfolding the classical iterative solver, our network integrates physical consistency with dual-domain deep priors via learned transforms, soft thresholding, and exact data reinsertion. Within the learned prior, a spatial Restormer branch captures local waveform structures, while a fast Fourier convolution (FFC) branch extracts global context, effectively suppressing incoherent components and enhancing spectral energy concentration in the $f-k$ domain. A dual-domain fusion module exchanges these complementary features via bidirectional channel attention and gated modulation, yielding substantial interpolation improvements. To overcome the severe loss of lateral continuity caused by large gaps, we introduce structural similarity (SSIM) supervision, complemented by focal frequency loss (FFL) and transform consistency constraints to suppress incoherent high-frequency components and regularize training. Experiments on a synthetic salt dome and a North Sea field dataset under 50% random and consecutive trace removal demonstrate the effectiveness of SSI-POCS. It significantly enhances event continuity across large gaps and mitigates artifacts, achieving a 3.285~dB SNR improvement over the best competing method while reducing parameters by 75.66%.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence in Pharmaceutical Development: Building Rigorous, Decision-Ready Evidence
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) are reshaping the pharmaceutical lifecycle, from discovery and clinical development through manufacturing and regulatory review to safety surveillance and health economics, creating evidentiary challenges that predictive performance alone cannot address. This review examines the inferential, causal, validation, and documentation requirements for AI-enabled evidence generation in high-stakes settings and argues that they must be built into workflows. We outline the evidentiary functions that AI-derived outputs must satisfy before supporting consequential decisions: estimand definition, fit-for-purpose data collection, bias control, uncertainty quantification, validation, interpretability, and decision-grade documentation. Because AI both depends on and accelerates large-scale, non-randomized data collection, the integration of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) with real-world data (RWD) is where its evidentiary risks concentrate; we therefore present a five-step causal roadmap for that integration, in which external data supplement but never replace a concurrent control, and characterize the safeguards required across development, pharmacovigilance, regulation, and health technology assessment. Priority frontiers answer recurring implementation problems: conformal prediction for overconfident predictions, randomization-based inference for scarce data, and federated causal inference and privacy-preserving generative modeling for data that cannot be pooled. Evidence generation depends not on competition between RCTs and RWD, or between statistics and AI/ML, but on their principled synthesis under causal and inferential frameworks, with statistical expertise central to decision-ready evidence.

papers.title: Can agents reliably design therapeutic antibodies?
papers.abstract: Recent work has demonstrated agents driving protein design workflows, either through orchestration of specialized tools or direct manipulation of sequences. Yet the fidelity with which agents follow protein design instructions and the factors contributing to their effectiveness remain understudied. We examine agentic antibody design under two settings: when explicit molecular-editing instructions are provided and when agents receive only previously-scored sequences and are prompted to propose improvements. We call the first task-guided and the second black-box design. For the task-guided setting, we curate ten expert-validated affinity-improvement tasks and show that LLM judges closely reproduce programmatic evaluations of instruction following. We then study two augmentations: access to antibody-relevant tools and to previously scored design history. Tools improve instruction following (IF) and sequence space exploration while reducing optimization performance, whereas design history reduces IF but improves optimization performance at the expense of exploration. Finally, we combine taskguided and black-box design within an in silico optimization loop and show that our agentic optimizer performs comparably to an established Bayesian optimization baseline.

papers.title: Wilsonian exact renormalization group flow in the gauged Nambu--Jona-Lasinio model
papers.abstract: We study the Wilsonian exact renormalization group flow of the gauged Nambu--Jona-Lasinio (NJL) model, a four-dimensional $U(1)$ gauge theory with chirally invariant four-Fermi interactions, by using the gradient flow exact renormalization group~(GFERG). Our gauge-invariant ansatz (truncation) for the 1PI Wilson action keeps a general photon kinetic function~$\mathcal{K}_τ(k^2)$, the fermion mass, and the scalar and vector four-Fermi couplings. For a fixed gauge coupling~$e^2$, the Gaussian and NJL (quasi-)fixed points on the critical surface merge at~$e_c^2\simeq17$, as anticipated by the ladder Schwinger--Dyson equation and the conventional Wilsonian renormalization group. We then let $e^2$ itself flow. Owing to the manifest gauge invariance of the GFERG, the flow of~$e^2$ is governed solely by the photon anomalous dimension~$γ_A$, which remains positive along both branches up to the merging point. Hence, no fixed point with~$e^2\neq0$ exists. Flows from a sufficiently large~$e^2$ in the ultraviolet (UV) reach the chirally broken phase even for vanishing four-Fermi couplings, so the gauge interaction does trigger chiral symmetry breaking. The merging point, however, is not a fixed point, and the gauge coupling vanishes in any continuum limit within our truncation.

papers.title: RayAR: Autoregressive Dominant Path Generation for Low-Overhead MIMO Beam Alignment
papers.abstract: Beam alignment in multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO) systems requires selecting suitable transmit and receive beam pairs with limited measurement overhead. Although 3GPP Release 18 investigates beam prediction from partial measurements, collecting these measurements still incurs probing overhead. Geometry can focus this probing through the departure and arrival directions of dominant paths, whose identification requires accounting for coupled diffraction interactions. To address this challenge, we propose RayAR, an autoregressive method that generates dominant propagation paths from urban geometry. RayAR conditions candidate ranking on the path prefix, local diffraction geometry, and receiver reachability, updating this context after each selection until the receiver becomes visible. The completed path's departure and arrival directions rank beam pairs for probing, allowing the pair with the highest received power to be selected from a small candidate set. Under 3GPP Release 18 beam-management metrics, RayAR reduces probing by 96.88\% relative to exhaustive sweeping and achieves the highest optimal-pair hit rate among compared methods at the same budget. Real-world measurements further demonstrate the accuracy of this geometric guidance, with simulation-trained RayAR achieving the lowest departure and arrival angular errors among compared methods without fine-tuning and a mean arrival-direction error of 9.07$^\circ$.

papers.title: Ultra-broadband quantum infrared spectroscopy extending to 20 {\textmu}m
papers.abstract: Quantum infrared spectroscopy (QIRS), which exploits quantum interference between photon-pair generation processes, enables infrared spectroscopy using only visible and near-infrared (VNIR) light sources and detectors. Extending the spectral coverage of QIRS into the long-wavelength infrared region up to 20 {\textmu}m is crucial for the identification and characterization of a broad range of materials. However, implementing QIRS beyond 10 {\textmu}m has been challenging because the nonlinear materials used to date do not provide suitable photon-pair sources in this spectral region. Here, we design a wavelength-tunable photon-pair source based on a gallium selenide crystal and develop a QIRS system covering a broad spectral range from 8.6 to 20 {\textmu}m. Using this system, we measure the transmittance spectrum of a polystyrene film and observe characteristic absorption bands beyond 10 {\textmu}m relevant to identifying polystyrene and to probing local chain conformation. These results demonstrate that QIRS is capable of covering the entire molecular fingerprint region.

papers.title: TabAbax: A Tabular Foundation Model Technical Report
papers.abstract: Tabular foundation models (TFMs) enable in-context prediction on unseen tabular datasets without task-specific training. Mechanistic work has shown that increasing the depth of the ICL Transformer yields weak gains, leaving the main headroom for gains in the synthetic pretraining prior and column-row encoder upstream of the ICL backbone. We introduce TabAbax, a TFM built on TabICLv2 that focuses all modifications on these two upstream components. On the prior side, we further improve the quality and complexity of the synthetic pretraining prior. On the encoder side, a two-pass column-row stack strengthens cross-feature interactions before row compression, using learned Fourier scalar encoding from TabFM and Causilo. Evaluations on BeyondArena and TabArena show strong regression-centric gains: TabAbax reaches 1,238 Elo on the 142-dataset BeyondArena suite (10th of 41 evaluated methods), 1,676 Elo on TabArena's overall 51-dataset suite (11th of 99 methods, +115 over TabICLv2), and 2,024 Elo on TabArena's regression benchmark (7th of 99 methods, +336 over TabICLv2, +21 over TabFM). A prior-only ablation confirms the attribution: the improved prior alone yields +228 Elo for regression, demonstrating that prior quality is the dominant knob for improving regression performance.

papers.title: Reversibility of Nonequilibrium Dynamics in a Unitary Fermi Gas
papers.abstract: We theoretically describe and experimentally observe the reversibility of a nonequilibrium state in a unitary Fermi gas confined in a time-dependent trap. Unlike the equilibrium case, reversibility out of equilibrium imposes a stringent condition: the accumulated dynamical phase must be an integer multiple of $2π$, i.e., $Δφ= 2ω_{0} s(T) = 2nπ$, where $ω_{0}$ is the initial trapping frequency and $s(T)$ is the rescaled time after a total evolution time $T$. We demonstrate the reversibility of an initial nonequilibrium state in an isotropic unitary Fermi gas by driving the optical trap through a round trip. We find two types of reversible pathways, the space-time scaling-invariant and polynomial shortcut-to-adiabaticity (STA) protocols. The phase condition restricts the round-trip time $T$ to discrete values, a distinguishing feature of nonequilibrium dynamics. Our work establishes a clear criterion for the quantum control of nonequilibrium many-body systems beyond linear response and provides practical pathways to reversibility.

papers.title: WAR-CRAFT: Refining Web API Recommendations through Requirement Auditing
papers.abstract: Web API recommenders return a set of APIs for a mashup request but do not check it against provider documentation, the main public evidence of an API's capabilities. The set can therefore contain unsupported or redundant APIs and miss requested capabilities. Filling every apparent gap does not fix this, because a gap may already be served, may not need its own API, or may have no documented provider. We study post-recommendation refinement, which revises a frozen recommender's output using only the request, the catalog, and provider documentation. We propose WAR-CRAFT, which treats refinement as three decisions. An LLM removes unsupported or subsumed APIs by judging candidates jointly, then audits the remaining set against a requirement checklist derived from the request. For each uncovered requirement, a fine-tuned catalog-constrained Resolver proposes a catalog API or abstains, and an independent documentation check admits only supported proposals. On ProgrammableWeb with 7 heterogeneous upstream recommenders, WAR-CRAFT raises mean SetF1 from 0.558 to 0.644, above the strongest of 5 refinement baselines (62.5%), and roughly halves functional redundancy (0.127 to 0.065) without changing mean functional coverage. Gains range from +2.2 points on generative recommenders to +18.2 on fixed-cutoff rankers. At matched set sizes, WAR-CRAFT still outperforms truncating the upstream output, so the gain is not explained by set-size calibration alone. Our code is available at https://github.com/ZsXu-enrico/WAR-CRAFT.

papers.title: Movement based social interactions with label uncertainty
papers.abstract: Drone-based imagery provides high resolution data for tracking wildlife populations. However, monitoring marine mammals like cetaceans is challenging because individuals frequently submerge into water or move out of the drone's field of view, resulting in disconnected trajectories due to uncertain identities. Existing social movement models assume individual identities are known, which is often only true when data come from physical tracking devices like GPS collars. To address this limitation, we propose a Bayesian hierarchical state-space model that treats the identities associated with observed locations as unknown random variables. This allows us to jointly estimate individual movement parameters while propagating the uncertainty about identity. We apply our framework to drone-measured movement data from Risso's dolphins (Grampus griseus) to estimate the effects of sonar exposure on the dolphins' movement behavior. Our proposed method offers a solution for analyzing collective animal behavior when continuous tracking of every individual is challenging.

papers.title: Structured Channel Network Pruning with Bi-Sparse Matrix Factorization
papers.abstract: Structured channel pruning for convolutional neural networks (CNNs) plays an important role in pattern recognition and deep learning. Nevertheless, existing methods usually calculate channel importance scores based on the magnitudes of individual filters, making it difficult to distinguish shared redundancy from individual channel contributions. To tackle this limitation, we propose a novel structured channel pruning method termed bi-sparse matrix factorization (BSMF). Specifically, BSMF characterizes the convolutional weight matrix as output-channel coefficients over a shared basis with row-wise $\ell_{2,p}$-norm and column-wise $\ell_{2,q}$-norm regularization terms, respectively. Note that $p,q\in[0,1)$, which, to our best knowledge, has not been explored in the literature. To solve the resulting non-convex optimization problem, we develop an efficient update scheme built upon the alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), in which all subproblems admit closed-form solutions. After that, a compact CNN is obtained by reconstructing the convolutional filters from the learned factors and discarding the redundant channels. Extensive experiments on the CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-1K datasets demonstrate that our proposed BSMF achieves significant network compression while maintaining high reconstruction accuracy. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/xianchaoxiu/BSMF

papers.title: Sedentariness in Cayley graphs
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be the adjacency matrix of a finite graph $Γ$. We say that vertex $u$ of $Γ$ is sedentary if for some constant $C>0$, $|\exp(itA)_{u,u}|\geq C$ for all $t\in\mathbb{R}$. In this paper, we investigate vertex sedentariness in walk-regular graphs with a focus on Cayley graphs and, more generally, vertex-transitive graphs. In particular, we define the necklace polynomial of an integral graph and use this notion to characterize sedentariness in integral walk-regular graphs. As an application, we use basic tools from algebraic number theory to show that an integral Cayley graph on a group of odd order is sedentary and provide a lower bound on its sedentariness. We also give sufficient conditions such that a unitary Cayley graph over a finite ring is sedentary. Furthermore, we characterize the existence of twin vertices in Cayley graphs and vertex-transitive graphs, and completely determine the occurrence of sedentariness, perfect state transfer and pretty good state transfer in vertex-transitive graphs with twins. Finally, we prove that if $Γ(G,S)$ is a nonempty, integral, normal Cayley graph, then for any prime $p$ with $\gcd(p, |G|)=1$, there is at least one eigenvalue of $Γ(G,S)$ which is not a multiple of $p$. This generalizes a result of Arnadottir and Godsil, which states that an integral normal Cayley graph of odd order possesses an odd eigenvalue.

papers.title: Holonomy classification, gyroscope precession, and Landau levels in Gödel-type spacetimes and their superfluid analog
papers.abstract: We derive the parallel-transport holonomies of circles centered on the symmetry axis in the homogeneous Gödel-type family of Rebouças and Tiomno, which includes the Gödel universe, the causal member with $m^2=4Ω^2$, and the Som--Raychaudhuri limit. The holonomy is governed by a single invariant $Δ(r)$, whose sign determines whether the Lorentz transformation is elliptic, parabolic, or hyperbolic. We determine the number of parabolic radii across the family and prove that, whenever the azimuthal circles become closed timelike curves (CTCs), the chronology radius satisfies $Δ(r_c)=-\cosh(mr_c)<0$. We also express this invariant in terms of Killing-vector scalars, derive the vector and spinor Wilson loops, give the exact condition for trivial holonomy after a finite number of turns, and analyze Fermi--Walker transport on circular CTCs. Finally, we discuss an analogy with the effective metric of a rotating superfluid, valid under stated conditions, and derive exact expressions for the radial $L^2$ localization of Klein--Gordon Landau modes relative to the Som--Raychaudhuri chronology radius. The geometric results are exact within the metric family considered; the discussion of the analog system relies on the validity of a coarse-grained effective description.

papers.title: Promotion and Extension of General Escape-Covering Duality Relationship
papers.abstract: Bellman's lost-in-a-forest problem, Moser's worm problem, Lebesgue's universal covering problems, and the classical 'fits and covers' questions can be organized by a common obstruction principle: an object fits a region if some admissible group action places it in the region, whereas an escape object is one for which every placement fails to remain in the interior. In this paper, we develop a general theory of escape-covering duality for any dimension and explore several applications. For convex translation covers of all closed planar curves of Euclidean length one, we prove $ W \ge f(\sqrt3/9)+c_1>0.15545785378555,c_1=0.000009944944227372... $ Here $f(\sqrt3/9)$ is Wetzel's classical lower bound. For a rational polytopal Minkowski gauge and prescribed rational facet directions, we express universal closed-loop cover feasibility as a rational polyhedron in the facet offsets. After removing translations, minimum volume is attained at a vertex. Refining the facet directions gives explicit two-sided rational bounds for the unrestricted fixed-gauge worm constant. Four exact benchmarks recover known sharp values. The construction uses an elementary circuit--circumradius form of the established non-fitting-polygon and capacity theory. We supply its support and ledger derivation, the finite complete test family in arbitrary dimension, a cover vertex bound, and the resulting algebraicity statement. The surrounding escape--covering framework includes endpoint placement, attainment, gauge stability, and finite-to-continuum error bounds. For nonsymmetric gauges the objects are parametrized closed curves, so orientation-dependent length is retained. Through the published capacity identity, the improved Wetzel estimate gives a product volume--capacity factor below $1.023781939711102$ for every planar ellipsoidal gauge.

papers.title: A Parallel Adaptive Proximal ADMM for Linearly Constrained Separable Composite Optimization Problems
papers.abstract: We propose and analyze an adaptive proximal alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM), based on Jacobi-type updates, for linearly constrained separable nonconvex composite optimization problems. The objective consists of two block-separable functions, one continuously differentiable and weakly convex, and the other convex and Lipschitz continuous. The proposed method is adaptive to all problem parameters and allows inexact solutions of the block proximal subproblems. At each iteration, we solve all block subproblems in parallel, then apply a novel test to decide whether to update the Lagrange multiplier and/or the penalty parameter. Without any rank assumptions on the constraint matrices, we establish an ${\cal O}(ε^{-3})$ iteration-complexity bound for obtaining an approximate first-order stationary point. This matches the best-known complexity for cyclic proximal ADMM methods and improves the existing complexity of Jacobi-type schemes in this general nonconvex setting. Numerical experiments on a nonconvex quadratic program illustrate the proposed method's computational benefits.

papers.title: Unconditional optimal convergence of a relaxation Crank-Nicolson difference scheme for 2D space-fractional NLS
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a linearly implicit relaxation Crank-Nicolson difference scheme for the two-dimensional space-fractional nonlinear Schrödinger (SFNS) equation, where the fractional Laplacian is approximated by a simple fractional central difference scheme. The proposed scheme is uniquely solvable and conserves discrete mass for general real-valued nonlinear coefficients, and a modified discrete energy in the cubic case. By introducing a modified error system employing a cut-off technique, we establish the optimal-order error estimates without mesh-ratio restriction. Specifically, the primary variable achieves second-order temporal and spatial convergence in the discrete $H_h^{α/2}$-norm, and the relaxation variable satisfies the same convergence in the discrete $L^2$-norm. Some numerical experiments confirm the relevant theoretical results.

papers.title: Total dominating sets and four-colorings of planar triangulations
papers.abstract: In 2018, Goddard and Henning conjectured that every planar triangulation on at least four vertices has two disjoint total dominating sets. It was proved by Francis, Illickan, Jose, and Rajendraprasad in 2024. As a strengthening of this result, Goddard and Henning also conjectured that every planar triangulation with at least four vertices has a proper $4$-coloring with color classes $C_1,C_2,C_3,C_4$ such that $C_1\cup C_2$ and $C_3\cup C_4$ are total dominating sets. In this paper, we disprove this conjecture: for every $n\ge 36$ there is a planar triangulation with $n$ vertices without such a coloring. As another strengthening of the result by Francis, Illickan, Jose, and Rajendraprasad, they conjectured that every near-triangulation has a $4$-coloring, not necessarily proper, in which every vertex $v$ sees at least $\min \{ \operatorname{deg}(v),3 \}$ colors on its neighbors. We prove this conjecture for all planar triangulations.

papers.title: Scaling Laws for Parameter Setting in Digitized Counterdiabatic QAOA
papers.abstract: Optimizing parameters separately for each problem instance limits the reuse of variational quantum algorithms. We develop empirical scaling laws for parameter setting in the digitized counterdiabatic quantum approximate optimization algorithm (DC-QAOA) for weighted MaxCut. The prescription combines exact covariance under uniform edge-weight rescaling with power laws in mean degree fitted separately to offline-optimized cost and counterdiabatic angles. After the weight and degree scales are removed, the optimized angles of different training graphs cluster around common amplitudes, so a small coefficient table suffices. Frozen coefficients assign angles from a target graph's mean degree and root-mean-square edge weight without target-instance variational optimization. In ideal-circuit simulations across 1050 test graphs spanning ten graph families and five positive edge-weight distributions, mean optimal-solution probability is higher than that of the fixed-angle quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) at each depth from one to four layers, reaching 19.36% versus 13.11% at four layers. A six-layer extension on 600 graphs also shows a mean probability advantage. Hardware execution on the IBM Quantum processor ibm_fez for 21 unit-weight 3-regular graphs shows a mean probability advantage at one layer, while the ordering reverses at two layers. In separate energy-based experiments, direct assignment gives a higher mean approximation ratio than random-start optimization reaches within 500 evaluations, and refinement started from the formula angles improves it further. These results show how a scaling-based representation of optimized angles can guide parameter reuse across graph instances, enabling direct parameter assignment without target-instance variational optimization and providing initial angles for local refinement.

papers.title: DERED: Enhancing Third-Party Library Detection in Binaries via Deceptive Reuse Mitigation
papers.abstract: This paper introduces the concept of deceptive reuse a misleading reuse relationship between recipient software that share common TPL code and proposes a novel approach, DERED, to enhance TPL detection by distinguishing between real reuse and deceptive reuse.

papers.title: Heterostructure morphology stability maps in multiphase nanoparticles
papers.abstract: In the rapidly growing field of nanocombinatorics, the advent of megalibraries of multiphase nanoparticles (NPs) has created a need for predictive computational approaches. A notable characteristic of multiphase NPs is the internal interface architecture that arises from the joining of constituent phases at boundaries. We propose a strategy to predict the ground-state interface architecture from the DFT-calculated surface and interfacial energies of all constituent phases as input and use this strategy to create stability maps to predict multiphase NP morphologies. A Potts model, a $q$-state generalization of the Ising model, in which $q-1$ spins represent discretized regions of a constituent phase, provides a flexible, discretized representation of a $(q-1)$-phase nanoparticle with arbitrary interfacial join morphology. Interactions between spins represent interactions between phases, or interfacial energies. To model the surface of a nanoparticle, an additional spin represents the surrounding environment and interaction energies with this spin are surface energies. We apply a Monte Carlo algorithm to search for the lowest-energy spin configuration. The trade-off between surface and interfacial energy minimization drives the formation of an interface morphology. We calculate a biphase nanoparticle interface morphology stability map to study the relation between the three biphase morphologies we found. Next, we use the stability map to predict NP morphologies of sample biphase systems and compare these to experimentally available data. We repeat the grid search approach for triphase nanoparticle interface morphologies and discover 11 triphase morphologies, nine more than previously enumerated. We then predict sample triphase systems and finally revisit experimentally reported triphase morphologies.

papers.title: The First-Order Value of Free Covariates in Budgeted Risk Monitoring
papers.abstract: A deployed model sees its inputs for free, but checking whether its risk has risen requires costly labels. We study how to spend a label budget so that a risk increase is detected quickly while false alarms stay controlled, including under input shifts that keep the risk below a safety threshold $τ$. Let $A$ be the false-alarm control scale and $h(r)=\mathrm{kl}(r,τ)$ the Bernoulli KL divergence between the changed risk $r$ and $τ$. At label rate $b=c/\log A$, we prove that every rule that chooses requests from its own label history has worst-case (Lorden) delay at least $(1/h(r)+1/c)\log A$ to first order: besides collecting evidence, it must wait for its next label. The bound needs only a label budget on one finite stretch of safe source data and false-alarm control over an initial window; a bound on the average time to false alarm does not suffice. When a harmful change also shifts the inputs, a rule that lets the inputs trigger labeling attains delay $\log A/h(r)$ to first order on a fixed Gaussian model, so free covariates save at least $1/b$ rounds. A hybrid rule adds a label-history fallback for risk changes that leave the inputs unchanged. Synthetic experiments and two ACS tasks, with strengthened label-only baselines, show the predicted pattern. The covariate trigger has a cost: because its budget is calibrated on the source, a benign input shift can make it request nearly every label.

papers.title: On the asymptotic distribution of the largest eigenvalue of unbalanced complex Jacobi ensembles
papers.abstract: Let $\mathbf{A} \sim \mathbb{C}\mathcal{W}_p(I,m)$ and $\mathbf{B} \sim \mathbb{C}\mathcal{W}_p(I,n)$ be two independent complex Wishart random matrices. In this work, we investigate the asymptotic distribution of the largest eigenvalue $θ_{\max}$ of the random matrix $\mathbf{J} = (\mathbf{A}+\mathbf{B})^{-1}\mathbf{B}$. The high-dimensional regime is potentially unbalanced in the sense that, as $p \to \infty$, $m$ may grow faster than $p$, whereas $n$ grows proportionally to $p$. The asymptotic behavior of $θ_{\max}$ is characterized by means of a Riemann-Hilbert (RH) problem for Jacobi polynomials with modified Jacobi weights. We establish the type 2 Tracy--Widom asymptotic distribution of $θ_{\max}$. This provides an alternative, RH-based proof of the corresponding result of Johnstone [Ann. Statist. 36 (2008), 2638-2716] in the balanced regime, and establishes a conjecture of Jiang [Probab. Theory Relat. Fields 144 (2009), 221-246] in the unbalanced regime. In addition, we obtain an explicit correction of order $p^{-2/3}$ to the Tracy--Widom approximation, with a remainder of order $\mathcal{O}(p^{-1})$, and show exponential decay, as a function of $p$, of the upper tail of the distribution of $θ_{\max}$.

papers.title: Non-asymptotic analysis of SGLD with discontinuous stochastic gradients: a new route to portfolio CVaR minimization
papers.abstract: Conditional-Value-at-Risk (CVaR) optimization is a fundamental tool in portfolio selection, yet its nonsmooth loss structure poses a challenge for the existing theory of stochastic gradient methods including associated Langevin algorithms. In particular, the positive-part loss and the softmax portfolio parametrization lead to stochastic gradients that need not be globally Lipschitz continuous, but rather discontinuous, where available non-convex stochastic gradient Langevin dynamics (SGLD) guarantees often exhibit an unfavorable exponential dependence on the problem dimension. In this article, we develop a non-asymptotic analysis of SGLD for a regularized CVaR portfolio optimization problem. We exploit the geometric structure of the CVaR objective to establish linear growth, convexity-at-infinity, and one-sided Lipschitz properties of the stochastic gradient without imposing density assumptions on the asset losses that are typical in previous works. Crucially, the constants appearing in the aforementioned structural conditions are shown to be independent of the number of assets. Moreover, we establish a convergence bound in Wasserstein-2 distance with rate $\mathcal{O}(λ^{1/4})$ and a finite-time guarantee for the expected excess risk. Our analysis, together with the dimension-independent constants in the structural conditions, leads to an excess risk bound that depends linearly on the number of assets. Numerical experiments with simulated Gaussian portfolios exhibit the predicted dimension dependence. Computational comparisons with alternative stochastic optimization methods further illustrate the practical efficiency of SGLD for the optimization problem under consideration. Finally, we extend the framework to a broader class of non-convex stochastic optimization problems with discontinuous stochastic gradients.

papers.title: From Apparent Search Gains to Selection Failures: Auditing Test-Time Inference in Structured Workflow Planning
papers.abstract: Test-time search can improve structured planning, but when methods differ in prompts, post-processing, and selection, it is unclear what an observed gain should be attributed to. We study this question on DisasterBench, where models compose typed multi-tool workflows, by decomposing inference into three observable stages: whether a correct workflow is discovered, whether it survives structural validation, and whether it is finally selected. Comparing independent sampling, a nominal tree-search configuration, and multi-operator search under controlled inference budgets on two model families, we find that (i) the nominal tree-search configuration realizes non-adaptive complete-workflow sampling, and independent sampling with its expansion prompt reproduces its candidate discovery without constructing a tree; (ii) structural validation never removes the last correct workflow in our evaluated candidate pools, whereas majority voting leaves a discovered correct workflow unselected on 10-19% of tasks per pool, with an audit confirming substantive tool-choice or information-flow errors in 57 of 60 examined cases; and (iii) a tool-specification-aware verifier recovers some of these losses but overturns more correct decisions than it fixes. Our results motivate auditing realized rather than nominal inference pipelines, and reporting discovery, validity, and selection separately.

papers.title: Evolving Scientific Intelligence: From Fragmented Evidence to Distributed Experimental Loops
papers.abstract: Scientific discovery advances when evidence from different investigations is brought into contact. Yet paper-centric communication leaves experimental results fragmented, delayed, or unreported, creating a "scientific memory wall" between growing computational capabilities and the evidence accessible to AI systems. We envision a different dynamic: in a network of intelligent laboratories, a failed or overlooked experiment in one domain could trigger a hypothesis in another, whose testing generates evidence that stimulates further investigations. Such chains of information collision and empirical validation could transform isolated discovery loops into a cumulative scientific process. We propose Evolving Scientific Intelligence (ESI), an architectural blueprint for enabling these evidence-driven chain reactions. ESI preserves experimental records in shared, computable scientific memory, where evidence from different domains can be recombined into testable hypotheses. It jointly selects candidates and evaluation methods according to scientific value, reliability, and cost, then coordinates physical tests across distributed experimental nodes. Their feedback revises hypotheses and evaluators, while slower meta-control reassesses research objectives and decision criteria to guard against self-reinforcing errors and misguided optimization. We call for an Information Manhattan Project to build the infrastructure for scientific intelligence that evolves through experimentally grounded chains of discovery.
