For the adaptive lower bound, we relate each query's distinguishing power to the prediction, based on previous answers, of whether its endpoints lie in the same part of the hidden partition. We bound the combined advantage of these predictions using the completed transcript, which lets us analyze the adaptively chosen pairs of vertices together despite their dependence on earlier answers.

papers.title: Content-Preserving Principal Feature Blending for Training-Free Style Personalization
papers.abstract: Reference-based style personalization should reproduce the appearance of a style reference while preserving the subject specified by a content prompt. In visual autoregressive models, dominant reference features can also carry object and spatial information, causing content leakage. We propose Content-Preserving Principal Feature Blending (CoPFB), a training-free method that estimates a low-rank content basis from a clean generation branch and removes the content-aligned component of the style residual. CoPFB applies rank-one blending at the first two autoregressive scales, followed by weaker content-projected refinement at the next three scales. On 1,900 combinations of Parti content prompts and FineStyle reference images, CoPFB improves text alignment from 0.293 to 0.297 and the harmonic score from 0.391 to 0.393 over PFB+SAC, while style similarity decreases from 0.590 to 0.577. CoPFB requires no fine-tuning or learnable parameters. Project page: https://vdkhoi20.github.io/CoPFB/.

papers.title: Density-Aware Calibration for Resource-Efficient Medical Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) show promise for clinical image understanding, but their computational and memory requirements hinder deployment on resource-constrained clinical hardware. Post-training quantization (PTQ) offers a practical compression strategy without retraining, yet its effectiveness depends strongly on the calibration data. We propose CoreCalib, a training-free and quantizer-agnostic framework for constructing compact calibration sets that preserve the target medical VQA distribution. CoreCalib stratifies data by clinical question class, identifies representative visual modes using frozen DINOv2 features with UMAP and HDBSCAN, and expands selected images into class-balanced question-answer pairs. On Kvasir-VQA-x1, we evaluate CoreCalib with MASQuant, GPTQ, and QIG using a fixed 128-pair budget. CoreCalib achieves the best METEOR with all three quantizers and the best ROUGE-L with MASQuant and GPTQ. With W4A8 MASQuant, it improves METEOR from 0.5672 with COCO calibration to 0.6234, recovering approximately 41% of the degradation relative to BF16. These results support CoreCalib as a data-centric component for resource-efficient medical VLM deployment. Project page: https://magnusdtd.github.io/CoreCalib/ .

papers.title: Text-to-music Generation via Structured Captions AND Interpretable Evaluation
papers.abstract: Text descriptions of music are central to the performance of text-to-music generation (TTM) methods, but creation of paired text information for music generation is relatively under explored. Here, we propose training latent diffusion/flow-based music generation models conditioned on structured captions (SCAPs) and compare with typical free-form captions via a set of controlled ablations. We compare free-form vs. structured captions, partial vs. full information coverage, and global vs. temporal text information during training, by fine-tuning different configurations of a pretrained flow-based diffusion transformer (DiT) and using a multi-stage inference-time prompt rewriter. Further, we introduce a new text-alignment evaluation protocol inspired by Davidsonian Scene Graphs (DSGs) for a fine-grained, interpretable measure of faithfulness of TTM methods. With multiple metrics, we show 1) that fine-tuning our DiT on SCAPs significantly improves text-alignment on music generation outputs while also improving quality, and 2) our proposed Music DSG metric better correlates with human preference than CLAP.

papers.title: Generative Forecasting from Coarse-Grained Observations: When Does Cascading Help?
papers.abstract: We study probabilistic forecasting of dynamical systems such as fluids and waves from coarse observations. Since the unseen fine scales influence the dynamics, the same coarse initial state can evolve into a whole distribution of futures. Generative forecasters may produce visually plausible samples, but it is hard to tell whether they sample the right conditional distribution, since trajectory data contain a single future for each initial state. We address this problem by generating reference data in a hierarchical way: for each coarse initial state, we generate many different fine-scale components and numerically evolve the full states. Using these conditional ensembles, we show that standard diffusion models and stochastic interpolants make substantial distributional errors. We then show that cascading shorter forecasts greatly reduces these errors for the turbulent flows and waves we study, but we also find and characterize cases in which it hurts. Since the coarse process is not Markov, cascading discards information about the unresolved fine scales even with exact transitions. To understand this, we propose a solvable analytic model which shows that the optimal cascade depth decreases as the coupling between the unresolved and observed scales gets stronger, and increases as the dependence of the forecast on the observation becomes more oscillatory. Consistent with our experiments, cascading is detrimental when the direct forecast is ``easy'' to learn, for example Gaussian as in the passive scalar case. We release our datasets as a first benchmark for probabilistic forecasting with ground-truth conditional ensembles.

papers.title: A note on the quantization of M2-branes on local Calabi-Yau manifolds
papers.abstract: In this note we present a detailed computation of the BPS states from M2-branes wrapping 2-cycles in local Calabi-Yau manifolds, at the level of brane quantization. For the cases of local Calabi-Yau threefolds, the supersymmetric quantum mechanics is the 1d $\mathcal{N}=4$ non-linear sigma model. We achieve systematic, physical interpretations of refined Gopakumar-Vafa (GV) invariants, first for the curve classes with fixed geometric genus, and then for curves whose geometric genus jumps. The BPS states of 5d $\mathcal{N}=1$ superconformal field theories are interpreted from the local geometries, which are presented in a number of case studies. In particular, we compute the refined GV invariants for generalized conifolds, local CY3 giving 5d $\mathcal{N}=1$ gauge theories and a singularity whose crepant resolution contains a singular divisor. For the cases of local Calabi-Yau fourfolds, we point out the supersymmetric quantum mechanics is of type $\mathcal{N}=2B$. We set up the framework for studying M2-branes wrapping 2-cycles, and discuss a few cases of M2-brane wrapping genus-0 curves with this new approach.

papers.title: Shaped by What's Missing: Topological Invariance Simplification Discovers Behavioral Transitions
papers.abstract: Understanding how animals move between behaviors is a central question in neuroethology, yet most segmentation methods first partition time into discrete states, leaving transitions as the unmodeled residue between them. We take the opposite view: in a suitable feature space, sustained behaviors are dense regions of the trajectory's density landscape, and transitions are the sparse corridors and loops that connect them. Because this structure is a property of the landscape's shape rather than of any particular coordinates, it can be read off directly with topology and should persist across feature spaces. We build this landscape from frame-by-frame trajectories, extract its discrete-Morse graph, and keep two kinds of structure: paths, the corridors a trajectory follows between dense behavioral regions, and cycles, closed routes whose entry and exit take different ways. Clustering these structures yields transitions directly, with no upstream state partition. On a rat behavior dataset across three feature spaces, including the latent space of a neural-network controller that imitates the animal in a physics simulator, the approach recovers transitions at coverage comparable to state-space and topological-clustering baselines, while carrying substantially more information about the transition identity, forming clusters at least as tight as the baselines', and matching annotated transitions with less reliance on time-warping. More broadly, the results show that behavioral transitions are a topological feature of a representation: recoverable from the shape of its trajectories, and consistent across distinct feature spaces.

papers.title: Getting a Grip: Operating Human-Agent Software Teams Through Governed Messages
papers.abstract: Software is increasingly developed by teams in which several people direct many coding agents from different vendors. Such teams must establish who may request what from whom, which messages start work, which decisions bind, and who caused a change. We propose to govern a human-agent team through its message protocol and present yoars, a relay in which humans and agents are authenticated principals that exchange typed, addressed messages in rooms holding goals, decision rules, routing and an attributable, append-only record. This report gives the architecture, the full controlled study and the field material. In 926 controlled runs (899 analyzable), small agent teams built programs under varied room rules, some with a hostile member planting a backdoor. Revising which messages start work, bundled with limits on repeated messages, was followed by a drop in total coordination failure from 42% to 13% (p = .0063, adjusted p = .057 over nine registered tests). Instructed roles and votes did not reliably produce the intended process, and no defense inside the conversation reliably prevented the backdoor. An auditor read the records of 96 runs with a confirmed backdoor. In the 25 runs where the attacker had persuaded a teammate to write it, the auditor named the persuader in all 25, but it also flagged 24 of 40 honest runs. In a four-week field study, up to nineteen agents and two people developed a distributed system through yoars, producing 7,457 acts. Human attention and decision making emerged as the critical resource: requests waited mainly for the human-run coordinator and for approvals, while agents answered within minutes. Most governance requirements emerged from operation, and holding context dominated token cost. We report twenty-six failures of our own instruments, derive seven lessons and a checklist, and release the corpus, the redacted room ledger and the analysis scripts.

papers.title: Learning Timeline-Preserving Speech-to-Speech Translation
papers.abstract: Speech-to-speech translation (S2ST) increasingly preserves what is said and how it sounds, but not necessarily when speech and silence occur. For dubbing and other temporally grounded applications, matching total duration is not enough: speech and pauses must also occur at corresponding moments. We formulate timeline-preserving S2ST, which aims to preserve the source endpoint and salient internal pauses on a shared absolute timeline. We present TransDubber, an end-to-end autoregressive system that learns this temporal structure directly from aligned target waveforms, without inference-time frame-level timing control or post-hoc temporal correction. To provide this supervision, we construct 642K exactly duration-matched English-Chinese speech pairs by translating and synthesizing target speech on source-defined temporal scaffolds. Training combines a progressive supervised curriculum with verifier-guided reinforcement learning to balance translation quality and temporal alignment. On a 4,353-utterance test set spanning read and spontaneous speech, TransDubber increases the proportion of translations within 2% of the source duration from 25.6% to 61.5% and pause-alignment F1 from 0.118 to 0.550 compared with UniSS, while maintaining competitive translation quality. Our analysis shows that aligned supervision establishes timeline following, while reinforcement learning refines temporal precision and partially offsets the translation-quality cost of strict synchronization. Together, these results demonstrate the effectiveness of our data and training framework for timeline-preserving S2ST. Audio samples, code, datasets, and pretrained models are available at https://zhishengzheng.com/transdubber/.

papers.title: ALDER: A Single-Loop Augmented-Lagrangian Damped Extragradient Method for Nonconvex--Concave Minimax Problems with Nonlinear Coupled Constraints
papers.abstract: ALDER, a single-loop augmented-Lagrangian damped extragradient method, is proposed for smooth nonconvex--concave minimax problems with nonlinear coupled inequality constraints. Within an augmented-Lagrangian framework, ALDER combines prediction--correction steps for the primal variables with explicit projected-and-relaxed multiplier updates in a single loop. The penalty parameter is fixed throughout each run, eliminating inner-loop subproblem solves and iterative penalty updates. We establish uniform boundedness of the relaxed multiplier sequence and, under an extended Mangasarian--Fromovitz constraint qualification, boundedness of the projected output multiplier. Building on these bounds, we show that ALDER finds an $\varepsilon$-KKT point within $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-7/2})$ complete first-order oracle evaluations in the strongly concave setting and $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-4})$ in the concave setting. These bounds improve upon the best known complexity bounds for multi-loop algorithms for this problem class, achieved by FAL, by removing a $\log(1/\varepsilon)$ factor, while retaining a single-loop update structure.

papers.title: Multilingual TASU: Extending Text-Only Alignment to Multilingual Speech Recognition via Simulated CTC Posteriors
papers.abstract: Speech Large Language Models (Speech LLMs) achieve strong multilingual ASR when large-scale paired speech-text data is available, yet such resources remain scarce and highly imbalanced across languages. Text-Only Alignment for Speech Understanding (TASU) alleviates this bottleneck by training cross-modal alignment from simulated CTC posteriors without paired audio, but prior work has been limited to English, leaving open whether text-driven alignment can scale to the multilingual setting where data sparsity and cross-lingual phonetic interference amplify the difficulty of learning a shared alignment interface. In this work, we investigate TASU-style posterior alignment as a means of mitigating paired-data scarcity in multilingual ASR. We adopt the native 50,002-way posterior space of a frozen OWSM-CTC frontend as a shared multilingual interface to Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, and systematically compare three supervision sources on eight Multilingual LibriSpeech languages: real audio-derived posteriors, heuristic CTC Posterior Simulation (CPS), and posteriors generated by a learned multilingual simulator. With real posteriors, LoRA adaptation reduces pooled WER from 10.08% (standalone OWSM-CTC) to 8.21%, improving all eight languages. For text-only alignment, the learned simulator substantially outperforms heuristic CPS and attains 10.51% WER with LoRA. Notably, a CPS-initialized model reaches 9.19% WER after only one real-posterior adaptation epoch using merely one-ninth of the complete MLS paired-speech training set, demonstrating that text-first initialization can drastically reduce the amount of paired audio required for competitive multilingual ASR. These findings establish TASU as a viable multilingual alignment framework and highlight text-only simulation as an effective remedy for paired-data scarcity and imbalance across languages.

papers.title: On Certain Congruences for Partition $k$-Tuples with $5$-Cores
papers.abstract: Let $A_{t,k}(n)$ denote the number of partition $k$-tuples of $n$ with $t$-cores. Using fifth-order modular equations and the Atkin $U_5$-operator, we prove the congruences $A_{5,125i+21}(25n+r)\equiv 0 \pmod{5^3}$ for $r\in\{9,14,19,24\}$, $A_{5,125i+41}(25n+r)\equiv 0 \pmod{5^3}$ for $r\in\{19,24\}$, and $A_{5,125i+111}(125n+r)\equiv 0 \pmod{5^4}$ for $r\in\{39,64,89,114\}$, which were stated by Tang \cite{tang2025iterative}.

papers.title: Photon-loss tolerance of the surface-GKP code with anti-photon-loss decoding
papers.abstract: Photon loss somewhat limits fault-tolerant photonic quantum computing. We investigate its effect on finite-energy Gottesman--Kitaev--Preskill (GKP) states by modeling the pure-loss channel directly. We obtain photon-loss threshold estimates for the surface-GKP code using nearest-lattice-point inner GKP decoding and minimum-weight perfect matching for the outer surface code. For GKP states with $ε=0.01$ and $ε=0.05$, corresponding to GKP squeezing of $20$ and $13\,\mathrm{dB}$, the estimated thresholds are $γ^\ast=5.5\%$ ($0.24\,\mathrm{dB}$) and $γ^\ast=5.9\%$ ($0.26\,\mathrm{dB}$), respectively. We then introduce an anti-photon-loss inner decoder that compensates for the contraction of the measured quadrature. It increases the corresponding threshold estimates to $γ^\ast=9.8\%$ ($0.45\,\mathrm{dB}$) and $γ^\ast=6.3\%$ ($0.28\,\mathrm{dB}$). Our results highlight the importance of accounting for loss-induced lattice contraction in inner decoding and demonstrate that quadrature compensation enhances the photon-loss tolerance of surface-GKP codes for both high- and moderate-quality GKP states, providing a route toward more photon-loss-robust optical quantum computing.

papers.title: Nonnegativity Shapes Predictive Uncertainty: Complementary Model Fits and Quantile Construction
papers.abstract: Knowing that a response cannot be negative can inform predictive uncertainty, including extreme upper quantiles. This knowledge matters especially when a black-box system returns long vector responses at few covariate settings, leaving large uncertainty across many entries. We develop a framework that assembles predictive distributions feature by feature from distributional fits that incorporate nonnegativity, optionally around any given mean predictor. The fits come from a latent factor model that represents response intensity through nonnegative patterns whose amplitudes follow rectified Gaussian processes over covariates. A variational algorithm jointly learns the factorization and the latent posterior. Varying a conditional-dispersion parameter yields a spectrum of fits that show complementary strengths in estimating distributional shape features. An orthogonal quantile expansion motivates using L-moments or their ratios as features. We select a fit separately for each using scores computable from a single validation observation per entry, then assemble the selected estimates through the expansion. In simulations, this construction reduces extreme upper-quantile errors by 17-22% relative to the respective best single fit, despite the mode-seeking tendency of our variational inference. In a streamflow demonstration across agricultural catchments, using an external point simulation to supply the mean reduces miss rates of rare shortage by 86-91%.

papers.title: Robust 3DMA GNSS Positioning in Urban Areas Using Conservative Candidate Set Determination Based on GNSS Shadow and Reflection
papers.abstract: In urban environments, global navigation satellite system (GNSS) positioning is often degraded by signal blockage and reflection caused by surrounding buildings. To address this problem, various three-dimensional mapping-aided (3DMA) GNSS techniques have been proposed. Among them, zonotope shadow and reflection matching (ZSRM) has demonstrated effective positioning performance by determining the candidate receiver position set using predicted GNSS shadow and reflection regions. However, ZSRM remains vulnerable to satellite signal misclassification, which may lead to positioning failure. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a conservative candidate set determination strategy for robust ZSRM positioning. Instead of using only the most probable signal reception condition from an artificial intelligence (AI)-based classifier, the proposed method combines the candidate regions associated with the two most probable classes. This allows the candidate receiver position set to be determined more conservatively, reducing the risk of positioning failure under signal misclassification. The proposed method was evaluated using real-world urban GNSS data. Experimental results show that the proposed method improved the positioning success rate to 100% for RF, GBDT, and SVM classifiers, compared with 8.2%-30.1% for the existing ZSRM algorithm using individual classifier outputs and 96.6% for ZSRM with unanimous voting. Although the proposed method increased the position bounds by retaining additional candidate regions, it produced smaller position bounds than ZSRM with unanimous voting. These results demonstrate that the proposed method substantially enhances the robustness of ZSRM under satellite signal misclassification in urban GNSS environments.

papers.title: Spatial Token Interleaving and Two-Pass BP Decoding for Semantic Image Transmission
papers.abstract: Semantic error control coding (SECC) can correct the residual errors of a standard channel code with a foundation model that supplies a prior on the source content, but existing SECC schemes are designed for text. In this paper, we develop SECC for image transmission with spatial token interleaving and a two-pass belief propagation (BP) schedule. At the transmitter, a vector-quantized (VQ) tokenizer converts an image into tokens, which are transmitted in multiple low-density parity-check (LDPC) code blocks of fifth-generation New Radio (5G NR). In raster order, a block that BP fails to decode corrupts consecutive token rows, so the interleaver reorders the tokens such that adjacent tokens are carried by different blocks, without additional transmitted bits. At the receiver, after the first BP pass, token recovery fuses the token probabilities given by BP with the predictions of the autoregressive model Emu3-Gen, and the second BP pass decodes each block again with the fused distributions as priors on the information bits. On Kodak24 at 0.5 channel uses per pixel and a signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of 0.15 dB, the second pass removes 92% of the token errors left by token recovery, and interleaving reduces the final token error rate by 88%. At medium to high SNR, the proposed receiver exceeds deep joint source--channel coding baselines with the same channel uses by at least 1.2 dB in peak signal-to-noise ratio.

papers.title: CLT for the Weight of the Minimum Spanning Arborescence on the Complete Directed Graph
papers.abstract: The minimum spanning arborescence (MSA) with a fixed boundary, defined on weighted directed graphs, is the directed analogue of the minimum spanning tree (MST). The behaviour of the MSA has been of recent interest and is known to be quite different from that of its undirected counterpart. On the complete directed graph, and for edge weights given by i.i.d. random variables with a broad class of distributions, we prove a Central Limit Theorem for the weight of the MSA with appropriate scaling. While the scaling for the CLT is similar to MST case explored by Janson, the centering required ($1$ as opposed to $ζ(3)$ for Uniform$[0,1]$ weights) and the limiting variance of the Gaussian ($1$ as opposed to $6ζ(4)-4ζ(3)$ for Uniform$[0,1]$ weights) are notably different.

papers.title: Vision-based Sensing of Urban Environment using Hardware-Software co-design at Scale
papers.abstract: Urban environmental monitoring is crucial for climate-adaptive cities, yet current approaches rely heavily on human inspection, overhead remote sensing, or limited terrestrial RGB imagery, thereby lacking comprehensive multispectral perspectives at street level. To bridge this gap, this paper introduces UrbanScapes, an adaptable and flexible hardware-software co-design platform for large-scale, vision-based sensing of urban environments. Built on a modular architecture, UrbanScapes seamlessly integrates multispectral imaging channels, including Red, Green, Blue (RGB), Near-Infrared, and Thermal, to capture multispectral street-level imagery. The system is designed for both opportunistic deployment on bicycles, vehicles, or pedestrians and targeted deployments on municipal fleets, ensuring high spatio-temporal scalability without requiring hardware redesigns. Crucially, the platform utilizes on-device deep learning models to automatically remove personally identifiable information (PII) at the edge, addressing privacy concerns inherent in street-level data collection. By combining this multispectral street-level imagery with overhead multispectral remote sensing imagery, UrbanScapes enables scalable calculation of physics-based environmental indices, providing a foundational tool for advanced citywide analysis.

papers.title: Optimal portfolio and consumption under no-shorting constraints: The exploratory formulation and reinforcement learning
papers.abstract: We develop a reinforcement-learning framework for the continuous-time optimal portfolio-consumption via utility maximization under no-shorting portfolio constraints. We adopt the exploratory formulation under entropy regularization and impose no-shorting constraint through a componentwise nonnegative conditional-mean constraint on the class of admissible randomized policies, while the sampled actions are allowed to be negative during the training. For CRRA utility, we derive the homothetic value function and the optimal Gaussian portfolio and Gibbs consumption policies under some model conditions and establish a verification theorem. These results allow compatible parameterizations in actor, critic, and $q$ functions for a constrained policy-iteration algorithm. Policy evaluation uses trajectory-based moment conditions, and policy improvement uses fitted coefficients to solve a convex quadratic program over the nonnegative orthant without requiring market coefficients as inputs. The mean constraint preserves tractable Gaussian exploration throughout parameter learning, while modal deployment converts the learned randomized policies into deterministic controls. In particular, the Gaussian mode coincides with its constrained mean and hence satisfies no-shorting constraint, and the Gibbs mode determines the deployed consumption rule.

papers.title: Boosted Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Solving Homogeneous and Non-Homogeneous Lane-Emden Type Equations
papers.abstract: The Lane-Emden Equation is a class of nonlinear differential equations commonly used to model phenomena in astrophysics and mathematical physics, such as stellar structure and thermal behavior in polytropic gas spheres. This study presents a novel hybrid framework that integrates Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) with boosting methods to enhance the accuracy and robustness of solutions for Lane-Emden type differential equations. Standard PINNs leverage physical laws encoded within the loss function, but their predictive performance can be constrained by optimization challenges and approximation errors. To address this, we introduce a post-processing boosting stage where the residual errors from the PINN prediction are modeled using some regression algorithms - including LightGBM, Random Forest, XGBoost, and Support Vector Regression (SVR). The outputs from these boosted models are aggregated to generate a corrected, high-fidelity prediction. The proposed methodology is systematically validated through quantitative metrics and comparative analysis against the standard PINN baseline. The results demonstrate that the boosted PINN framework significantly reduces prediction error, and improves generalization, offering a powerful and flexible approach for solving scientific and engineering problems governed by differential equations.

papers.title: Additive mappings of unweighted directed graphs preserving individual values of the cycle length
papers.abstract: On the set of unweighted directed graphs on $n$ vertices, the union of graphs is defined as the union of their arc sets. A mapping of graphs is said to be additive if it preserves the union operation. In this paper, a characterization of additive mappings of unweighted directed graphs preserving a fixed value $k \geq 3$ of the cycle length is obtained.

papers.title: The e-Property for Quantum Markov Semigroups
papers.abstract: Let $(\mathcal{T}_t)_{t\geqslant0}$ be a quantum Markov semigroup on a von Neumann algebra and let $\mathcal{A}$ be an invariant Feller $C^*$-algebra. We formulate the $e$-property on the full state space and show that its quantitative defect is equivalent, within an optimal factor two, to the Hausdorff measure of non-compactness of observable orbits. We develop Cesàro and Lip-norm criteria and a generalised Doeblin minorisation by a state-space contracting positive map, including finite-dimensional and measure-prepare factorisations. When every observable has the $e$-property, the Jacobs--de Leeuw--Glicksberg decomposition identifies the reversible Choi--Effros algebra and the norm-stable sector. Expected and decoherence-free subalgebras transfer the property under norm decay of the complementary dynamics, including infinite-dimensional ultracontractive and finite-index Pimsner--Popa regimes. Finally, we establish the full comparison hierarchy among ordinary, eventual, Cesàro and pointwise eventual equicontinuity notions, reinforced by matrix Jamison and homoclinic flow counterexamples. Projection-face criteria are treated in a companion paper.

papers.title: LoD-Loc v4: Towards Generalized Aerial Visual Localization via Panoptic LoD 3D Map Registration
papers.abstract: Aerial visual localization over Level-of-Detail (LoD) 3D Maps has recently gained significant traction due to its global scalability, storage efficiency, and privacy-preserving nature. However, existing methods rely almost exclusively on building elements, which leads to catastrophic localization failures in rural or undeveloped areas where buildings are sparse or non-existent. To address this, we construct a unified Panoptic LoD 3D Map by fusing OpenStreetMap (OSM), Digital Elevation Models (DEM), and LoD assets, reformulating the problem as a panoptic registration task. By parsing the query image into discrete building `thing' instances and continuous `stuff' regions comprising road, vegetation, and water, we establish a holistic alignment with this map to robustly optimize the camera pose. To enable reliable panoptic perception, we develop a new automated pipeline that constructs AirPan - the largest aerial panoptic segmentation dataset to date, comprising 85k images with pixel-accurate annotations. This empowers our panoptic segmentation model to exhibit remarkable zero-shot generalization capabilities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LoD-Loc v4 consistently outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) baselines by a significant margin. Most notably, it successfully maintains reliable localization in building-less scenarios, completely overcoming the catastrophic failures of prior building-centric paradigms.

papers.title: Estimating Average Treatment Effects with Projected Instrumental Variables
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a projected instrumental variable framework that relaxes conventional assumptions for causal identification with instrumental variables. Building on the interpretation of conditional expectation as an orthogonal projection in a Hilbert space, the framework replaces the conditional expectation operator with a general projection operator. We provide an alternative inverse problem formulation based on the Riesz representation. Drawing on semiparametric efficiency theory, we further develop debiased and adaptive machine learning methods for estimation and inference. The proposed framework connects invalid instrumental variables to instrumented difference-in-differences. We also examine invalid projected instrumental variables and discuss their relationship to existing methods. Simulation studies and real data analysis demonstrate that the proposed methods perform favorably compared with existing approaches.

papers.title: Charged Gravastars with Casimir Energy in Quadratic f(T) Gravity
papers.abstract: We investigate a charged gravastar configuration in the framework of modified teleparallel gravity, considering the quadratic form $f(T)=T+αT^{2}$ and incorporating Casimir vacuum energy as a source for the interior region. The gravastar is constructed as a three-region configuration consisting of a Casimir-energy dominated vacuum interior, an intermediate thin shell of ultra-relativistic matter satisfying the equation of state $p=ρ$, and an exterior Reissner-Nordstrom spacetime. The modified field equations are derived for a static, spherically symmetric geometry, and the interior and shell solutions are obtained by incorporating the contributions of Casimir energy and the electromagnetic field. The matching between the interior and exterior geometries is performed using the Israel-Darmois junction conditions, from which the surface energy density and pressure of the shell are determined. We examine the physical properties of the configuration through the proper length, shell energy, and entropy. The influence of the charge parameter on these quantities is also investigated. The resulting profiles remain finite and smooth across the shell, while the proper length, energy, and entropy exhibit regular behaviour with increasing shell thickness. The model provides a framework for studying the interplay between quantum vacuum effects, electric charge, and torsional modifications of gravity in compact-object configurations.

papers.title: Verification-Gated Redraw and Repair for Local Small Language Models: A Paired Evaluation
papers.abstract: Executable checks can reject incorrect model-generated programs, but rejection alone does not determine whether fresh sampling or diagnostic repair is preferable. We present a controlled, resource-bounded conceptual replication and extension of established recovery policies: a single answer (N), one verification-triggered redraw (R), and one diagnostic repair (D), for Ornith 1.5 9B and Gemma 4 E4B served locally in nominal 4-bit MLX format. The frozen evaluation contains 72 tasks: 40 HumanEval+ problems, 16 SQL tasks and 16 shell tasks. Policies share initial responses and use only public checks for online decisions; every candidate is model-generated. Each task has one stochastic trajectory per model, so the study does not estimate variation across independent sampling blocks. Redraw increases observed final-test success from 51.4% to 59.7% for Ornith and from 55.6% to 62.5% for Gemma. Diagnostic repair reaches 52.8% and 63.9%, respectively. None of four internally prespecified paired contrasts is significant after Holm correction (minimum adjusted p = 0.125). Public checks falsely accept 25 Ornith and 11 Gemma candidates, demonstrating that acceptance is not a correctness guarantee. A post-review audit of initial answers gives perfect-retry upper bounds of 76.4% and 87.5%, respectively: accepted initial errors cannot trigger recovery under the fixed gate. This one-block, resource-bounded study provides a finite-cohort experimental record, not policy equivalence, a general model ranking or universal reliability

papers.title: von Neumann-Morgenstern stable sets in job matching problems
papers.abstract: We show that a von Neumann-Morgenstern (vNM) stable set generically exists in the many-to-one job-matching model. Unlike the core, which can be empty in this model, a vNM stable set exists whenever there is a unique efficient matching: the set of all individually rational (IR) and efficient outcomes form a vNM stable set. If an economy has multiple efficient matchings, a vNM stable set may not exist. If the vNM stable sets are required to be rich in a certain sense, then such a rich vNM stable set exists if and only if the set of efficient matchings is essentially unique, and the set of all efficient and IR outcomes forms the unique rich vNM stable set.

papers.title: Absorption and scattering of massless scalar waves by black holes with scalar hair
papers.abstract: We use partial waves to study massless scalar absorption and scattering by the normal ($ξ=5$) and phantom ($ξ=-2$) Bakopoulos--Nakas black holes, described by mass $M$ and scalar charge $q$. At fixed mass $M=1$, increasing $q/M$ decreases the horizon area and geometric capture cross section in the normal branch, but it increases both in the phantom branch. The low-frequency absorption tends to the horizon area, while photon-sphere scaling brings the absorption spectra close together. In scattering picture, charge and branch change the interference pattern, and higher frequencies make the fringes narrow. However, matching the capture or glory scale of the normal branch with Reissner--Nordström black holes indicates finite-frequency differences.

papers.title: Free energy of spherical vector spin glasses
papers.abstract: We identify the limit free energy of spherical vector spin glasses by a variational formula. The covariance function need not be convex. Using the global symmetry of the spin configurations, we introduce a family of constraint measures that gives a disintegration of the original spin distribution. We first identify the limit free energy of each constrained model and then apply the Laplace method to recover that of the original model.

papers.title: Certified computation of Buehler confidence limits for system reliability
papers.abstract: Component tests can support a lower confidence limit for a system that has not been tested as a whole, but numerical optimization can compromise its coverage. A feasible point in the minimization defining a Buehler limit gives an upper bound on that limit; reporting it can therefore overstate reliability. We develop a computation that maintains lower and upper bounds on the ideal endpoint for a prescribed ordering. Bounds over entire parameter regions justify the reported lower endpoint at every completed checkpoint, including under adaptive stopping and selection among runs. Separate refinement conditions establish convergence, and an explicit error allocation accounts for simulated tail probabilities and confidence-region localization. The theory retains nuisance and dependence parameters in the observation model. Monotone corner bounds give the implemented specialization for scalar and two-component binomial systems; Bernstein and probability-distance bounds provide further theoretical constructions. Four benchmark problems reach a certified width of $10^{-5}$ under each of four search strategies. Additional stochastic candidates increase cost without reducing subdivisions, whereas complete sample-space enumeration verifies the implemented coverage at three parameter vectors. For the all-success example, the certified lower limit is $0.68128$, compared with $0.41738$ from Bonferroni-adjusted component limits.

papers.title: Personalized Rollout Allocation for Federated LQR Policy Optimization under Heterogeneous Process Noise
papers.abstract: We study federated model-free learning of a common linear quadratic regulator (LQR) gain under a limited uplink communication budget, with clients that share dynamics and costs but experience different process-noise levels. Conventionally, clients transmit gradient matrices whose dimension equals the number of controller parameters. Exploiting the structure of two-point zeroth-order estimates, we consider an implementation in which clients transmit only one scalar cost-difference coefficient per rollout pair, while the server regenerates the associated perturbation directions from shared seeds. Communication thus scales with the number of rollout pairs rather than the controller dimension, turning the uplink budget into a rollout budget. Because noise heterogeneity produces gradient estimates of widely differing variance and every client carries equal weight in the fleet objective, uniform rollout allocation allows noisy clients to dominate the aggregated update and increases the probability of destabilizing updates. We propose a rollout-allocation scheme that assigns rollout pairs in proportion to the standard deviation of each client's estimates and show that it minimizes the variance of the aggregated update. The scheme is implemented exactly through a greedy integer allocation rule whose weights are estimated from the communicated scalars. We further prove that a single allocation factor quantifies its improvement over uniform allocation in a one-round instability bound, the certified step size, and the error floor of a joint stability and convergence guarantee. Simulations show that, under the same communication budget, personalized allocation reduces the one-step instability rate from $37\%$ to $0.3\%$.

papers.title: Adversarial Robustness Is Not Zero-Day Generalization: A Controlled Evaluation of Flow-Based Intrusion Detectors on Corrected CIC-IDS2017
papers.abstract: Synthetic variants of known attacks, including feature-space adversarial perturbations, are sometimes used as stand-ins for unseen ("zero-day") attacks when evaluating machine-learning network intrusion detection systems (NIDS). We test whether this proxy holds. On the corrected CIC-IDS2017 release we train Random Forest, XGBoost, a 1D-CNN and an FT-Transformer and compare, at a fixed 1% false-positive rate over five seeds, detection under constrained perturbations of known attacks (gradient-based and black-box attacks on 42 attacker-controllable features) with leave-one-attack-family-out (LOAO) detection, where an entire family is absent from training. Detection under the strongest perturbation we tested, with budgets of at most 0.2, stays between 90.9% and 99.7%, yet mean detection of held-out families falls to 76.2% (RF), 40.2% (XGBoost), 25.8% (1D-CNN) and 22.8% (FT-Transformer). Robustness exceeds LOAO detection for every model (gaps of 24 to 72 percentage points, 23 to 66 when robustness is also averaged over families; Holm-adjusted p $\le$ 0.00096), and the two measures agree at most on a coarse ranking of the models. An exact mixed-integer evasion search confirms the tree ensembles' scores. Benign-only anomaly detectors and a simple multi-class open-set baseline do not close the gap. A temporal split on 5 seeds (3 of the 4 models) leaves the gap in place. On CSE-CIC-IDS2018 the gap recurs for every model (16 to 68 points). On these benchmarks and under this threat model, a robustness score should not be read as a zero-day score, and the two should be reported separately. Code and per-seed results are publicly available.

papers.title: Cube-freeness and a square formula for canonical trace ideals of Stanley--Reisner rings
papers.abstract: Let $I$ be a monomial ideal in $S=\mathbb{k}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, and set $R=S/I$. We prove that if $I$ is $\mathbf{a}$-bounded and $M$ is a positively $\mathbf{b}$-determined $R$-module, then $\mathrm{tr}_R(M)$ is $(\mathbf{a}+\mathbf{b})$-bounded. For the canonical module, this gives the bound $2\mathbf{a}$. In particular, the canonical trace ideal of every Stanley--Reisner ring is a cube-free monomial ideal. We also prove that, for a Stanley--Reisner ring satisfying $(S_2)$, the canonical trace ideal is the square of its radical if and only if the ring satisfies $(G_2)$.

papers.title: Adversarial robustness does not entail human-aligned categorization
papers.abstract: Adversarial training can improve some forms of correspondence between artificial and biological vision, but whether robust classifiers acquire human-aligned classification behavior remains unclear. We generated 1,008 controversial stimuli by optimizing latent inputs to a pretrained GAN to elicit high-confidence disagreements between pairs of robust ImageNet classifiers. We compared four adversarially robust ImageNet classifiers - ResNet-101, ViT-B, ConvNeXt-L, and Swin-L - with two-alternative category judgments from 60 participants. We first evaluated each classifier on stimuli optimized to elicit disagreement with another model. Across classifiers, accuracy in predicting individual participants' single-trial category choices was near chance (48.6-51.3%), whereas majority judgments from other participants predicted responses with 85.0-86.8% accuracy. An analysis incorporating model prediction strength and participants' reported confidence found weak positive model-human correspondence for the two convolutional models. On stimuli optimized for disagreement between other model pairs, all four robust classifiers predicted human responses above chance but less accurately than predictions based on other participants' majority judgments; the same pattern held for 17 additional RobustBench models not used in stimulus generation. Across these 17 models, mean model-participant agreement was 67.3%, versus 81.3% mean participant-participant agreement on the same images. These results identify model-specific failures of human alignment and a model-human mismatch that persists across robust classifiers and substantially exceeds disagreement among human observers. Our findings show that adversarial robustness alone does not guarantee human-aligned categorization and suggest that robustness and human alignment should be evaluated as distinct properties of visual recognition systems.

papers.title: Uncertainty Aware Quality-Diversity Optimization For Offline Biological Sequence Design
papers.abstract: Designing sequences such as nucleic acids and proteins with desired properties is a fundamental challenge in biology. Due to the vast, discrete nature of sequence spaces and the high cost of experimental evaluation, offline computational sequence design plays a crucial role in proposing novel sequences before costly wet-lab validation. In practice, it is also essential that proposed designs are diverse to increase the likelihood of downstream experimental success. This motivates methods that balance performance, novelty, and diversity, whilst mitigating against uncertainty inherent to offline optimization. Quality-Diversity optimization (QD) can discover diverse, high-performing solutions, making it well suited to this problem, but its elitist nature makes reliable exploration under uncertainty challenging. To address this, we introduce Prior-guided Offline MAP-Elites (POME), an uncertainty-aware QD framework explicitly adapted to the offline regime. Our method leverages foundation models as priors to guide search toward biologically plausible regions and enable robust exploration under uncertainty. Across three sequence design tasks, POME consistently improves both performance and diversity over prior offline QD methods, and achieves the most reliable balance compared to offline MBO baselines, obtaining the best performance on two tasks and the second-best on the third, while maintaining high diversity and novelty.

papers.title: Cutoff for Simple Random Walk on Preferential Attachment Graphs
papers.abstract: We consider simple random walk on the sequential affine preferential attachment graphs with fixed parameters $m\ge2$ and $δ\ge0$. We prove the walk has total-variation cutoff, and for every fixed $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, \[ t_{\mathrm{mix}}^{(n)}(\varepsilon) =\frac{\log n}{νd} +O_{\mathbb P}\!\left(\sqrt{\log n}\right), \] where $ν>0$ is the walk speed and $d>0$ is the entropy per level of harmonic measure on the Pólya--point tree, the local weak limit of the graph. Thus cutoff occurs at the entropic time. Entropic cutoff was previously established for a range of random graph models including configuration models under mild degree assumptions and on Erdős--Rényi random graphs for typical starting points. We extend the harmonic-measure approach to preferential attachment, accounting for its age-dependent structure and hubs of polynomial degree. The local weak limit, the Pólya--point tree, provides a more tractable setting for analyzing the walk. The proof combines regeneration estimates on the local limit tree, a quantitative graph--tree coupling on the mixing-time scale, and control of hub excursions. We show that shortly before the cutoff time its distribution is close in total variation distance to a measure with small $L^\infty$ distance from stationarity. When $m\ge2$, the spectral gap is bounded away from zero with high probability which completes the upper-bound coupling argument.

papers.title: STEER: Route-Aware Adaptive Reasoning for Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: Vision-language action (VLA) models excel for end-to-end autonomous driving, yet their tendency to over-invoke chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning mirrors a human cognitive pitfall: overthinking. Just as deliberate reasoning can slow or mislead human judgment in routine tasks, excessive CoT in VLA incurs unnecessary compute overhead and can paradoxically degrade planning performance. Recent research tackles this via adaptive reasoning, which dynamically modulates inference complexity by selectively triggering CoT for complex scenes while responding directly to routine ones. While prior adaptive methods rely on implicit adaptation, recent work shows that explicitly optimizing the route between CoT and direct responses yields superior performance, assuming scene-difficulty annotations which are labor-intensive, poorly scalable, and prone to error due to the subjectivity of judging driving complexity. We explore, for the first time, whether adaptive reasoning with explicit route optimization can be achieved without any scene-difficulty labeling. We introduce STEER, a generic over-reasoning mitigation strategy featuring two key components: (i) routing uncertainty-aware rollout, which calibrates sampling to align routing diversity with model uncertainty; and (ii) cross-route advantage credit assignment, which introduces a differential metric to reinforce optimal routing decisions based on environmental rewards rather than subjective labels. Extensive experiments on NAVSIM v1/v2 demonstrate that STEER is competitive with state-of-the-art methods in both planning quality and the Pareto front of inference efficiency.

papers.title: Pricing Today, Shaping Tomorrow: Contextual Dynamic Pricing in Purchase-Driven Evolving Systems
papers.abstract: Across diverse markets, it is important for firms to balance attracting customers with managing operational conditions, such as workloads and delivery times. Dynamic pricing plays a central role in this tradeoff, as the orders generated today can change the conditions faced by future customers. We develop a novel framework for contextual dynamic pricing with an observed shared state and unknown purchase-driven transitions. The valuation model allows unknown mean functions of customer covariates and state, unknown state-specific scales and a common unknown standardized noise distribution. We propose Shadow-Adjusted Pricing in Evolving Systems (SHAPE), which incorporates a purchase's future revenue consequences into current pricing. Purchase-shadow adjustment and scale standardization reveal a common one-dimensional oracle price map across states, allowing SHAPE to retain its pricing history across value updates without repeating coarse exploration. The same active sales records support price-map learning and joint updates of continuation values and purchase shadows, without fitting the noise distribution or full transition matrices. To support this reuse under purchase-driven feedback, we establish pricing guarantees for history-dependent inputs and stability bounds for the joint updates. Under regularity, coverage and design conditions, we obtain sublinear expected regret against a finite-horizon dynamic oracle for linear, Hölder and sparse linear mean models. For affine valuations at fixed state and feature dimensions, SHAPE matches the static semiparametric minimax time exponent up to logarithmic factors for every fixed noise-tail smoothness order $β\ge2$. Numerical experiments further demonstrate the appealing performance of SHAPE.

papers.title: Sharp digirth bounds for C(k,k)-subdivisions in digraphs
papers.abstract: For an integer $k\ge2$, let $C(k,k)$ denote the oriented cycle formed by two internally vertex-disjoint directed paths of length $k$ with the same initial and terminal vertices. We extend a problem of Picasarri-Arrieta and Rambaud [European J. Combin. 122 (2024)] on subdivisions of $C(k,k)$ to digraphs with several vertices of out-degree one. Following the sharp result of Chen et al. [arXiv:2610.38574v1 (2026)] for at most one such vertex, we determine the exact digirth threshold when at most $r\ge4$ such vertices are permitted. Specifically, for all integers $k\ge2$ and $r\ge4$, every digraph of minimum out-degree at least one, with at most $r$ vertices of out-degree one and digirth at least $r(k-1)+1$, contains a subdivision of $C(k,k)$.

papers.title: Representation-Aware Closed-Surface Parameterization: Exact Sensitivity Analysis and Pole-Aware Planar Preconditioning
papers.abstract: Surface parameterization is a fundamental task in geometry processing and shape analysis. For topologically closed surfaces, it is common to parameterize them onto a standardized closed domain in $\mathbb{R}^3$, with a prime example being a unit sphere for genus-0 closed surfaces. Many mapping methods use planar projections and perform computations on the plane rather than directly on the 3D surface. However, perturbations introduced before projection or geometric evolution propagate through the computation and may affect map quality, convergence, stopping behavior, and geometric validity. In this work, we formulate representation sensitivity as a branchwise input--output problem, separating smooth propagation through active Jacobians from changes in anchors, stopping rules, and fallback events. Under consistent piecewise-linear assembly, the unmodified south-pole Beltrami correction in the FLASH method for spherical conformal parameterization reduces exactly to source-mesh harmonic extension. On a fixed-anchor branch, the corrected map factors into chart transition, harmonic propagation, and inverse stereographic projection, yielding an explicit sensitivity Jacobian and a finite-triangle conditioning bound. Separately, we introduce a bounded five-parameter affine preconditioner over planar scale, translation, and anisotropy and evaluate candidates on the corrected spherical map. Across 30 genus-0 surfaces, it reduces median polar upper-tail log-condition and chord-angle distortion by $10.17\%$ and $10.97\%$, respectively, with both measures improving on every mesh. We also apply the framework to other spherical mapping methods including the conformalized mean-curvature flow and spherical density-equalizing maps. Altogether, our work highlights the importance of representation selection as a structural and practical component of spherical parameterization and downstream computation.

papers.title: SAVIER: Source-Anchored Visual Inspection and Evidence-Guided Repair for Vietnamese Cultural Text-to-Image Generation
papers.abstract: We present SAVIER, a training-free, one-pass framework that repairs the depiction of a named Vietnamese cultural entity in a generated image while preserving the scene details requested by the user. The problem is hard because a plausible scene can miss the cues that identify the entity, and prompt-level refinement never inspects the image it produces. SAVIER starts from a Culture-TRIP expanded prompt; a Curator separates source-linked cultural cues from prompt-preservation requirements, a prompt-blind Observer describes the first image, and a Refiner turns the discrepancies into at most three positive instructions before one regeneration with the same seed and a fixed bank of reference photographs. On the 50 bilingual prompts of ViCuP, evaluated with SDXL and FLUX.1-dev against a frozen, human-verified visual contract, SAVIER raises contract fulfillment from 55.6 to 69.6 and from 59.1 to 67.3 over Culture-TRIP and raises CAIRE cultural relevance on FLUX.1-dev. A reference-only ablation that removes the agent repair shows that SAVIER's photographs account for most of the contract gain; the agent roles add country-level relevance on FLUX.1-dev without lowering adherence to the original prompt under the official VQAScore. Project page: https://oxyzgiahuy.github.io/savier/

papers.title: Architecting Fairness-Aware LLM Interactions
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used as decision-support tools but may generate stereotypical, discriminatory, or unfair responses. As LLMs become embedded in decision-critical software systems, fairness can no longer be treated as a downstream evaluation step, but must become an architectural concern of the interaction itself. Yet current fairness approaches operate as standalone evaluation techniques, lacking a reusable mechanism to verify and mitigate violations at runtime. We propose a fairness-assurance architecture grounded in three reusable design patterns, instantiated as a multi-agent framework that evaluates and iteratively refines LLM responses before delivery. A preliminary evaluation across eight configurations involving different LLM families shows that the architecture identifies fairness violations and iteratively produces compliant responses in all configurations, with behavior differing depending on the model-family composition. These results provide initial evidence for the joint instantiation of the proposed patterns and a first step toward architecting non-functional properties into LLM-based systems.

papers.title: Unitary implementability of Darboux transformations
papers.abstract: We investigate the unitary implementability of the canonical transformations corresponding to Darboux transformations in the Hamiltonian formalism recently developed for gauge invariant perturbations of nonrotating black holes. Starting from the formalism in the black hole interior, we demonstrate that these canonical transformations are unitarily implementable under general conditions on the effective potentials appearing in the master equations of the perturbations. We also show that the privileged massless Fock representation of the perturbative variables selected by admitting (Heisenberg) unitary dynamics, employed in our quantization, is not unitarily equivalent to the simple massless representation of the master variables satisfying the effective Regge-Wheeler equation. This highlights the importance of the choice of master variables in which the quantum representation is initially defined. Furthermore, we show that not all such choices of variables possessing unitarily implementable dynamics can be reached through Darboux transformations, but rather through more general canonical transformations. These results advance our understanding of the relationship between well-established classical relations in black hole perturbation theory and their quantum representations, explaining how isospectral Darboux transformations can be extended to include all the infinitely many possible values of the angular momentum such that they are unitarily implementable in a quantum field theory context.

papers.title: The Long Con on the Web: Earn-then-Exploit Fraud Attacks against Coding Agents
papers.abstract: Coding agents increasingly operate with web access and high privileges, creating a new attack surface where web fraud can directly target autonomous agents. Existing studies mainly focus on malicious links, prompt injection, and interface deception, while content-level web fraud against agents and the amplification of attacks through agent trust remain underexplored. In this paper, we present EtE (Earn-then-Exploit), a web fraud attack framework against coding agents, in which a malicious website first provides multiple rounds of genuinely verifiable assistance to establish trust and then introduces task-related instructions that cross intended operational boundaries. To systematically evaluate its effectiveness, we construct 56 organizational environments (8 task contexts x 7 attack consequences) and evaluate three representative coding agents. EtE achieves an average scene-level attack success rate of 71.4%, including 85.7% on Codex-GPT-5.5, 67.9% on ZCode-GLM-5.3-Flash, and 60.7% on QwenCode-Qwen3.7-Plus, significantly outperforming all injection-based baselines. More importantly, our experiments reveal that coding agents exhibit trust-like behavioral reliance on previously helpful Web sources, and that such accumulated credibility significantly increases their susceptibility to subsequent malicious instructions. Based on this finding, we propose action-authorization separation (AAS), which prevents web content from directly authorizing privileged actions and reduces the attack success rate to 0% while preserving 100% task completion, outperforming all evaluated defense baselines.

papers.title: Constructing Budgeted KGW Evasion through Token-Event Evidence Replacement
papers.abstract: KGW watermarks bias sampling to accumulate keyed detection evidence. We construct budgeted evasion through token-event evidence replacement using ordinary phrase rewrites. Our construction jointly selects compositions of LLM-proposed alternatives from an independent model and measures global token-edit distance on complete outputs. At the largest attainable cost within the budget, exact coverage search maximizes removal of original scored token pairs. It uses a known tokenizer without the key, detector feedback or queries to the watermarked model. Exact accounting separates source evidence removed, evidence created and length effects, with initial strength setting the required reduction. Separate signed-event analysis found that mean suppression arose mainly from removing watermark-enriched source events. In controlled, occurrence-counted, one-token-context KGW tests on short passages, 39 of 82 qualified, initially detected sources yielded rewrites with terminal detector score Z < 4 that passed blinded source-relative model review, at a mean actual token-edit cost of 16.0% under a 20% allowance. To examine whether this initial requirement can be inferred, a separate historical 95-passage study estimated initial detector score Z0 from generation traces with correlation 0.793 and an in-sample association beyond length. This aggregate information did not establish improved allocation, and the separate no-trace stopping test did not reliably exploit cheaper reviewed crossings in the candidate bank. Comparisons did not establish an advantage over simpler selection and ordinary constrained rewriting. The construction makes budgeted evidence replacement executable while exposing limits in signed reduction and recognition of sufficient editing.

papers.title: Forgetting matters: when subspace optimization accelerates without the strong convexity parameter
papers.abstract: Sequential subspace optimization (SESOP) minimizes the objective exactly over a few directions built from past iterates. It needs no problem constants, is accelerated on smooth convex functions and behaves like an accelerated method in experiments. This led to the conjecture that it is accelerated in the strongly convex case without knowing the strong convexity parameter. We show that the conjecture fails in the worst case. For every subspace method whose memory forgets slowly, namely a window of recent gradients and steps together with cumulative sums with subexponential weights, we construct a counterexample: acceleration requires a window of length of order $\sqrtκ$, where $κ$ is the condition number. SESOP and the plane form of conjugate gradients are therefore not accelerated. Memories that forget fast avoid this obstruction. Pairs of geometric filters give accelerated methods with logarithmic memory or only two stored vectors. They need neither the strong convexity parameter nor the smoothness constant, never restart the iterate and restart their memory at most $O(\logκ)$ times. Finally, the method with fixed activation times remains asymptotically accelerated on functions with Lipschitz Hessian even when each subproblem is solved by a single Newton step.

papers.title: Partition statistics and universal mixed mock modular forms
papers.abstract: In this note, we construct combinatorial statistics in terms of partitions, overpartitions, and two-color partitions and relate the corresponding generating functions to the universal mock theta functions. Our framework primarily builds on two $q$-series identities of Fine.

papers.title: AgentCap: Capability-Based Runtime Authorization for Secure LLM Agent Execution
papers.abstract: Language-model agents commonly collapse two decisions that security systems separate: selecting an action and determining whether that action is authorized. When a model exercises standing authority, indirect prompt injection can convert influence over its reasoning into unauthorized effects. We present AgentCap, a runtime authorization layer that externalizes this decision from the model and mediates every tool invocation through an MCP wrapper. Each request declares an intent, and AgentCap evaluates policy constraints over trust, workflow prerequisites, mutually exclusive authority, and the provenance of security-sensitive arguments. Authorized requests receive short-lived, budget-bounded capability tokens that are validated at the tool boundary. Delegation is restricted to session-bound parent-child chains that preserve action and resource while budget and lifetime can only be attenuated, preventing authority from being expanded or reused across unrelated agent sessions. A declarative policy language provides a common representation for runtime enforcement and predeployment analysis. Across AgentDojo and InjecAgent, AgentCap reduces attack success in every evaluated model-benchmark setting, including zero attack success with GPT-5.4 on both benchmarks. Controlled adversarial scenarios further show that AgentCap blocks every attempted unauthorized execution (ASR 0%) while preserving all legitimate operations exercised. These results demonstrate that agent security requires authorization of model-proposed effects at the tool boundary, independently of the model's reasoning.

papers.title: Stable solutions to $p$-Laplacian type equations with variable coefficients
papers.abstract:
We study stable regular solutions of the variable-coefficient equation $-\operatorname{div}((A(x)
abla u\cdot
abla u)^{p/2-1}A(x)
abla u)=f(u)$ in $B_1\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, where $p>1$, $f\in C^1(\mathbb{R})$ is nonnegative, and $A$ is a locally Lipschitz, symmetric, uniformly elliptic matrix field. We prove quantitative interior Hölder estimates for $n<p+4p/(p-1)$ when $p\ge2$, and for $n<5p$ when $1<p<2$. We also obtain interior energy estimates and higher integrability of the gradient in every dimension. These estimates are given in terms of $\|u\|_{L^1(B_1)}$, with constants depending only on $n,p$, the ellipticity bounds, and a local $L^\infty$ bound for $DA$, but not on $f$ or higher derivatives of $A$. These results extend the corresponding interior estimates of Cabré, Miraglio, and Sanchón for the $p$-Laplace equation to this variable-coefficient setting. The proof uses weighted Hessian estimates to control coefficient errors and a comparison between radial and full gradient energies.

papers.title: Coherent heat-bath configuration interaction with many-body perturbation theory for multivalent atoms
papers.abstract: Combinatorial growth of configuration-interaction spaces limits accurate calculations as the valence-electron number and orbital space increase. To reduce the size of the configuration-interaction space, we develop coherent heat-bath configuration interaction in a configuration-state-function basis and combine it with many-body perturbation theory. Configurations are selected by thresholding their coherent couplings to target wave functions, and a perturbative correction recovers residual valence correlation. For Al, a stringent threshold gives about 16-37 fold compression with excitation-energy deviations from the uncompressed calculations below 0.74 /cm; a looser threshold gives 63-113 fold compression with a maximum deviation of 18.22 /cm. For Si and P, roughly threefold to eightfold compression is achieved with maximum relative deviations of approximately 0.70% and 0.32%, respectively, for optical excitation energies. The perturbative correction improves the accuracy of all calculated total energies. These results support extending the method to high-precision calculations in more complex atomic systems.

papers.title: 8 Bits to End the Loudness War: Lossless Floating-Point Compression for Audio Streams
papers.abstract: We present a native extension to the Free Lossless Audio Codec (FLAC) providing lossless compression for IEEE 754 single-precision (binary32) floating-point audio, alongside a survey and empirical benchmark of existing floating-point compression methods. While professional recording hardware increasingly adopts 32-bit float converters and digital audio workstations process sound exclusively in floating-point math, consumer distribution remains constrained to fixed-point integer PCM. Through Dynamic Positional Alignment (DPA), our implementation achieves approximately 44.1% compression ratios on natural multi-stage ADC recordings--matching the storage footprint of standard 24-bit integer FLAC--and approximately 60.2% on complex digital workstation masters. By preserving dynamic peaks beyond 0 dBFS, the format also allows listeners to undo clipping, providing a practical technical path away from the loudness war with virtually no storage overhead. We do not claim to introduce a fundamentally new compression paradigm; our approach is conceptually similar to the floating-point mechanism in WavPack (which remains undocumented in published literature). Instead, this paper compares existing methods, provides theoretical grounding for why they succeed or fail, benchmarks current codec implementations, and contributes a reference implementation of a proven method within the FLAC ecosystem.

papers.title: Quantized valley source in bilayer graphene via adiabatic quantum pumping
papers.abstract: We propose a quantized valley source based on adiabatic quantum pumping in bilayer graphene in the presence of both quantum spin Hall and quantum valley Hall effects. By periodically modulating the gate voltages of two quantum dots coupled to a bilayer graphene nanoribbon, the helical edge states enable the generation of a pure valley current. Depending on the geometry of quantum dots, the number of emitted valley pairs either forms quantized plateaus or varies continuously with the pumping amplitude. The quantized plateau structure can be tuned by the static gate voltage and by the coupling between the quantum dots and the ribbon. Quantized valley pairs are robust against Anderson disorder applied in the quantum dots and persist for both zigzag and armchair quantum-dot boundaries. These results demonstrate that adiabatic quantum pumping provides a route toward electrically controllable quantized valley sources.

papers.title: MOST: Memory of Object States and Task Progress for Long-Horizon Mobile Manipulation
papers.abstract: Long-horizon embodied manipulation requires policies to act on information that is no longer visible. Modified objects may leave the field of view, while completed subtasks continue to constrain future actions. Existing approaches extend temporal context through recurrent state updates, test-time training, or storage and retrieval of past observations. As horizons grow, these mechanisms can still leave the policy to infer task state from long, redundant, and viewpoint-dependent visual experience. We argue that long-horizon agents benefit not merely from remembering more, but from remembering task-relevant state changes and progress. We propose Memory of Object States and Task Progress (MOST), a policy-internal memory framework that compresses multi-view observations into temporal tokens. Historical and predictive future tokens are explicitly supervised with object states and subtask progress, structuring memory around what has changed in the world and what has already been accomplished. The resulting memory directly conditions action generation within a single end-to-end policy, without an external planner or retrieval stage. We further introduce RoboCasa-Long, a benchmark of multi-minute, multi-stage mobile manipulation tasks. Across RoboCasa365, RoboCasa-Long, and real-world robot experiments, MOST consistently outperforms Xiaomi-Robotics-1 (XR-1), the previous state-of-the-art model. It raises average success from 65.9% to 72.1% on RoboCasa365, average maximum task progress from 20.83% to 42.22% on RoboCasa-Long, and real-world success from 6.66% to 43.33%. MOST also outperforms a matched visual-history memory variant, showing that effective long-horizon memory depends not only on how much experience is retained, but on whether it preserves decision-relevant progress and world-state changes.

papers.title: On the complexity of isomorphism problems for tensors, groups, and polynomials V: over commutative rings
papers.abstract: Tensors over commutative rings naturally appear in number theory, geometry, and group theory. For example, $2\times 2\times 2$ tensors over $\mathbb{Z}$ form the starting point of Bhargava's celebrated works generalising Gauss's composition law (Bhargava, Ann. Math., 2004). Symmetric tensors over $\mathbb{Z}$ are central to the classification of Calabi--Yau threefolds (Yau, Commun. Pure Appl. Math., 1978; Wall, Invent. Math., 1966), geometric objects of significance in string theory. Additionally, tensors over finite commutative rings closely correspond to finite nilpotent groups of class 2 (Baer, Trans. Am. Math. Soc., 1938). In this work, we study isomorphism testing of tensors over commutative rings from a complexity-theoretic viewpoint, and its applications. Some of our main results are: 1. Let $\mathrm{R}$ be a commutative ring. We introduce two complexity classes: $\mathsf{3TI}_\mathrm{R}$ consisting of problems that are polynomial-time reducible to isomorphism problems of tensor products of three modules over $\mathrm{R}$, and $\mathsf{3FTI}_\mathrm{R}$ consisting of problems that are polynomial-time reducible to isomorphism problems of tensor products of three free modules over $\mathrm{R}$. 2. We show that some classical problems considered by Grunewald and Segal (ibid.), and the problem of classifying Calabi--Yau threefolds, are $\mathsf{3FTI}_\mathbb{Z}$-complete. We also show that many natural problems are complete for $\mathsf{3TI}_{\mathbb{Z}/p^e\mathbb{Z}}$. 3. We show that testing isomorphism of tensors in $\mathbb{Z}^2\otimes\mathbb{Z}^2\otimes\mathbb{Z}^2$ is polynomial-time equivalent to the principal ideal problem in algorithmic number theory. 4. We present an $N^{O((\log N)^{8/9})}$-time algorithm for testing isomorphism of finite nilpotent groups of class $2$ and odd order $N$.

papers.title: On the Local Regularity of Homogeneous Complex Monge-Ampère Equations
papers.abstract: We establish a local higher regularity theorem for the homogeneous complex Monge-Ampere equation on $X\times D$, where $X$ is a complete, possibly noncompact Kahler manifold and $D\subset\mathbb C$ is the unit disc. For a bounded weak solution given by the Perron envelope, we prove higher regularity on a smaller spatial domain when the smooth boundary data are locally small. The geometric hypotheses require uniformly convex local Kahler potentials and a local barrier threshold sufficiently large relative to the global $L^\infty$ bound of the solution. We also obtain quantitative local Holder estimates. The proof combines a perturbative construction of local holomorphic disc foliations with a construction of global subsolutions using convexity and barriers. A key analytic difficulty is the loss of Holder regularity in the construction of holomorphic disc families, which we address using BMO estimates and Nash-Moser-Zehnder theorems. Comparison along the discs identifies the local smooth solution by holomorphic discs foliation with the global weak solution. We apply the theorem and its proof to compact Kahler manifolds and to ALE, ALF, and asymptotically complex hyperbolic (ACH) ends. Under the stated geometric and decay assumptions, we obtain higher regularity of each prescribed order sufficiently far out, together with weighted Holder estimates preserving the boundary decay.

papers.title: Can Jev Improve Demonstration Retrieval for In-Context Learning?
papers.abstract: Demonstration selection plays a crucial role in the effectiveness of in-context learning (ICL) for large language models (LLMs). Extensive research has explored various retrieval strategies to identify informative demonstrations and improve downstream performance. Recently, the emergence of Jev, a decision-oriented language model capable of producing probabilistic judgments, offers a new perspective on evaluating demonstration utility. This motivates us to investigate a fundamental question: Can Jev improve demonstration retrieval for in-context learning? In this paper, we demonstrate that Jev can effectively enhance demonstration retrieval by directly assessing the utility of candidate demonstrations for a given query. However, applying Jev to large-scale retrieval introduces substantial computational overhead, as each candidate requires an additional decision-making inference. To address this limitation, we propose a simple yet effective knowledge distillation approach that transfers Jev's utility estimation capability to a lightweight multilayer perceptron (MLP). By learning to approximate Jev's probabilistic judgments, the distilled model enables efficient demonstration ranking while maintaining competitive retrieval performance. Our study highlights the potential of decision-oriented language models for demonstration selection and provides an efficient framework for integrating their decision-making capabilities into ICL.

papers.title: Cross-Evidence Authorization State Learning for Runtime Detection of Broken Object-Level Authorization in Black-Box Web Applications
papers.abstract: Broken object-level authorization (BOLA) remains difficult to detect in black-box Web applications because external runtime monitors generally lack access to source code, authorization policies, and object-ownership records. This paper proposes a cross-evidence authorization-state learning method that reconstructs subject--resource--object--action relations from request--response transactions. The method represents authorization relations with confidence-aware states, aggregates positive and negative evidence while accounting for provenance independence, and applies contamination-gated promotion, evidence quarantine and rollback, expiration, and revocation. A Python prototype is evaluated using a deterministic synthetic benchmark comprising 64,400 requests across five independent random seeds. In this benchmark, the proposed method achieves 100.00% recall, an F1-score of 56.63%, and a false-positive rate of 33.65%, while the measured unauthorized-relation pollution rate is 0.00%.
