This polynomial was introduced by Brenti in 1992. In this paper, we prove Conjecture~6.7 and the $w$-assertion of Conjecture~6.5 posed by Brenti, Royle and Wagner in 1994. The first states that $w(C_n;x)$ has only real zeros for $n\ge 5$. The second assertion states that if $G\cap H$ is complete and both $w(G;x)$ and $w(H;x)$ have only real zeros, then $w(G\cup H;x)$ has only real zeros.

papers.title: Auslander-type grade conditions and subcategories related to syzygy modules
papers.abstract: The question of when a syzygy module or a module satisfying a Serre condition satisfies the cohomological vanishing conditions known as higher torsionfreeness has been extensively studied. In this paper, we address these questions using grade conditions introduced and studied by Auslander-Bridger and Auslander-Reiten. We also investigate homological conditions on Ext modules and, as an application, give a partial answer over commutative rings to a question of Auslander-Bridger concerning whether higher reflexive modules are higher torsionfree.

papers.title: A Clustered Equivalent-Source Method with Local Response Compression and Group-Symmetry Reduction for Antenna-Array Analysis
papers.abstract: Full-wave analysis of finite antenna arrays is computationally demanding because detailed element responses must be resolved and coupled across the entire array. To reduce this cost, this paper presents a clustered equivalent-source method that combines local response compression with group-symmetry reduction. Local responses are represented in compressed equivalent-surface bases or coordinates inherited from child clusters. Symmetry constraints associated with the cluster partition and excitation reduce the coupled system, while the corresponding group transformations recover the complete response in the retained coordinates. To assess overall efficiency, we evaluate the costs of local construction, propagation, global solution, and recovery. Numerical examples involving layered and finite annular patch arrays show close agreement between the computed and reference complex far fields and shorter complete-run times than those of the corresponding symmetry-reduced direct solvers. Among the three equivalent-source implementations for the layered array, the one with the smallest coupled system has the longest runtime because local construction and propagation dominate the cost. These findings highlight the need to consider local construction and coupling costs when assessing the benefit of reducing the global system dimension.

papers.title: Elastic Precision: Software-Hardware Co-Design of a Mixed-Precision Architecture for Long-Context LLM Inference
papers.abstract: Low-bit quantization reduces the data movement and computation costs of large language model (LLM) inference, but uniform widths can waste precision and degrade model quality. Existing mixed-precision methods do not fully account for how the other input of the current GEMM tile affects output error when selecting one input's width. Using both inputs to guide precision introduces additional estimation and selection overheads on conventional hardware. We propose Coffee, a runtime precision allocation architecture for long-context LLM inference. Under a fixed average bit-width budget, Coffee combines statistics from both current input matrices to estimate output errors at candidate widths and select each subarray's two input widths, allocating more bits where they yield greater estimated error reductions. Its mixed-precision hardware supports the selected widths in data access and computation, while overlapping error estimation and width selection with transfers and computation to limit stalls. The same read path supports attention-guided KV reads during decoding, reducing memory traffic. Coffee achieves lower perplexity and higher average zero-shot accuracy than the evaluated quantization baselines, and higher long-context retrieval recall than PLENA. For long-context decoding, system modeling projects up to $2.55\times$ the throughput and $2.61\times$ the energy efficiency of the reconfigured PLENA baseline, and up to $4.96\times$ and $12.56\times$, respectively, compared with the B200 GPU baseline.

papers.title: Distances in the collinearity graphs of geometries related to simplex codes
papers.abstract: Let $\cS(k,q)$ be the point-line geometry whose points and lines correspond to one-dimensional and two-dimensional subcodes of $q$-ary simplex codes of dimension $k$, respectively. We determine the complete distance relation and the diameter of its collinearity graph. For two points whose representing vectors have different sets of zero coordinates there is a common neighbour. If the representing vectors have the same zero set, then a common neighbour exists precisely when $(q-1)q^{k-2}$ of their non-zero coordinate ratios can be selected so that their product is one. To prove this, we use a generalization of Hall's result for finite abelian groups. Applying the Erdős--Ginzburg--Ziv theorem, we establish that the above product condition holds for $k\ge3$, which implies that the diameter is two. If $k=2$, then the diameter is one when $q=2$, two when $q=3$ and three when $q\ge4$.

papers.title: Benchmarking Classical Machine Learning Models for Shading-Fault Detection in Rooftop Photovoltaic Systems Using Real Sensor Data
papers.abstract: Most published comparisons of machine-learning classifiers for photovoltaic (PV) fault detection are validated on simulated faults. We compare seven classical and ensemble-tree classifiers on the Réunion dataset, a 4 kW domestic rooftop plant on which shading faults were physically staged and logged. Readings within a staged episode are near-duplicates, so every train/test split is grouped by episode. A 20,800-row subsample that retains all 17 fault episodes was evaluated with three repeats of five-fold group-aware nested cross-validation, with synthetic minority oversampling (SMOTE) applied inside the training folds. Random Forest and XGBoost gave the highest mean accuracy (0.838 and 0.831) and Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC; 0.526 and 0.522). After Holm correction across the 21 pairwise Wilcoxon tests, only Random Forest's accuracy advantage over k-nearest neighbours and the multi-layer perceptron remained significant. Logistic Regression and the Decision Tree (accuracy 0.820) could be separated neither from the ensembles nor from the weakest models. SMOTE lowered binary MCC for six of the seven classifiers. Errors were concentrated in whole episodes: the Random Forest almost entirely missed four of the 17 fault episodes, including one of two uniform-shading and two of five intermittent-shading episodes. A post-hoc diagnostic shows that the no-fault rows were sampled over a wider range of times of day and output levels than the fault rows. Clock time alone reaches an MCC of 0.44, and PV-side voltage alone 0.72. The reported scores therefore reflect operating-condition differences as well as shading signatures. We release the pipeline and the diagnostics, and identify matched no-fault sampling as the step needed before the classifier ranking can be generalised.

papers.title: Sensitivity of the IceCube atmospheric muon rate to decadal trends in the effective atmospheric temperature
papers.abstract: Decadal changes in the Antarctic stratosphere, generally associated with ozone recovery and shifts in polar circulation, are of broad geophysical interest. However, independent long-term measurements of the atmosphere above the Antarctic interior are scarce. We assess whether the atmospheric muon rate recorded by IceCube could constrain decadal changes in the effective atmospheric temperature, $T_\mathrm{eff}$, a weighted average of temperature through the atmosphere that is most sensitive to the stratosphere. Using public atmospheric reanalysis data and records of cosmic-ray, solar, and geomagnetic variability, we reproduce the measured seasonal response of the IceCube muon rate. We then test whether the same response applies to long-term temperature changes with a different vertical temperature profile. The limiting requirement is detector stability rather than counting statistics: an unmodeled muon rate drift of $1\%\,\mathrm{decade^{-1}}$ would mimic a temperature trend of $2.8\,\mathrm{K\,decade^{-1}}$. The long-term rate must therefore be stable to approximately $0.3\%\,\mathrm{decade^{-1}}$. Within this budget, snow accumulation contributions can be constrained. For a 14-year record, atmospheric variability gives a one-sided 95% CL statistical sensitivity of $1.6\,\mathrm{K\,decade^{-1}}$. Given this sensitivity, the $\sim0.9\,\mathrm{K\,decade^{-1}}$ cooling indicated by the 2011-2025 atmospheric records would become distinguishable after approximately 30 years of measurement.

papers.title: TreePIN$^{2}$: Tree-Prior Initialized Neural Networks
papers.abstract: Fitted decision trees provide predictive knowledge for neural network initialization. We present Tree-Prior Initialized Neural Networks (TreePIN$^{2}$), a method that translates split rules, decision paths and leaf predictions into initial network weights and biases for classification and regression. Sigmoid units encode split responses, hidden units combine them along decision paths, and leaf predictions initialize the output layer. We calibrate split softness using local training margins, sample support and impurity reduction, relating the initial responses to the data at each node. All weights and biases remain trainable, allowing gradient-based optimization to refine the transferred decisions and their combinations. Across six classification and six regression tasks with twenty paired seeds, TreePIN$^{2}$ improves mean initial and early validation performance over initialization baselines on most tasks. After fifty epochs, it achieves the best or tied-best mean validation performance among the six compared methods on ten tasks. Paired ablations show how split calibration and leaf-informed output initialization contribute to the starting predictor and its subsequent learning.

papers.title: What matters in classical machine learning for non-intrusive load monitoring? A factorial benchmark on REFIT with validation on unseen houses
papers.abstract: Published classical machine-learning results for appliance ON/OFF classification in nonintrusive load monitoring (NILM) range from F1-type scores of 0.53 to 0.98, and the sources of this spread have not been separated. This study separates them with a factorial benchmark on REFIT: seven models, two feature sets and four class-imbalance strategies for five appliances (270 fitted configurations), each evaluated by pooled nested cross-validation and on houses unseen during training, with robustness checks. An analysis of variance shows that the appliance explains 38% of the variance in F1, the feature set 13% and the model only 8%. Engineered rolling-window features raised the mean F1 score by 52% under both protocols. Other conclusions changed on unseen houses: the support-weighted F1 score of the best pooled configurations fell from 0.548 to 0.447, the differences between the models selected by pooled validation were no longer significant, and the benefit of class weighting over no correction rose from 32% to 69%. In a nested comparison, house-grouped selection on the training houses improved F1 on unseen houses for three of five appliances, by up to 0.110, and was within 0.007 for the other two. These findings held across four house partitions and without the solar-affected houses. A same-protocol convolutional network reached a weighted F1 score of 0.50, about 0.05 above the classical models (0.45) and far below the published deep-learning scores of 0.78 to 0.91, which were obtained under a different protocol. The results support low-cost appliance monitoring in buildings and yield a NILM reporting checklist.

papers.title: Solvable dynamics model of in-context learning
papers.abstract: Pretrained Transformer architectures display a surprising in-context learning ability without additional training. How the learning process guides the network to achieve this intriguing capability remains unsolved. In this study, we focus on a single-layer, single-head linear attention model, where empirical risk minimization is defined for learning. Given a finite amount of training examples, we determine the exact solution of network parameter dynamics, which is linked to the training error and generalization error, characterizing how memorization and generalization emerge from learning and how these transitions are related to curvatures of the empirical risk landscape. Furthermore, we calculate a data-dependent free energy, from which the training and generalization errors in the long-time limit of learning dynamics can be well predicted. Our work adds insights toward understanding the mechanism of in-context learning, especially from a learning dynamics perspective.

papers.title: Closed-Form Gaussian Mixture Representations of d-Dimensional Triangulated Domains
papers.abstract: We derive a Gaussian Mixture (GM) representation of a full-dimensional subset of Euclidean space with finite volume from a finite simplicial triangulation in closed form. On each simplex, we replace the uniform probability density function (PDF) with a Gaussian PDF that minimizes the Kullback--Leibler (KL) divergence, arriving at the information projection onto the family of Gaussian PDFs. By exploiting affine isomorphisms between simplices, the joint convexity and bijection invariance properties of the KL divergence, identities for Dirichlet PDFs, and a partition-of-unity argument, we establish a dimension-dependent but geometry-independent sharp upper bound on the global KL divergence between the resulting GM PDF and the uniform PDF on the original domain. Numerical examples illustrate the construction and demonstrate its potential in practical applications.

papers.title: Illusion: Safeguarding Topology Confidentiality in LLM Multi-Agent Systems via Behavior-Preserving Obfuscation
papers.abstract: The communication topology of Large Language Model Multi-Agent Systems (LLM-MASs) governs how information propagates among agents and encodes critical domain knowledge and expert workflow design. It is valuable intellectual property and plays a decisive role in system utility and safety, yet remains vulnerable to inference attacks that stealthily reconstruct it from agent outputs. Existing defenses detect or mitigate such attacks but do not proactively conceal the topology itself. We propose \textit{Illusion}, a proactive topology obfuscation defense for LLM-MAS. \textit{Illusion} injects fake edges and fake messages to present attackers with a deceptive topology, while selecting low-impact candidates that preserve output-distribution equivalence and task-accuracy non-inferiority. The resulting fake edges are designed to be indistinguishable from genuine messages under black-box observation. Extensive experiments show that \textit{Illusion} reduces edge-level F1 from over 0.87 to 0.62 and graph similarity from over 0.94 to 0.71. It also largely preserves output distributions and task performance, and its fake edges resist both similarity-based and LLM-judge filtering, even under adaptive pruning.

papers.title: An exhaustion-aware product moment and zero-free half-planes for Hecke L-functions
papers.abstract: We refine the ordinary product moment in the cubic-theta comparison by allowing a returned prime product to be exhausted. The return stops either when the positive-prime length inequality holds or when the established prime-free ordinary estimate applies. Keeping the extracted central coefficients gives a local normalization inequality on a larger domain. On the critical ordinary-length interval this yields a net first-mean gain of $1/20000$. We prove the complementary-class, short-sum and algebraic comparison inequalities directly, and obtain the endpoint $B_*-1/160000=0.87446205769353\ldots$, where $B_*$ is Liu's algebraic boundary. The zero-free conclusion is conditional on the cited general-field theta, detector, prior-bound and Mellin input theorems in their stated uniform forms. The proof includes the actual return weights, both approximate-functional-equation arms, the principal-residue normalization and descent to arbitrary number fields.

papers.title: A density theorem for non-standard irreducible cyclic codes
papers.abstract: We prove a fixed-characteristic density form of the Berger-Charpin conjecture for non-degenerate irreducible cyclic codes: for each prime $p$, the lengths admitting such a non-standard code over some finite field of characteristic $p$ have natural density zero. Thus, for almost every length coprime to $p$, every such code over every finite field of characteristic $p$ has only the permutation automorphisms generated by the cyclic shift and the Frobenius map. The proof uses the Feng--Hollmann--Li--Xiang classification for non-standard irreducible cyclic codes, a normal form for the deriving constructions in that paper, and a theorem by Wiertelak on multiplicative orders, in the form recalled by Moree.

papers.title: UI-UG 2: Advancing Mobile UI Understanding and Generation with Fine-Grained Supervision and Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Mobile UI understanding and generation require both fine-grained component perception and reliable structured synthesis. Inspired by the unified direction introduced by UI-UG, we present UI-UG 2, a compact 4B-parameter multimodal large language model (MLLM) that advances mobile UI Understanding and Generation with broader task coverage, a front-end-aligned taxonomy, and online render-aware reinforcement learning. UI-UG 2 constructs a multi-source understanding corpus from RICO, VINS, Android in the Wild, and Android Control, annotated with an 80-category two-level UI taxonomy aligned with front-end component semantics, and pairs it with over 5,000 requirement-screenshot-JSON tuples for progressive structured UI generation through a domain-specific language (DSL). For understanding, UI-UG 2 introduces decomposed rewards for category prediction, OCR fidelity, color recognition, dense grounding, and GUI grounding. Unlike the offline Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)-style generation optimization in UI-UG, UI-UG 2 optimizes generation through end-to-end online Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO): sampled DSL outputs are rendered with a Playwright-based server-side pipeline and evaluated using LLM-as-a-Judge and contrastive preference ranking. Experiments show that UI-UG 2 achieves the strongest referring and dense-grounding results among the evaluated models on our 80-category benchmark, and achieves the best composite generation score among compared models at a compact scale (4B). More importantly, we observe a consistent understanding-to-generation transfer: adding fine-grained UI perception supervision improves generation quality under a fixed training budget, suggesting that component-level semantics provide a shared representational foundation for both tasks.

papers.title: Latin cubes of order $4$ and $4320$-point quaternionic constructions in ${\mathbb R}^{16}$
papers.abstract: Possibly the most enduring lower-bound record for kissing numbers in dimensions greater than $8$ (excluding $24$) is $$ κ_{16}\geq 4320. $$ This lower bound is attained by a shell of the famous Barnes--Wall lattice, which was discovered in 1959. Besides this configuration, at least one alternative $4320$-point kissing arrangement is currently known. Recently, it was noticed that all these configurations can be described in terms of the so-called quaternionic construction, a general type of construction that was instrumental in explaining the geometry of the $841$-point kissing arrangement in ${\mathbb R}^{12}$. We give a simple generalization of quaternionic constructions in ${\mathbb R}^{16}$ obtained from record configurations. They are parameterized by three Latin cubes of order $4$, six permutations of $3$-element set, and are all infinitesimally jammed. Computer-aided counting shows that there are $4\,072\,728\,621$ isometry classes in this family of $4320$-point kissing arrangements.

papers.title: Efficient Interpolation of the Bethe-Salpeter Hamiltonian at Arbitrary Momenta
papers.abstract: We develop an efficient reciprocal-space method to reconstruct the static Bethe-Salpeter (BSE) Hamiltonian at arbitrary crystal momenta from coarse first-principles grids. Bloch states are interpolated within an optimally smooth Wannier subspace, while the screened Coulomb interaction is reconstructed from the dielectric response. This decouples the electron-hole transition momenta and transferred momentum from the underlying ab initio sampling. We benchmark the method on monolayer hBN, monolayer MoS$_2$, and bulk GaAs against explicit ab initio calculations, finding excellent agreement for dense-grid Bloch states, dielectric screening, and BSE optical spectra. Furthermore, our cost analysis estimates speedups of up to $22\times$ on the grids considered here. Arbitrary transferred-momentum sampling gives direct access to the long-wavelength exciton dispersion: in hBN and MoS$_2$, we resolve the nonanalytic behaviour induced by long-range electron-hole exchange at momenta well below the spacing of practical uniform grids. For bulk GaAs, locally refined transition-momentum sampling yields a converged binding energy for the threefold-degenerate lowest exciton, in close agreement with experiment and reference calculations, using far fewer BSE points than conventional uniform meshes. As the present framework provides exciton energies and amplitudes at arbitrary crystal momenta, it opens the way to incorporating ab initio excitonic effects into nonlocal electron-phonon vertices and to extensions towards exciton-phonon interactions and nonequilibrium exciton dynamics.

papers.title: Deformed Q-learning for High-Dimensional Dynamic Treatment Regimes
papers.abstract: In high-dimensional dynamic treatment regimes, nonlinear terminal outcome models complicate upstream conditional-mean modeling and inference based on recursively estimated continuation values. We introduce a Deformed Q-learning procedure for general action spaces that accommodates a terminal-stage GLM, random designs, conditional heteroscedasticity, and fine-grained action discretization. The procedure changes the recursive criterion by propagating the terminal deformed optimal Q-function through sparse block-wise linear conditional-mean models. Under the stated models and regularity conditions, we establish consistent and asymptotically normal estimators, accounting for downstream estimation uncertainty in inference for optimal Q-values, deformed optimal Q-values, and their contrasts. We bound population regret relative to the original terminal mean-outcome objective without explicit stage-wise accumulation. Estimation and inference also extend to a growing number of stages under conditions uniform across stages. Simulation studies demonstrate accurate estimation and variable selection. In an empirical application to sepsis management using the MIMIC-III database, the proposed framework supports stage-specific value inference, while an auxiliary action-alignment analysis provides an exploratory signal that early-stage concordance with the learned recommendation may be associated with improved survival.

papers.title: From Kination to Detection: Scotogenic Scalar Dark Matter
papers.abstract: We investigate scalar dark matter in the scotogenic model during an early kination-dominated epoch. The enhanced expansion rate causes earlier freeze-out and increases the relic abundance, opening viable dark matter masses from approximately $200~\mathrm{GeV}$ to $1~\mathrm{TeV}$ while reducing the need for co-annihilation with a nearly degenerate singlet fermion. Current indirect searches strongly constrain the $(100-200)~\mathrm{GeV}$ region, whereas much of the surviving parameter space can be probed by CTA and next-generation direct detection experiments. The viable spectra also lead to complementary collider signatures, including missing transverse energy, displaced leptons, and disappearing charged tracks, providing promising tests at the HL-LHC and future lepton colliders.

papers.title: Binary Quantum Hypothesis Testing with a Rejection Option: The Exact Error-Exponent Trade-off
papers.abstract: We characterize the exact error-exponent trade-off in binary quantum hypothesis testing with a rejection option for faithful states on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space. The probabilities of rejection under the two hypotheses are required to vanish exponentially, with exponents at least $K$ and $L$. We show that a quadruple $(a,b,K,L)$ of positive error and rejection exponents is achievable if and only if it satisfies three single-letter conditions: two conditions involve Petz--Rényi quantities and coincide with the converse bound conjectured to be tight by Ji and Regula; the third involves the $α$--$z$ Rényi quantities on the triangle $\max\{α,1-α\}\le z\le1$. The proof combines a sector decomposition inside Schur--Weyl blocks, an explicit one-shot measurement construction, and an exact minimax argument.

papers.title: A dual approach to $L^p$ estimates for orthogonal martingales satisfying the differential subordination
papers.abstract: We develop a new dual approach, which can be used to establish sharp $L^p$ bounds for orthogonal differentially subordinate martingales. The method rests on the construction of a certain special function enjoying appropriate majorization properties and a novel differential condition.

papers.title: A new perspective on Riemann surfaces and von Neumann algebras via thin Blaschke products
papers.abstract: In 2014, K.Guo and the second author constructed the first example of an infinite Blaschke product $B$ (a thin Blaschke product), for which the associated multiplication operator $M_B$ is irreducible on the Bergman space $L_a^2(\mathbb{D})$ over the unit disk $\mathbb D$. We take a substantial step forward toward characterizing the irreducibility of the operator $M_B$ on $L_a^2(\mathbb{D})$, or equivalently, the trivialness of the von Neumann algebra $\{M_B,M_B^*\}'$. This characterization indicates a close connection with the primeness of $B$ and with the two-component property of the Riemann surface $\mathcal{S}_B$ associated with $B$. The approach is built upon a nested family of connected components of the sublevel set $\{z\in \mathbb{D}:|B(z)|<t\}$ for $0<t<1$, which captures the function-theoretic and geometric feature of $B$.

papers.title: Single-Mode Squeezing Using Degenerate Four-Wave Mixing in a Dual-Pump TWPA
papers.abstract: Single-mode squeezing of the electromagnetic vacuum is a key resource for mode-selective noise reduction in quantum measurements. At microwave frequencies, single-mode squeezing is typically obtained by using Josephson and Traveling-Wave Parametric Amplifiers designed for three-wave mixing operation. In single-pump degenerate four-wave mixing, the coincidence of pump, signal, and idler frequencies complicates separation of the squeezed field from the strong pump. A dual-pump configuration enables degenerate operation while keeping both pumps spectrally separated from the squeezed mode. Here, we demonstrate single-mode squeezing in a flux-tunable, dual-pump Traveling-Wave Parametric Amplifier, employing reversed-Kerr phase matching. By independently calibrating the single-pump gains, we find that the strongest squeezing occurs along approximately balanced-gain trajectories, while the optimal squeezing does not necessarily correspond to the highest dual-pump gain. At flux biases $Φ_\mathrm{ext}/Φ_0 = 0.0$ and $0.5$, the minimum quadrature noise levels reach $-2.48 \pm 0.18~\mathrm{dB}$ and $-1.62 \pm 0.20~\mathrm{dB}$ relative to vacuum, respectively. These results establish the proposed architecture as a platform for single-mode squeezing in microwave continuous-variable quantum technologies.

papers.title: Grid triples, link cobordisms in $\CPbar$ and the computation of Heegaard-Floer TQFT
papers.abstract: We give a combinatorial description of the Heegaard--Floer link-cobordism maps associated with pointed triple grid diagrams in the complement of three $4$-balls in complex projective plane with reverse orientation. Every contributing index-zero holomorphic triangle decomposes into Euclidean triangular sheets. We characterize the compatible collections of sheets that contribute by an explicit geometric separation criterion, expressed as a lattice-point test, and prove that each has mod-\(2\) count one. Individual sheets may wrap around the torus in the unblocked theory, whereas they are embedded in the blocked theory. In each fixed \(\SpinC\) structure, the map is determined by a finite enumeration. A difference number computed from the triangular regions determines the \(\SpinC\) structure of a Whitney triangle. Together with the topology of the associated surface, this gives an explicit formula for the absolute bigrading of each summand of the cobordism map. After basepoint reduction, the formula determines the Laurent monomial representing any nonzero map on the rank-one torsion-free two-variable knot Floer modules, yielding vanishing and ideal-containment criteria. We apply the construction to an affine family of grid links \(K(n;p,s)\), obtaining explicit cobordisms involving infinite families of torus knots and links, together with closed formulas for the bigradings of their distinguished grid states.

papers.title: Labadain-MedQA: A Tetun Medical QA Dataset for Fine-Tuning and Evaluating Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Advances in large language models (LLMs) have created opportunities for cross-lingual transfer of medical knowledge from high-resource to low-resource languages to support access to healthcare information. However, medical question-answering (QA) datasets for fine-tuning and evaluating LLMs remain scarce for Tetun. To address this gap, we translated MedAlpaca's Medical Flashcards and WikiDoc Patient Information collections into Tetun using Gemini 2.5 Flash, producing 39,077 medical QA pairs. Translation quality was assessed on 50 randomly sampled QA pairs (100 documents) using automatic metrics against human reference translations and evaluations by two native Tetun-speaking healthcare professionals, focusing on medical accuracy and Tetun fluency. Human translations achieved higher mean ratings than LLM-generated translations for both criteria (4.43/5 vs. 4.02/5), with statistically significant differences (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p < 0.001). To assess downstream utility, we fine-tuned Gemma and Llama variants on the translated MedAlpaca dataset using parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) and evaluated them on 325 Tetun-translated United States Medical Licensing Examination multiple-choice questions. Gemma 4 12B fine-tuned using QLoRA achieved relative improvements in mean accuracy of 10.79% with 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4) inference and 10.42% after merging the LoRA adapters into the BF16 base model, compared with the corresponding base models. These results highlight the viability of automatic dataset translation for Tetun medical QA and the effectiveness of PEFT in enhancing model performance. The datasets, models, and evaluation resources are accessible at https://github.com/labadain/labadain-medqa to support reproducible research on Tetun medical QA and facilitate machine translation, cross lingual, and multilingual research.

papers.title: Cometary dust activity as a proxy for refractory organic material release
papers.abstract: Cometary dust is an important reservoir of refractory organic matter and may contribute to the redistribution of carbon-rich material throughout planetary systems. We investigate whether the widely used dust-activity parameter $Afρ$ can serve as a first-order observational proxy for the release of refractory organic material. A sample of 27 active small bodies representing active asteroids, main-belt comets, quasi-Hilda comets, quasi-Trojan objects, Jupiter-family comets, Centaurs, and long-period comets was compiled from published photometric studies. Representative near-perihelion, phase-corrected $A(0)fρ$ values span more than three orders of magnitude, from a few centimetres for weakly active asteroids and main-belt comets to $\sim 10^4$ cm for the most active long-period comets. The large dispersion within individual dynamical classes shows that orbital classification alone does not determine the level of dust activity. Direct compositional measurements of cometary dust, including the high refractory-organic fraction measured for 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko, support the interpretation of dust activity as an indirect indicator of potential organic-material release. However, a universal conversion of $Afρ$ into dust mass-loss rate is not possible because of uncertainties in grain-size distribution, density, porosity, velocity, and optical properties. We therefore suggest that $Afρ$ may be used as a comparative, first-order proxy for refractory-organic material release.

papers.title: What Helps Denoising Can Hurt Memory: Rethinking History in Long Video Generation
papers.abstract: Autoregressive video generators produce long videos block by block, using historical context to maintain temporal consistency. After denoising, a committing pass encodes each clean block into keys and values (KV) that later blocks read, and the same clean block can be encoded into different KV depending on the history it reads. We therefore study historical context not only as a condition for denoising but also as an input to committing. Older historical context that supports denoising can harm subsequent generation when read during committing. At fixed context size and temporal positions, older historical context lowers mean clip-to-clip Subject Consistency. Across 5 generator configurations supporting longer contexts, consistency rises, plateaus, and then declines as committing context expands. Motivated by these findings, we propose Commit Forcing, a training-free rule that organizes committing into a chain. During committing, each block reads only the preceding block's stored KV, so older historical context reaches new entries only through the chain. We apply this rule to 6 pretrained generators. On 60-second VBench, Commit Forcing improves Quality and Total on all 6 generators, by up to 1.27 Quality points and 1.10 Total points. Long-range consistency gains extend to 240-second videos. In a blinded comparison on 120-second LongLive videos, Commit Forcing achieves win rates of 83.5% for subject and scene consistency and 82.9% for overall preference against the base generator, excluding ties.

papers.title: A Bayesian Magnitude-Composition Model for Tree-Size Distributions and Stand-Tables
papers.abstract: Sparse forest inventories often provide too few plots to estimate species-specific tree-size distributions for individual stands. We develop a general Bayesian magnitude-composition model that separates overall abundance from its allocation among categories. A negative-binomial model describes total counts, while multinomial models describe how those counts are allocated among categories. In forest inventory, this construction allocates trees among species and then size classes within species, without imposing a parametric form on the tree-size distribution. Covariates inform both abundance and composition. Shared latent factors represent residual spatial and group-level dependence among categories using relatively few processes, while smoothing priors on regression coefficients borrow information across neighboring size classes. Nearest-neighbor Gaussian processes support efficient spatial computation. Joint posterior prediction and area-weighted aggregation yield stand-tables---tree densities by species and size class---and derived measures such as size-class diversity, with associated uncertainty. Simulations show small estimation errors and near-nominal predictive-interval coverage for forest and stand summaries. An application combining field plots and light detection and ranging (LiDAR) covariates illustrates estimation of species-specific distributions of diameter at breast height and size-class diversity in sampled and unsampled stands.

papers.title: Reformulation and Equivalence of Bock's Algorithm for Exact Dependency Parsing
papers.abstract: Bock's algorithm provides a matrix-based alternative to Chu--Liu/Edmonds (CL/E) for exact dependency parsing. We present a reformulation that retains original node and arc identities through component labels, column adjustments, and star-and-bar transfers. In exact arithmetic, we prove operational equivalence to original Bock under matching scan and tie rules, and establish correspondence with corrected Tarjan under a prescribed component schedule. A separate analysis establishes optimal-value equivalence with Dozat-derived CL/E under the stated score and single-root conventions. We integrate reformulated Bock into a biaffine dependency parser and evaluate decoding and structured training on the Penn Treebank and Chinese Treebank. These results establish Bock as an alternative exact oracle for dependency parsing and structured training, while distinguishing equality of optimal values from identity of returned trees and training trajectories.

papers.title: An all-weather microwave-based AI retrieval of pan-Arctic melt pond fraction
papers.abstract: Melt pond fraction (MPF) is a key variable governing Arctic sea ice albedo and seasonal sea ice predictability, yet existing pan-Arctic MPF products rely almost exclusively on optical sensors, limiting availability under cloud cover and seasonal darkness. This study presents PRISM-MPF, the first pan-Arctic, multi-year, all-weather MPF dataset, derived from PRISM (Polar Retrievals through Intelligent Sensor Merging), a machine learning framework fusing multi-source microwave observations with auxiliary thermal and spatiotemporal information to complement optical products. An XGBoost model was trained on eight melt seasons (2017-2025, excluding 2019) using Sentinel-1 C-band SAR backscatter, AMSR2 brightness temperatures and sea ice concentration, NOAA OISST sea surface temperature, and spatiotemporal descriptors (date and grid position). Three experiments assessed baseline skill and feature importance, independent sensor-group contributions (including CryoSat-2 radar freeboard), and regional specialisation, all under Leave-One-Year-Out (LOYO) cross-validation on unseen melt seasons. The baseline retrieval achieved a per-season mean R2=0.468 and RMSE=0.080 (pooled over 1,066,808 pixels: R2=0.532, RMSE=0.077), comparable to prior regional microwave-based studies, now at pan-Arctic, multi-year scale. Removing spatiotemporal features or C-band SAR reduced skill comparably (Delta R2=+0.089 and +0.085), whereas physical sensors alone outperformed spatiotemporal features alone (R2=0.375 vs 0.261), showing the two groups are complementary. Regional specialisation offered no advantage over a single pan-Arctic retrieval. This framework establishes a reproducible foundation for all-weather Arctic MPF monitoring, extensible to new sensors, longer records, and reference products.

papers.title: MarkovTS: Pretrained State-Transition Representations for Zero-Shot Time Series Generation
papers.abstract: Across heterogeneous real-world domains, time-series generation supports simulation, model development, and data augmentation by generating sequences that preserve target-domain statistics and temporal dependencies when real observations are scarce or costly. However, existing methods predominantly address in-domain generation, limiting their reuse in unseen domains. We study reference-conditioned zero-shot time series generation: target domains are unseen during pretraining, generation uses a single target-domain reference sequence, and no model parameters are updated. MarkovTS characterizes sequence evolution through local morphologies and their ordered transitions at multiple temporal scales. Its pretrained encoder quantizes normalized time-series patches into multiscale morphological states with a state codebook, while a transition codebook encodes contextual transitions between adjacent intervals. These transferable state-transition representations condition a pretrained flow-matching model. At generation, the frozen model combines a reference-derived condition with independent Gaussian noise to produce stochastic samples that retain the reference's temporal organization. Across 12 unseen target datasets, MarkovTS outperforms strong baselines in most distributional comparisons and generates diverse, reference-consistent sequences. As downstream augmentation, its samples yield overall gains across forecasting, classification, and anomaly detection benchmarks and diverse model families. Our code is available at https://github.com/blisky-li/MarkovTS.

papers.title: EPIC: Differentiable Energy-Force Consistent Uncertainty Quantification and Propagation for Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
papers.abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) now rival density functional theory in accuracy and are increasingly used to screen vast crystal databases, yet they can produce unreliable predictions for chemistries outside their training distribution without clear warning. Existing force-level evidential approaches do not inherently define a corresponding uncertainty model over the potential energy surface, limiting the consistent propagation of uncertainty to energy-derived observables. Here we introduce Energy-Propagated Intrinsic Confidence (EPIC), a general energy-centered evidential framework that derives forces as exact gradients of the predicted mean energy, ensuring conservative force fields while providing an analytical estimate of energy uncertainty. Coupled to a MACE backbone trained on the Materials Project trajectory dataset, EPIC propagates uncertainty diagnostics to equations of state, anisotropic structural uncertainty ellipsoids, and phonon dispersions through a Monte Carlo procedure. Applied to 10,966 candidate crystals, the fraction classified as robustly dynamically stable increases from 11\% in the highest-uncertainty quartile to 53\% in the lowest-uncertainty quartile. Furthermore, element-resolved analysis reveals a pronounced chemistry dependence in the relationship between epistemic uncertainty and predicted dynamical stability, highlighting potential limitations in the description of complex bonding environments. EPIC thus provides a physics-aware, chemistry-sensitive uncertainty diagnostic for high-throughput screening and autonomous materials discovery.

papers.title: The Exact Central-Index Profile of Groups with Bounded Noncommutativity
papers.abstract: For a finite group $G$, let $ω(G)$ be the largest size of a pairwise noncommuting set and put $z(G)=[G:\mathrm Z(G)]$. We determine the maximum possible central index under $ω(G)\le k$ for every integer $k\ge1$, giving an exact answer to Neumann's central-index question and sharpening Pyber's exponential upper bound. The maximum is $1$ for $k=1,2$, $(k-1)^2$ for $3\le k\le6$, $81$ for $k=7,8$, and $4^{\lfloor(k-1)/2\rfloor}$ for $k\ge9$. In the last range, with $r=\lfloor(k-1)/2\rfloor$, equality holds exactly when $G'\cong C_2$ and $G/\mathrm Z(G)\cong\mathbb F_2^{2r}$. We also obtain the sharp universal bound $z(G)\le(81/64)2^{ω(G)-1}$. All maximizers are classified up to isoclinism. The results extend to arbitrary groups with finite clique number through finite isoclinic representatives.

papers.title: SNAPPerf: Software-Aware Tabular Foundation Model for Retraining-Free Performance Prediction of Configurable Systems
papers.abstract: Modern software systems expose hundreds of configuration options whose combinations can substantially affect execution time, memory and energy usage. Measuring software performance resulting from a configuration set requires running a realistic workload. Since the configuration space grows exponentially, exhaustive benchmarking is infeasible. Prior work therefore trains models on a small set of measured configurations to predict the performance of the rest. Yet these models are specific to a particular software version, hardware platform, and workload, so changes require new measurements and retraining, and such changes are becoming more frequent with coding agents. We challenge this per-system training assumption with SNAPPERF (Software-aware, No-retraining, Adaptive Prediction), a sample-efficient tabular foundation model specialized for configurable software. SNAPPERF is pretrained once on synthetic data. Each new update only requires a few measured configurations as context to predict the rest without any per-system training or hyperparameter tuning. Across 39,866 configurations from 12 real-world systems, spanning 6 domains and 4 performance metrics, SNAPPERF reduces prediction error by 38% over the prior state of the art at the same measurement budget, and by 25% over the best general-purpose tabular foundation model. It matches the state of the art's accuracy with 54% fewer measurements on average. These results suggest that knowledge about software can be encoded in pretraining data rather than in per-system models, opening a new research direction in software-aware pretraining.

papers.title: HieraNTP: Structured Risk Representations for Time-Series Anomaly Detection via Hierarchical Next-Token Prediction
papers.abstract: Time-series anomaly detection commonly converts deviations from learned temporal regularities into anomaly scores. This practice can conflate violations of temporal regularity with task-specific anomaly judgments: the same deviation may be anomalous under one task definition and benign under another. Aggregating heterogeneous deviations into a single score before task-specific adaptation can obscure the evidence needed to distinguish these cases. We introduce HieraNTP, a Hierarchical Next-Token Prediction framework that separates self-supervised predictive modeling from task-specific risk interpretation. HieraNTP pretrains a hierarchical tokenizer and a causal next-token predictor to capture temporal regularities at multiple scales. It then organizes prediction discrepancies into a structured risk representation, preserving complementary evidence across temporal scales in token, local-statistic, and observation spaces. A task-adaptive detector uses anomaly labels to select and combine this evidence for the target task. Across anomaly detection benchmarks, HieraNTP improves VUS-PR by 12.0% on TSB-AD-U and 15.5% on TSB-AD-M relative to the strongest baselines, and achieves the highest composite score on both TAB tracks, with controlled comparisons supporting the value of retaining distinct evidence. Our code is available at https://github.com/blisky-li/HieraNTP.

papers.title: Explicit Boundary-Entropy Deficits in the XX Spin Chain with arbitrary boundary fields
papers.abstract: The exact thermodynamics of the XX spin-1/2 chain with arbitrary Hermitian boundary fields is constructed via fusion techniques. The rigorous result shows that (1) each end with a nonzero transverse field contributes $+\frac12T\ln2$ to the low-temperature free energy, whereas strictly diagonal and free ends contribute no such linear term; (2) each nondiagonal end has a characteristic temperature $T_B$, which scales as $T_B\propto h_\perp^2/J$ in the weak-field regime. For $T\ll\min\{J,T_B\}$, the boundary entropy approaches a deficit of $\frac12\ln2$ relative to a diagonal end. As the transverse field tends to zero, the boundary crossover scale vanishes and the low-temperature expansion becomes nonuniform. The present result provides a clear benchmark not only for the boundary thermodynamics of open boundary quantum integrable systems, but also for dot defects in quantum critical systems.

papers.title: Bootstrap Inference for Riemannian Optimization Problems
papers.abstract: We develop an online multiplier bootstrap for manifold-valued parameters estimated by averaging the iterates of Riemannian stochastic approximation. The method runs weighted iterations alongside the original algorithm, with each path using the same observations while updating its own state and intrinsic average. The weighted averages provide uncertainty assessments without a plug-in asymptotic covariance estimator. Under local stability and regularity conditions, we establish bootstrap consistency and show that a fixed number of paths suffices for asymptotically valid Student intervals and intrinsic confidence regions. The theory accommodates samplewise nonsmooth scores and identifies a critical oracle-bias regime in which the estimator's limiting distribution shifts, but the centered bootstrap distribution does not. Applications include spherical means, positive-definite matrix means and medians, and principal-subspace estimation. Simulations show coverage close to nominal in regular settings, and an analysis of North Atlantic storm locations illustrates descriptive online inference for a spherical center.

papers.title: Heavy Quarkonium Physics: An Experimental Review at Tevatron, LHC, and e+e- Colliders
papers.abstract: We review recent experimental advances in heavy quarkonium physics at the Tevatron, e+e- colliders (Belle, BaBar, Belle II, BESIII, and LEP), and the LHC (ALICE, ATLAS, CMS, and LHCb), including Run 2 and early Run 3 results. Differential cross sections and polarization measurements of charmonium (Jpsi, Psi(2S)) and bottomonium (Upsilon(nS)) test perturbative and non-perturbative QCD within the Non-Relativistic QCD (NRQCD) framework and probe symmetry relations among spin and orbital configurations. CDF and D0 established production baselines and exposed polarization tensions with early NRQCD predictions. Complementary e+e- measurements provide precise spectroscopy, branching fractions, radiative and hadronic transitions, and observations of exotic quarkonium-like states, constraining non-perturbative dynamics. LHC measurements extend production and polarization studies across broad kinematic ranges. Spectroscopic advances include fully-heavy tetraquark candidates, exotic structures in Jpsi Jpsi and Jpsi Psi(2S) reported by LHCb, and studies of toponium (ttbar) quasi-bound states. Sequential bottomonium suppression in PbPb collisions probes the quark-gluon plasma, while pPb measurements constrain cold nuclear matter effects. Multi-quarkonium production explores multi-parton interactions and exotic-hadron structure. Together, these results establish heavy quarkonium as a laboratory for QCD and a probe for physics beyond the Standard Model, while highlighting unresolved theoretical challenges. Future programs at the LHC, Belle II, and BESIII promise greater precision and new discoveries.

papers.title: Riemannian Newton Methods with Statistical Inference
papers.abstract: We develop online statistical inference for Polyak-Ruppert averages of inexact Newton iterates on Riemannian manifolds. A local asymptotic representation separates observation noise, solver randomization, and accumulated implementation bias, and yields one-pass covariance estimators and asymptotically valid Wald regions under local regularity and centering conditions. Independent fresh solves add a positive semidefinite term to the score-sandwich covariance; averaging solver replicas reduces this term in inverse proportion to their number. Slowly varying predictable gains instead cancel from the first order law. Product torus simulations show how Newton scaling shortens an ill-conditioned transient and how retaining solver variation restores coverage. Intrinsic means and principal subspaces provide geometric applications, with a streaming data illustration.

papers.title: The size and structure of graphs with a unique $k$-factor
papers.abstract: For integers $n>k\ge1$ with $nk$ even, let $m(n,k)$ be the maximum size of a graph of order $n$ with a unique $k$-factor. In 1964, Hetyei and in 1984, Hendry [\emph{J. Combin. Theory Ser. B} \textbf{37} (1984), 53--63] proved $m(n,1)=n^2/4$ for even $n$ and $m(n,2)=\lfloor n(n+1)/4\rfloor$, respectively. In 2000, Johann [\emph{J. Graph Theory} \textbf{35} (2000), 227--243] showed that $m(n,k)=nk/2+\binom{n-k}{2}$ for $k>n/2$ and $kn$ even and $m(n,k)=n^2/4+(k-1)n/4$ for $n=2kq$, where $q$ is a positive integer. Later, Volkmann [\emph{Combinatorica} \textbf{24} (2004), 531--540] proved $m(n,k)=k^2+\binom{n-k}{2}$ for $n/3\le k<n/2$ and $kn$ even, and he determined $m(n,3)$. In this paper, we determine $m(n,k)$ for all admissible pairs, proving the size conjecture posed by Volkmann. We also prove that every extremal graph with $2\le k\le n-2$ has a universal vertex whose neighbors in the unique factor are precisely its degree-$k$ vertices. In particular, this result confirms Volkmann's structural conjecture.

papers.title: Why Koopman Structure Does Not Help Differentiable World Models for Humanoid Whole-Body Tracking
papers.abstract: We test whether Koopman structure, linear dynamics in a lifted state space, helps when a humanoid whole-body tracking policy is trained by backpropagating through a differentiable world model, replacing the MLP world model of an otherwise unchanged pipeline for simulated Unitree G1 tracking. It does not: return is at best equal (0.823 versus 0.830), one-step error on identical data is 1.3 to 1.6 times the MLP's, and training is about 15% slower. Lifted rollouts diverge or fail to train a policy; of the schemes tested, re-lifting at every imagined step trains best. Re-lifting never uses the lifted linear dynamics and leaves a model affine in the action, with state-dependent offset and slope; an action-affine MLP also predicts worse, so the cost belongs to this class. At a fixed state, the curvature of the true dynamics in the action explains only part of it. Across states, the policy's actions span a curved region, so an affine model fits policy data only as the tangent at the policy's action, the operating point: on G1, the MLP's tangent there is as accurate as the MLP; at the mean action, 31 times worse. The offset must encode, from the state alone, where the policy acts, whereas an MLP reads the action. Supplying the policy's action removes most of the remaining gap on G1, Ant and Humanoid. The only online repair approaching the MLP feeds the action into the nonlinear lift, giving up the structure. The MLP world model thus remains the better choice here.

papers.title: Gravitational form factors of heavy quarkonia and their nonrelativistic expansion in a self-consistent light-front quark model
papers.abstract: We investigate the gravitational form factors of the pseudoscalar heavy quarkonia $η_c(1S,2S)$ and $η_b(1S,2S)$ in a light-front quark model with physical radial wave functions represented by orthogonal mixtures of the two lowest harmonic-oscillator basis states $φ_{1S}$ and $φ_{2S}$. The Bakamjian--Thomas prescription is applied consistently to constituent matrix elements and Lorentz prefactors at the integrand level. Working in the $Δ^+=0$ frame with $Δ=P'-P$ and $t=Δ^2$, we extract $A_q(t)$ from the quark energy--momentum tensor components $T_q^{++}$, $T_q^{+i}$, and $T_q^{ij}$, and $D_q(t)$ from $T_q^{+-}$, $T_q^{-i}$, and $T_q^{ii}$ using appropriate momentum-transfer projections. The independent extractions agree in the full relativistic calculation and in the analytic nonrelativistic expansions through $ O(v^2)$, where $v=β/m_Q$, $β$ is the Gaussian width, and $m_Q$ is the constituent mass. At zero momentum transfer, the expansions give $D_q^{φ_{1S}}(0)=-v^2+ O(v^4)$ and $D_q^{φ_{2S}}(0)=-2/3-(13/3)v^2+O(v^4)$. The interference, defined as the sum of the two cross overlaps, first contributes as $D_q^{\mathrm{cross}}(0)=-(4/\sqrt{6})v^2+O(v^4)$. Thus, the pure Gaussian $1S$ contribution is suppressed, whereas a nonzero $2S$ admixture at fixed mixing angle leaves an $O(v^0)$ D-term in the physical ground state. Full numerical results for the mixed states illustrate the effects of heavy-quark flavor and radial structure on mass distributions and internal stresses.

papers.title: PSF-Informed Reconstruction: An Enhanced 2D Directional Filtered Backprojection Method for Cone-Beam Rotary Computed Laminography
papers.abstract: Cone-beam rotary computed laminography (CL) presents a viable alternative to cone-beam CT for imaging objects with high aspect ratios. Conventional reconstruction techniques, such as CL-FBP and CL-FDK, often yield suboptimal results charac?terized by pronounced superimposition artifacts, reduced contrast,and blurred edges, primarily due to their reliance on 1D row-wise filtering along detector rows. To address these limitations and improve reconstruction quality, we proposed a novel 2D directional filtered backprojection (DFBP) method based on the point spread function (PSF). First, an exact expression for the projection process is derived by establishing the relationship between a reconstructed pixel and its corresponding projection point on the detector. Second, a revised backprojection process incorporating two weighting factors is introduced to counteract the nonlinearity inherent in conventional backprojection, leading to a simplified PSF formulation. Third, to circumvent the computational burden of 3D image space filtering,an approximate method by linearizing the coordinate relationship in Fourier space under some assumptions is developed that transfers the 3D filtering operation to the 2D projection space. This approach facilitates the derivation of a formally simple yet effective 2D direc?tional filter, which integrates a 2D von Hann window and a 2D sinc window. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method produces reconstructions with superior contrast, sharper boundaries,and fewer superimposition artifacts compared to CL-FBP and CL?FDK. Moreover, it enables more accurate recovery of internal structures, such as bubble defects and electronic components.

papers.title: Spontaneous Chirality and Collective Chern Bands in a Dipole-Conserving Bose System
papers.abstract: We demonstrate spontaneous chiral dipole order and an isolated collective Chern band in a time-reversal-symmetric microscopic bosonic lattice model with exact dipole-moment conservation. In a controlled large-occupation limit at zero temperature, frustrated dipole exchange and three-particle conversion stabilize two time-reversed chiral condensates. The two dipole Goldstone modes remain gapless, while a separate finite-frequency band carries Chern numbers $-1$ and $+1$ in the opposite domains. We trace this topology to complex mode couplings in the chiral background that gap finite-frequency Dirac crossings. Site-resolved density drives preserve dipole-moment conservation and reconstruct the band Chern number from band-resolved absorption spectra in the quadratic theory.

papers.title: Task-Specialized Language-Conditioned Models for Fine-Grained Robotic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Fine-grained robotic manipulation requires instruction grounding, robust perception, and precise contact control. We describe our submission to the MetaFine Open Competition at CoRL 2026. Five independently trained models use a common architecture with frozen DINOv2 and CLIP encoders, trainable language-conditioned feature modulation, and task-specific action heads. We improve demonstrations through contact-aware grasp filtering, instruction-matched data, and expert correction of insertion failures. At inference, task-dependent strategies include photometric test-time augmentation, stochastic action averaging, and uncertainty-triggered replanning. Our submission achieves an official overall score of 0.914 and ranks third among 15 teams. We analyze the models and their task-specific behavior.

papers.title: Strong complete immersions in graphs with independence number two
papers.abstract: We prove that every graph $G$ with independence number at most two contains a strong immersion of $K_{χ(G)}$. This strengthens Dahlke's theorem for weak immersions and establishes the Lescure--Meyniel conjecture for this class of graphs.

papers.title: Evaluating Tactile Foundation Models for End-to-End Imitation Learning in Contact-Rich Manipulation
papers.abstract: Tactile sensing plays an important role in imitation learning for contact-rich manipulation by providing direct observations of physical contact with objects. Recently, several tactile foundation models (TFMs) have been proposed to learn general-purpose tactile representations through pretraining on large-scale tactile datasets. However, how these pretrained tactile representations should be leveraged for end-to-end imitation learning remains insufficiently explored. In this work, we integrate multiple TFMs into Diffusion Policy and systematically evaluate their effectiveness for contact-rich manipulation under common experimental settings. We further investigate adaptation strategies, including encoder fine-tuning and task-specific mid-training, to understand how pretrained tactile representations can be effectively used for downstream imitation learning. Through extensive evaluation across diverse manipulation tasks in both real-world and simulation environments, including more than 5,000 real-world policy rollouts, we provide empirical insights into the use of TFMs for end-to-end imitation learning. Project page: https://mmurooka.github.io/tfm4il-project-page/

papers.title: Quantifying Repair Risk in Crypto Option Surfaces
papers.abstract: Option desks adjust crypto option quotes into price surfaces that remain within bid-ask intervals and satisfy standard no-arbitrage restrictions across strikes before computing Greeks, hedge quantities, or risk measures. For the same quote panel, however, these constraints may admit multiple such surfaces, which we call admissible repairs, with different downstream outputs. We define the resulting variation as repair risk and propose repair-risk validation, a matched framework for quantifying dispersion in Greeks, hedge quantities, and risk measures. The mechanism is finite-difference amplification: two admissible repairs within price distance $\varepsilon$ can differ in local normalized-strike curvature by $4\varepsilon/h^2$, where $h$ is local normalized-strike spacing. We evaluate repair risk on Deribit BTC and ETH option chains, using $L_1$ and $L_2$ projections of midpoint prices onto the same admissible set as matched controls. Across 108 matched evaluations spanning 18 sampled calendar months, the median 90th percentile of the scaled spot-gamma gap for $L_2$ versus the $ρ=10$ smoothness-penalized repair is nearly twenty times the matched $L_1$--$L_2$ control. We also instantiate NN-Proj, a neural-projection repair, to test whether learned repairs exhibit repair risk. Despite good held-out fit, its downstream outputs remain distinct from those of classical repairs. Across five seeds with the same training window and architecture, its curvature dispersion exceeds the matched $L_1$--$L_2$ control in 17 of 18 months ($p=1.45\times10^{-4}$). For a USD 1 million risk reversal, switching from $L_2$ to the $ρ=10$ repair shifts the median 90th-percentile hedge notional by 18.62 basis points of gross spot notional. VaR-style estimates also exhibit greater dispersion across repairs. The repair rule is therefore part of the risk model, not merely a feasibility check.

papers.title: NovaFilter - A Rule-Based ETL Staging Framework for Fault-Tolerant Relational Databases
papers.abstract: NovaFilter is a completely new approach to deriving structured relational data from heterogeneous input data in different data formats. It combines consistency checks, rule-based data transformation, and a human-in-the-loop example discussion. Using these three components, NovaFilter stores all transformation knowledge in an explicit rule base, which is continuously expanded through the example discussion with the user. The resulting data transformation process is deterministic, transparent, and reusable. As a result, the method can replace conventional ETL scripts and offers a completely new strategy for transforming data between different data models and schemas. Its main advantage is that users without programming skills (e.g. domain experts) can answer the example discussion and thus it is a building block for democratization of ETL script developement.

papers.title: Self-Refining Prompt Induction for Streaming Text-to-SQL
papers.abstract: Text-to-SQL assistants for streaming engines must handle dialect-specific types, windowing rules, and temporal semantics, including constructs poorly handled by generic prompts. We present Self-Refining Prompt Induction (SRPI), an offline method that converts generation failures into reusable dialect instructions while keeping model weights fixed. A Refiner revises the Generator's prompt using reference-conditioned feedback from three LLM judges; a sampled regression guard checks earlier successes, and a separate Compressor reduces prompt length. Inference uses the frozen prompt without retrieval or query repair. We evaluate cross-domain and cross-model transfer on Confluent Cloud Flink SQL using a controlled synthetic workload seeded by 30 expert-written examples, with 335 induction examples and 257 questions from held-out domains. The same induced prompt improves mean judge scores across seven Generators by 7.1-19.2 percentage points, including an increase from 85.3% to 97.5% for the induction model. A separate compression study reduces prompt length by 52.7% with a 0.19-percentage-point score decrease. An assistant using the induced prompt is in early access, with initial user feedback to inform subsequent refinement.

papers.title: Linear resolutions of powers of edge ideals of gap-free graphs with matching number four
papers.abstract: For a finite simple gap-free graph $G$, let $B(G)$ denote the vertices $v$ for which $G-N_G[v]$ is not co-chordal, and put $C(G)=V(G)\setminus B(G)$. We prove a sufficient condition for all ordinary powers of its edge ideal to have linear resolutions from the second power onward: every induced anticycle of length at least five must contain an edge with both endpoints in $C(G)$. The argument uses variable generators of augmented colon ideals to eliminate anticycles that may persist in the ordinary quadratic colons. It yields linear resolutions for all powers $I(G)^q$, $q\ge2$, whenever the ordinary matching number is at most four, which answers the first part of a question of Erey, Hà, Hibi, Kara and Morey. The criterion also applies to certain graphs with adjacent exceptional vertices and matching number five. The proofs are theoretical and valid over arbitrary fields. We do not assert linear quotients.

papers.title: Markov-driven self-similar measures and non-homogeneous slicing
papers.abstract: We introduce the concept of Markov-driven self-similar measures, a notion that simultaneously generalizes classical self-similar measures, self-conformal measures, dynamically driven self-similar measures and many random measures. This class is also closed under Cartesian products and linear projections. We initiate the study of this class of measures and investigate the $L^q$ dimension of Markov-driven self-similar measures under certain Diophantine conditions. As an application, we obtain the first Furstenberg slicing type results for intersections of Cantor sets in non-homogeneous settings.

papers.title: 4K Image Super-Resolution on Mobile NPUs: Mobile AI 2026 Challenge Report
papers.abstract: Image super-resolution is widely used on mobile devices for upscaling various types of image data. This creates a need for efficient deep learning-based models that are not only performant but can also be deployed on neural processing units (NPUs) present in the majority of mobile and IoT chipsets. In this Mobile AI challenge, we address this problem and propose the participants to design fast solutions that can upsample images from Full HD to 4K resolution while running on popular mobile NPUs from Qualcomm and MediaTek. For this, the participants were provided with the DIV2K dataset and trained models to do an efficient 3X image upscaling. The competition had two tracks: in the first track, the models had to be fully quantized (INT8), and the runtime of all models was evaluated on the Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 NPU. In the second track, the participants were developing floating-point solutions that were evaluated on the MediaTek Dimensity 9500 NPU. Top solutions proposed in this challenge are able to reconstruct 4K images under 5 milliseconds while reaching a PSNR score of 30 dB. A comprehensive description of the models developed in the challenge is provided in this paper.

papers.title: Stability threshold for 3D Boussinesq equations with rotation near the Couette flow and vertical stratified temperature
papers.abstract: The most important features that distinguish fluid flow in the atmosphere and ocean are the effects of rotation and stratification, which are described by the Boussinesq equations with rotation. This paper examines the stability threshold at high Reynolds number $\mathbf{Re}$ for the 3D Boussinesq equations with rotation near Couette flow and a vertical stratified temperature. For the zero modes, the combined effects of rotation and stratification sustain velocity-temperature oscillations with frequencies bounded away from zero. In the stable rotational regime, rotation suppresses the linear growth associated with the lift-up effect, while stratification sustains oscillations in the double zero modes. Although the zero modes dynamics are not fully dispersive, we exploit the structure of the oscillatory phases and cancellations in the equations to obtain a modified energy estimate for the entire zero modes system. Combining this estimate with enhanced dissipation and inviscid damping of the nonzero modes, we establish a bound for the stability threshold, with order $\mathbf{Re}^{-2/3}(1+\log\mathbf{Re})^{-1-a_0}$ for any fixed $a_0\in(0,1/2)$.

papers.title: High-Frequency Estimation of the Leverage Effect under Rough Volatility with Microstructure Noise
papers.abstract: This paper develops feasible high-frequency inference for the leverage effect when the spot variance follows rough Volterra dynamics, leverage loadings depend on endogenous rough states, and observed prices may be contaminated by microstructure noise. We define an integrated leverage parameter through a scaled covariation between log prices and spot variance that accounts for their different local fluctuation scales. The scaled realized covariation admits a stable functional central limit theorem with an explicit pathwise centering correction arising from within-interval variation in the leverage loading. A loading regularity condition renders this correction asymptotically negligible, and we verify the condition for direct Volterra loadings and for smooth functions of closed rough states for every Hurst index below one half. We construct a block-based estimator with an exact finite-window correction for the leading proportional bias, together with a nonnegative single-scale estimator of its asymptotic variance. Pre-averaging extends feasible inference to observations with independent and identically distributed microstructure noise. Simulations under the rough Heston model demonstrate accurate finite-sample calibration with and without noise. An empirical application to fifteen years of one-second data on nine U.S. equities and ETFs finds negative median leverage estimates for every asset at weekly and monthly horizons.

papers.title: Categorifications of noncrossing partitions of type B and affine type A
papers.abstract: The lattice of wide subcategories of a tube is isomorphic to the lattice of noncrossing partitions of type B. We prove that through this categorification of noncrossing partitions, Kreweras complement is taking left perpendicular categories. With the help of this categorification and weighted projective lines, we obtain an inclusion from the lattice of noncrossing partitions of type B_n to a lattice of affine type A_n which preserves Kreweras complement.

papers.title: RTP-LLM: Building an Evolvable and Reliable LLM Inference Engine at Alibaba Scale
papers.abstract: Large language models and inference techniques evolve rapidly, making model enablement a recurring production task rather than a one-time integration effort. At Alibaba, a shared inference infrastructure must keep pace with new models and serving capabilities while remaining reliable across heterogeneous production environments. To reconcile rapid evolution with production reliability, we present RTP-LLM, an open-source production inference engine developed and deployed at Alibaba. Its architecture separates model-specific execution from shared request processing, state management, and resource coordination. Explicit interfaces localize compatible model changes while allowing models and deployment configurations to reuse common serving mechanisms. RTP-LLM has evolved from an exploratory system into a shared production engine that supports $\sim$100 models and processes hundreds of trillions of tokens per day. We describe how its architecture and production practices accommodate model evolution and contain the impact of failures, and share lessons for building evolvable and reliable inference engines at enterprise scale.

papers.title: Autotuning GPU Thread Block Sizes for Large-Scale Stencil Applications Using the OPS DSL
papers.abstract: Large-scale structured-mesh stencil applications can run for hours or days on modern HPC GPU platforms, making launch-configuration choices important. OPS enables high-level stencil codes to target multiple GPU architectures, but its GPU backends rely on a default or user-selected global block/workgroup shape, even though different kernels, problem geometries, and architectures may favor different configurations. This paper presents a transparent per-kernel block/workgroup-shape autotuning extension for OPS. The extension explores valid block/workgroup shapes during execution, records the fastest configuration for each kernel, and enables precomputed replay of the selected configurations in subsequent runs. We evaluate the approach on structured-mesh proxy and academic research applications, covering 459 unique kernels across 3 NVIDIA and 2 AMD GPUs. The evaluation reports speedup distributions, representative wall-time summaries, timing variability, and input problem shape effects. Replaying the best per-kernel launch shapes improves 923 of 995 measured application/input/GPU cases over the default OPS shape. Depending on the GPU, the median speedup ranges from 1.02x to 1.18x, with individual configurations of LAPL2D, TTI3D, and OpenSBLI-based TGV solvers exceeding 1.5x. The results also show that performance sensitivity is not limited to launch shape. At fixed cell count, changing the input problem shape changes precomputed-replay runtime by 0.8-34.6% in representative cases, while kernel-level timing variability depends on the interaction between runtime contribution, input problem shape, and GPU/backend behavior. Overall, automatic per-kernel block/workgroup-shape selection improves OPS performance across GPUs, provided shape sensitivity and timing stability are interpreted together.

papers.title: Decay Rate toward the Rarefaction Wave and the Viscous Contact Wave for Jin--Xin Relaxation Model
papers.abstract: This paper establishes the time-decay rates toward the rarefaction wave and the viscous contact wave for the one-dimensional Jin--Xin relaxation system under the $L^1$ integrability condition of the initial perturbation. In the case of a strictly convex flux, we employ a decomposition method to derive a logarithmic $L^1$ estimate related to a conjecture proposed by Liu\cite{liu2001lp}. Furthermore, a time-weighted $L^2$ method yields the optimal decay rate toward the rarefaction wave. Regarding the case where the flux is partially linearly degenerate, by employing a similar \(L^1\) estimate and time-weighted \(L^2\) method, along with a refined estimate of the nonlinear wave interactions, we obtain the corresponding decay rate toward the composite wave. The decay estimates are obtained without smallness assumptions on the initial perturbations or the wave strength.

papers.title: A JWST/NIRSpec Catalog of Low-Mass Candidates toward NGC 2024 from Multi-component Spectral Modeling
papers.abstract: Young low-mass objects in crowded, highly obscured star-forming regions are difficult to characterize. Deriving reliable physical parameters requires separating photospheric emission from complex extinction and circumstellar emission. We apply a multi-component spectral-modeling framework to JWST/NIRSpec PRISM spectra toward NGC 2024, obtaining adopted fits for 78 sources. The framework incorporates atmospheric models, dust and ice opacities, and optional thermal emission. Most spectra favor additional large-H$_2$O-ice opacity over the baseline small-grain model, while a smaller subset requires additional gray opacity, potentially arising from large refractory grains. Some spectra also require a thermal component to reproduce the long-wavelength continuum. The parameters inferred with this framework, together with the NGC 2024 distance, yield radii and bolometric luminosities. Comparison with evolutionary models for young low-mass and substellar objects provides mass estimates and identifies 46 candidate members, 27 sources classified as background, and five uncertain sources. Candidate members show lower fitted surface gravities than likely background stars. Of the candidate members, 23 lie above the youngest available isochrones, plausibly reflecting the cluster's youth and uncertainties in model initial conditions. The resulting catalog provides a uniform characterization of the NGC 2024 sample and establishes a framework for treating complex extinction and circumstellar emission in JWST spectra of other obscured star-forming regions.

papers.title: E-UDE: A Scientific Machine Learning Model for Malware Propagation Dynamics
papers.abstract: Understanding the malware propagation dynamics over the Internet is crucial for effectively controlling its spread. Existing mechanistic and data-driven models in the context of malware propagation dynamics, have some issues with either interpretability or predictive accuracy. This study presents an Enhanced Universal Differential Equation (E-UDE) framework that explicitly incorporates more detailed key factors that influence malware propagation. Evaluation on real-world malware propagation data shows that the E-UDE achieves the best overall performance, attaining an overall RMSE of 783.70 and MAE of 421.65. Compared with the Classical ODE and the UDE models, the proposed approach reduces RMSE by approximately 66 percent and 39 percent, respectively. Its robustness to predictive capability is further evaluated. In this experiment, the E-UDE achieves a Test RMSE of 634.6, a Test MAE of 419.3, and a Test Correlation of 0.964. The E-UDE maintains relatively stable prediction performance as the noise level increases, showing limited degradation compared with the baseline models. Furthermore, this E-UDE model enables us to perform several scenario analyses under different cybersecurity scenarios, providing a useful framework for better understanding the effective control factors.
