The model, structured as a system of nonlinear ordinary differential equations, is analyzed for the existence of the equilibrium and its stability. In the analysis, the stable disease-free equilibrium is found to exist, representing complete societal balance. The other endemic equilibrium is shown to be infeasible through simulations and thus requires certain parameter constraints, which represent a specific scenario that may occur in the population. However, it is found that the endemic equilibrium always remains unstable. The model's ability to quantify how micro-level stressors spread into macro-level imbalance is demonstrated by numerical simulations, which also validate the analytical results. This work establishes a rigorous mathematical foundation for WLB, enabling future empirical and mathematical calibrations.

papers.title: A Kernel-Based Test for Multi-Way Conditional Independence
papers.abstract: Conditional independence involving more than two variables, or multi-way conditional independence, is a fundamental probabilistic structure useful in many areas of statistical research, including latent-variable and graphical models. However, most existing works focus on pairwise conditional independence. To address this gap, we propose a kernel-based test of multi-way conditional independence. Specifically, we characterize this hypothesis through the simultaneous vanishing of a vector of conditional cross-covariance operators and construct a test statistic based on the norm of the vector of their estimators. We derive the statistic's asymptotic distributions under the null hypothesis and local alternatives. As a related methodological contribution, we also develop a test of multi-way unconditional independence and provide a procedure for its implementation. An application to RNA data illustrates the method's use in genomics.

papers.title: New Scaling Relations for Nucleons in Three-Nucleon Short-Range Correlations
papers.abstract: The search for three nucleon short range correlations~(3N- SRCs) in nuclei is one of the intensive areas of research in high density nuclear physics. It is in part motivated by the prediction of the above two-solar mass neutron stars based on 3N short-range forces and the subsequent observation of such stars. The 3N-SRCs serve as a "laboratory" for probing the dynamics of largely unknown irreducible 3N-forces. However, the identification of 3N-SRCs in high energy nuclear processes is still elusive making the prospects of their investigation problematic. In this work we introduced new dynamical parameters for 2N- and 3N- SRCs, $β_{2N}$ and $β_{3N}$ respectively, which characterize the strength of SRCs beyond combinatorial counting of nucleons in SRCs. For 2N-SRCs the introduction of $β_{2N}$ parameter resulted in a previously known and experimentally verified relation for proton and neutron momentum distributions in 2N-SRCS. For 3N-SRCs the $β_{3N}$ parameter allowed to factorize momentum distributions of nucleons in the correlation resulting in a prediction of a new scaling relation between proton and neutron momentum distributions in 3N SRCs. This relation, if valid gives a new venue for identification of 3N-SRCs in electro-nuclear processes. Even though the obtained scaling relation is relevant in the relativistic domain, the possibility of separating center of mass motion of SRCs on the light-front allows to check the validity of predicted scaling using non-relativistic ab-initio wave functions. We found surprisingly reasonable confirmation of our prediction analyzing ab-initio wave functions of nuclei in the range $3\le A\le 12$. This indicates the robustness of the scaling relation and opens up a new direction in searching for 3N-SRCs experimentally.

papers.title: Profile decomposition, strict binding and global compactness for a critical Grushin embedding
papers.abstract: We study attainment of the best constant in \begin{equation*} \int_{\mathbb R^{m+n}} \bigl(|\nabla_xu|^2+|x|^2|\nabla_yu|^2+a|u|^2\bigr) \geq S_a\left(\int_{\mathbb R^{m+n}} (1+|x|^2)^{n/(Q-2)}|u|^q\right)^{2/q}, \end{equation*} where \(m,n\geq1\), \(Q=m+2n\), \(q=2Q/(Q-2)\), and \(a>0\). Using annular interpolation and a transverse-average recurrence with \(L^q\) contraction \(2^{-m/q}\), we decompose bounded sequences into finite, Grushin and Euclidean profiles. Energy and critical mass split, with a power bound in the number of profiles on the remaining mass. We prove compactness of normalized minimizing sequences modulo \(y\)-translations under \(S_a<\min\{S_G,a^{n/Q}S_E(1)\}\), where \(S_G\) and \(S_E(1)\) are the tangent constants. The strict-binding set is empty or an open interval; we prove nonemptiness for \(n=1\) and even \(m\geq6\). At finite positive endpoints of a nonempty binding interval, we characterize attainment by first-order binding gaps. We obtain a finite critical-profile decomposition of Palais--Smale sequences with a remainder vanishing in energy.

papers.title: Pop Goes the Verifier: Phoneme-Targeted Data Poisoning of Voice Liveness Detection
papers.abstract: Many Automated Speaker Verification Systems (ASVs) commonly employ liveliness detection techniques, such as VoicePop, which identify genuine speech by analyzing low- frequency pop bursts from plosive phonemes using Gammatone Frequency Cepstral Coefficients (GFCC) and an SVM classifier. While effective against traditional replay attacks, such systems are vulnerable to data poisoning techniques. Prior work shows that broadly applied SyntheticPop attacks can collapse model to accuracy to as low as 14.01% using only 20% poisoned samples, but the resulting artifacts are easily detectable when visualizing the waveform energies. This paper introduces Pop Goes the Verifier, a stealthier phoneme injection poisoning attack. By leveraging FastSpeech 2 (FS2) with a modified HiFi-GAN vocoder, we inject localized pop bursts at plosive phoneme locations and overlay subtle Gaussian noise to reduce the visibility of injected artifacts in waveform and spectrogram analysis. Using the ASVSpoof 2019 as the dataset, we observe that the approach achieves a moderate poisoning attack while providing greater resistance to signal-level inspection than the original SyntheticPop attack.

papers.title: From Gaussian to stable and back: Non-Pareto points in growing dimension
papers.abstract: We study the number of non-Pareto points in two high-dimensional models: a homogeneous Poisson point process and a fixed-size sample of independent uniform points in the unit cube. A point is non-Pareto if some other sample point is coordinatewise less than or equal to it. As the dimension grows on the logarithmic scale of the intensity or sample size, the asymptotic behavior exhibits a surprising sequence of transitions: from Gaussian to stable fluctuations, back to Gaussian, then to a Poisson limit at the sparsity threshold, followed by the eventual disappearance of non-Pareto points. We identify the critical thresholds, normalizations, and limiting laws in both models. Notably, the return to Gaussianity occurs while the stability index remains strictly below $2$ and is driven by a change in the dominant fluctuation mechanism. Moreover, in part of the returning Gaussian regime, the natural normalization is the square root of the expected count rather than its standard deviation. At the stable--Gaussian transition, the two mechanisms can coexist, giving rise to a sum of independent stable and Gaussian random variables.

papers.title: The Blind Spots of Detection: Adversarial Perturbation Attacks against Watchdogs in Distributed LLM Inference
papers.abstract: Decentralizing large language model (LLM) inference across untrusted Web nodes requires robust verification to ensure computational integrity. Existing activation-based verification and detection mechanisms validate intermediate outputs against reference values, permitting bounded numerical deviations to accommodate benign cross-hardware discrepancies. However, a critical security question remains: what can a malicious worker achieve while operating within these tolerance bounds? In this work, we introduce Hush-Up, a stealthy availability attack against distributed LLM inference, where a single malicious worker halts generation while evading attribution. The attacker first profiles its local execution to model an empirical bound of benign hardware errors. Using this error bound as a feasibility constraint, the attacker optimizes an adversarial perturbation on its output activations to maximize the final-layer probability of the end-of-sequence (EOS) token, i.e., to hush up the model. Across diverse models and benchmarks, Hush-Up effectively forces premature generation termination and collapses model capabilities. Furthermore, the attack hushes up the watchdogs themselves: existing defenses often fail to detect the sabotage entirely or falsely attribute the amplified downstream anomalies to honest workers. Our findings expose a fundamental gap between local numerical verification and end-to-end accountability: perturbations too small to indict a worker locally can nevertheless be powerful enough to break distributed inference globally.

papers.title: Mitigating Catastrophic Forgetting in Task-Free Federated Continual Forecasting via Two-Tier Replay under Concept Drift
papers.abstract: Federated time-series forecasting is increasingly important in applications where temporal data are distributed across privacy-sensitive clients, such as environmental monitoring, smart cities, and industrial sensing. A central limitation of current continual-learning protocols is that they usually assume predefined task boundaries, whereas deployed forecasting systems receive an uninterrupted stream and must decide autonomously when adaptation is necessary. This paper addresses catastrophic forgetting in task-free federated forecasting under concept drift. We introduce a drift-aware continual-learning protocol in which each client monitors prediction-window RMSE, calibrates a robust median threshold from the offline base period, and triggers adaptation only after persistent degradation. To mitigate forgetting, we propose a TwoTierReplay mechanism that separates fixed offline representative memory from online memory. The offline tier preserves long-term knowledge learned during the base phase, while the online tier captures recent distributional changes after drift. Experiments on the Beijing Multi-Site Air- Quality dataset with 12 clients, three forecasting targets, and three horizons show that TwoTierReplay achieves the best stability-plasticity score in all nine target-horizon configurations. It improves over the strongest baseline by approximately 11.4%. These results suggest that explicit temporal structuring of replay memory is a practical and effective mechanism for task-free federated continual forecasting.

papers.title: Anomalous response, re-emerging localization-transition and robust corner sates in self-similar peano fractal
papers.abstract: Anomalous spectral response from the non-interacting electrons on a peano fractal is recorded within tight-binding framework. It is observed that a minimal off-diagonal anisotropy can modulate the transport characteristics of the lattice. Drastic modification in the nature of the eigenstates has been validated through the workout of level spacing statistics. Further, a two-dimensional quasiperiodic Aubry-André and Harper variation in the overlap integral can invite re-entrant localization-delocalization transition for the self-similar model. This is associated with the possible existence of single-particle mobility edge in the energy landscape. Our results are corroborated by the evaluation of inverse participation ratio, fractal dimension and quantum dynamical response. The spectrum is shown to formulate a quantum butterfly pattern with the frequency of the modulation. Chiral symmetry protected edge states are found to be insensitive with respect to moderate diagonal disorder.

papers.title: Co-design of Output-Feedback Neural Network Control Barrier Functions and Observers for Stochastic Jump-Diffusion Systems
papers.abstract: In this paper, we present a framework for designing controllers for partially observed continuous-time stochastic systems. We use the notion of control barrier functions (CBF) and provide an upper bound to the probability of state trajectories violating the system's safety when starting in an initial region. Our framework co-designs a neural network-based controller, an output-feedback observer, and a control barrier function for the given system. Although CBF requires full state information, we formulate CBF conditions over an augmented state space of actual and observer states. We train the neural networks simultaneously by defining appropriate loss functions, and finally demonstrate the effectiveness through two case studies: a linear DC motor and a nonlinear system.

papers.title: A localized packing lemma for sets of bounded $\operatorname{VC}_2$-dimension
papers.abstract: In the setting of abelian groups, Haussler's packing lemma implies that any subset of bounded $\operatorname{VC}$-dimension can be approximated by one of a small number of representative translates. While this exact statement is provably false under the weaker hypothesis that $A$ has bounded $\operatorname{VC}_2$-dimension, we show that in $\mathbb{F}_p^n$ a similar statement does hold after localization to cosets of subspaces depending on the individual translates. More precisely, given $ε>0$ and $A\subseteq \mathbb{F}_p^n$ with $\operatorname{VC}_2(A)<k$, we show that there exist $r\leq ε^{-O_{k,p}(1)}$ and $g_1,\ldots, g_r\in \mathbb{F}_p^n$ with the property that for every $x\in \mathbb{F}_p^n$, there is a partition $\mathcal{C}_x$ of $\mathbb{F}_p^n$ into cosets of (possibly distinct) subgroups, each of index at most $\exp(ε^{-O_{k,p}(1)})$, and a subcollection $Ω_x\subseteq \mathcal{C}_x$ whose union has size at least $(1-ε)|\mathbb{F}_p^n|$, such that on each $C\in Ω_x$, the translate $A-x$ looks like one of $A-g_1,\ldots, A-g_r$, in the sense that $|((A-x)Δ(A-g_{i_{x,C}}))\cap C|<ε|C|$ for some $1\leq i_{x,C}\leq r$. We also prove a second version of this result in which each partition $\mathcal{C}_x$ is the set of cosets of a single subgroup $H_x$ of quasipolynomial index but where the bound on $r$ is a quadruple exponential.

papers.title: A matroid characterization of the combinatorially symmetric maximum nullity of a graph
papers.abstract: The graph parameter ${\mathrm N}(G)$ is the maximum nullity among all combinatorially symmetric matrices associated to a graph $G$. The zero forcing number ${\mathrm Z}(G)$ is a well-known upper bound for ${\mathrm N}(G)$, and a zero forcing set of $G$ is exactly a set that intersects each fort of the graph. So the zero forcing number can be defined as the size of a minimum set that intersects every fort of $G$. This paper provides a similar characterization of ${\mathrm N}(G)$ that is purely combinatorial, using a connection to matroid theory and collections of forts that are compatible in a certain sense. We provide several examples highlighting subtle differences among compatible collections of forts and how they relate to full spark matrices and matroids associated to $G$.

papers.title: Comment on "Zero temperature, degenerate fermion stars" [S. Boatto, M.B. Paranjape, V. Pessanha, C.A.D. Zarro. ArXiv: 2609.20950]
papers.abstract: In contrast to S. Boatto et al. \cite{Boat}, the degree of compactification or compactness is clarified for the self-gravitating spheric star of fermionic matter.

papers.title: Secant dimensions and bilinear decomposition widths for finite Heisenberg groups
papers.abstract: Let $G=UT_3(\F_q)$ be the finite Heisenberg group. We study the image closures and secant varieties of a family of equivariant bilinear maps between representations induced from central characters. Evaluation at a basepoint identifies the ambient space with $M_{q^2}(\C)$. A single channel is represented by $A^T\operatorname{diag}(d)B$, with $A$ and $B$ in prescribed twisted-convolution algebras. We prove that its affine image closure has dimension $3q^2-2$ for every central-character pair and that its affine second-secant closure has the expected dimension for every prime power $q$. For $q\ge3$, the proof constructs two differential images with zero intersection. We also prove a subgroup-lifting theorem for channel parameterizations on finite abelian groups with bicharacter coefficients: a parameter point with differential rank $r(3|H|-2)$ on a subgroup $H$ extends by zero to a parameter point with differential rank $r(3|K|-2)$ on the ambient group $K$, provided that every parameter vector is nonzero. Exact Jacobian certificates determine all secant dimensions for $q=2,3,4,5$, with generic widths $2,4,6,9$. The lifting theorem yields specified higher-secant dimensions on infinite families of extension fields. Attainment of the dimension lower bound for arbitrary $q$ remains a conjecture.

papers.title: Minimum-Norm Interpolation in Weighted Variation Spaces: Direct and Inverse Problems
papers.abstract: We study minimum-norm interpolation in weighted variation spaces generated by ReLU$^s$ ridge functions on the unit ball, where $s$ is a positive integer. For a target $f$ in the weighted variation space and a node set with sufficiently small fill distance $h$, every minimum-norm interpolant satisfies the direct bound $\|f-\mathscr{I}_{X_h}f\|_{L_2(\mathbb{B}^d)}\lesssim_{d,s}h^{(2s+1)/4}\|f\|_{\mathcal{V}_s}$. Under a boundary separation condition on the nodes, we construct a matching lower bound for the worst-case interpolation error. For the inverse problem, we introduce dual certificates and derive an estimate analogous to a Bernstein inequality. Under suitable upper bounds on dictionary size and spectral lower bounds for the atomic Gram matrices, sufficiently fast $L_2$ convergence of minimum-norm interpolants along geometrically decreasing fill distances implies that the target belongs to $\mathcal{V}_s$. As a byproduct, the best $L_2$ approximation error $E_n(f)_{L_2(\mathbb{B}^d)}$ for shallow ReLU$^s$ networks of width at most $n$ satisfies $E_n(f)_{L_2(\mathbb{B}^d)}\lesssim_{d,s}n^{-1/2-(2s+1)/(2d)}\|f\|_{\mathcal{V}_s}$, with the weighted atomic cost of an approximating network bounded by a constant multiple of $\|f\|_{\mathcal{V}_s}$, independently of $n$.

papers.title: The Value of Steiner Hubs in Two-Hop Distance Labeling
papers.abstract: Two-hop distance labelings were introduced in 2002 by Cohen, Halperin, Kaplan, and Zwick with hubs of two kinds: vertices of the graph, or, in their Steiner variant, arbitrary objects carrying arbitrary real values. On no family is the value of that freedom known. We determine it on $\ell_1$ products of betweenness-free metrics, those with no point between two others, a class containing every Hamming graph. The freedom is worth nothing when the factors have at most three letters, while from four letters on the largest saving is polynomial in the size of the product, attained on products of positively weighted stars. The $d$-dimensional hypercube is the two-letter case, and labeling it takes $(5/2+o(1))^d$ entries even with arbitrary hubs, matching the vertex-hub optimum of Goldberg, Razenshteyn, and Savchenko. Every lower bound here comes from one semidefinite program on a single factor, whose value $Λ$ never exceeds the rate that vertex hubs already achieve on the Hamming graph; where $Λ$ meets that ceiling, the freedom is worth nothing, and the ceiling is met exactly up to three letters.

papers.title: Digital Twin-Assisted Fast Beam Alignment for mmWave MIMO Networks
papers.abstract: Millimeter-wave (mmWave) communication relies on directional beam sweeping for initial access, which incurs substantial latency and signaling overhead as antenna arrays grow large and deployments become denser. Machine-learning-based beam prediction can reduce this overhead, but its effectiveness depends on training data that accurately reflects the deployment environment, a requirement that is difficult to meet in practice. This paper presents a latency-aware beam management architecture that integrates digital-twin-assisted prediction, regionbased localization, weighted ensemble learning, and explainability-driven beam pruning into a unified framework. A digital twin (DT) generates site-specific ray-traced channel knowledge offline, enabling environment-aware beam prediction without exhaustive real-world measurements and supporting both initial access and beam tracking. The proposed ensemble learning scheme combines a base classifier and a specialist classifier through reliability-weighted fusion to improve prediction accuracy and robustness, while explainable artificial intelligence (XAI)-based attribution pruning reduces the beam codebook to a small subset of the most informative beams for beam allocation. To capture the distributional mismatch between the DT and real-world environments: the network was trained on imperfect digital-twin data but evaluated on real-world surrobase data. Results show that the proposed method achieves 96.80% top-1 and 98.36% top-3 beam prediction accuracy, while reducing over-the-air sounding overhead by nearly an order of magnitude relative to exhaustive sweeping, outperforming convolutional and deep neural network baselines from prior work.

papers.title: Semiclassical Wave Packet Dynamics For Nonlinear Schrödinger Equations with Harmonic Potentials
papers.abstract: We propose an approximate Hamiltonian dynamics for the Gross--Pitaevskii equation $i\hbarψ_t = -\frac{\hbar^2}{2m}Δψ+ V(x)ψ+ \hbar^2 λ|ψ|^2ψ$ with harmonic potential $V(x)$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}^d$. We do this by extending the Gaussian ansatz of Perez-Garcia et al.~(Phys.~Rev.~A 56, 1424 (1997)) to the semiclassical wave packets of Hagedorn. We derive the evolution equations for the wave packets from the Hamiltonian/symplectic perspective, rather than the Lagrangian/variational one taken by Perez-Garcia et al. We first show that these two perspectives yield identical evolution equations in the Gaussian case. We then derive the evolution equations for an arbitrary element of the semiclassical wave packets. Finally, we demonstrate the efficacy of the approximate dynamics with numerical experiments.

papers.title: Light Fidelity in Academic Libraries: A Radiant Journey to Light the Future
papers.abstract: Academic contexts have changed due to the fast expansion of communication technology, affecting information access, sharing, and dissemination. Light Fidelity (LiFi) is a new technology that may transform academic library connections in this changing environment. This article examines how LiFi can accelerate data transmission, secure data, and provide a more dynamic and collaborative learning environment to spur creativity. Academic libraries may accelerate information interchange using visible light communication with LiFi technology. LiFi is the solution for the increasing need of digital access it adress the situation by enabling faster research activities and enhancing collaboration among students, faculty, and researchers. Present paper discusses the importance and application of LiFi in libraries.

papers.title: Phase-Tunable Liouvillian Topology: Dual Winding Structures and Skin Effects
papers.abstract: Liouvillian skin effects are usually associated with dissipation whose rates favor unidirectional flow. In this work, we show that directional edge localization can emerge even when population exchange between sites is exactly balanced, with a single tunable phase parameter $α$ deciding their direction and a dual winding structure deciding their nature. Although this number-conserving bath is known for eigenstate selection, we demonstrate here that its phase controls a steady current, which Hamiltonian hopping converts to directional edge localization. Further, we study the spectral winding structure by independently twisting the left (ket) and right (bra) vector indices of the density matrix, revealing two distinct windings whose relationship is dictated by an antiunitary mirror symmetry. Nearest-neighbor jump operators break this symmetry: both windings coincide, giving rise to a common spectral winding $W_0(α)=\pm1$, producing a unipolar skin effect in which the density accumulates at a specific edge. However, next nearest neighbor jump preserve it. The two windings are forced to be opposite, and the ket and bra are pushed to opposite edges, giving a bipolar skin effect of coherences present in eigenmodes, without edge localization of the density in the steady state. Remarkably, in a dimerized chain the phase-controlled density skin effect gives the steady-state zero modes a size-independent weight at the skin edge, accompanied by a kink at the topological transition. In addition, the relaxation time grows linearly with the system size, however at specific phases $α$ where the jump operators are rendered Hermitian, edge-localized eigenmodes with skin character coexist with diffusive relaxation.

papers.title: Optimal Fan-Out and Break-Even Routing Loss in Waveguide-Integrated Ge-on-Si SPAD Arrays
papers.abstract: Splitting a waveguide mode over several Ge-on-Si single-photon avalanche diodes (SPADs) relieves dead-time saturation but multiplies dark counts. We quantify this trade-off with the asymptotic count-based information rate, which prices dark counts and dead time in one unit and is attained by an optimally weighted moment estimator. For a non-paralyzable pixel, the information per pre-dead-time signal event peaks at a signal rate $y^*=\sqrt{D(D+1/τ)}$ with exact efficiency $(\sqrt{1+Dτ}-\sqrt{Dτ})^2$, which sets the optimal fan-out and a critical flux above which equal splitting is optimal. We then compare four routing architectures on 64 simulated 16-pixel arrays: an equal passive tree, static trees (uncalibrated, and an idealized calibration-informed benchmark), an ideal programmable tree, and a thermo-optic Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) tree with 1.32 dB excess loss. Ideal programmability gains up to 15.9 dB over equal splitting at low flux. At one known flux, however, the calibrated static splitter beats the MZI tree by 0.14-2.7 dB, and the penalty tends to twice the excess loss when dark counts dominate. In ensemble-median worst-case regret, the MZI tree breaks even only for flux windows wider than 2.55 decades, and not within six decades above about 3.4 dB excess loss. Event-level Monte Carlo simulations reproduce the count statistics and the predicted estimator variances within bootstrap confidence intervals. Sensitivity analyses cover dark-count level, heterogeneity, detector model and random seed. All results are simulations with representative literature parameters.

papers.title: Auriga Technical Report: A Task-Agnostic Agent Harness for Zero-Shot Embodied Manipulation
papers.abstract: Vision-language models can interpret instructions and plan manipulation tasks, yet struggle when acting directly as robot policies. On RoboDojo, a large planning-execution gap separates high-level task decisions from physical execution: removing arm execution raises GPT-6 Astra's success rate from 22.5% under the reference control interface to 76.2%. We present Auriga, a task-agnostic agent harness that closes 68.3% of this gap in zero-shot manipulation without target-task trials or resets. In Auriga, the model makes all task decisions over an explicit task belief and acts through either direct tool calls or synthesized multi-step Python programs, while the harness supplies calibrated 3D measurements, finger-referenced dual-arm control, and a single admission gateway to the robot. Before motion, the model inspects a visual trajectory preview while simulation is paused; during execution, the harness checks declared stage tolerances and grasp bounds, stopping the robot on divergence and returning the measured discrepancy for in-place recovery. Developed across 13 cross-task capability iterations and frozen for evaluation, Auriga ranks first on the RoboDojo leaderboard with a 57.7% success rate (64.0 Score), more than doubling the reference harness on the same model, and remains first under scene randomization while learned policies drop by up to 33.9%. On RoboCasa365, the same frozen harness reaches a 73.2% success rate, outperforming VLA-assisted agents by up to 23.1% on composite tasks. Project page: https://auriga.stelledge.com/ Code: https://github.com/lose4578/Auriga

papers.title: CogRSI: Evolving and Auditing Cognitive Reasoning Strategies
papers.abstract: Can a language model learn better ways to reason about other people's minds by improving its own strategies, and are the strategies it learns actually right? We study this with cogrsi. A grounded reader marks who saw each event in a story and uses a short written principle to settle disagreements between its readings. With a principle written by experts, it beats self-consistency at the same token cost. A self-improvement loop then writes the principle itself. It keeps an update only if accuracy rises by a calibrated margin, and in one variant only if it also passes counterfactual test pairs. The learned principles transfer: on 800 BigToM pairs that no system had seen, each of them scores higher than the expert principle. We then check what the learned rules actually say. Each rule is translated into code and run on thousands of small stories with known answers. Most of them give a wrong answer in at least one situation they claim to cover, for example by treating a character who is in the room as knowing what happened even while asleep. Accuracy does not reveal which rules are wrong, and the counterfactual test does not fix this. A strategy can help in practice and still be wrong as a rule, so both need checking. Our code and data are publicly available.

papers.title: Channel Estimation for Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces with Mutual Coupling
papers.abstract: Channel estimation for stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIMs) has relied on the cascade model, which ignores mutual coupling and inter-layer reflection. Under a coupling-consistent multiport model, we show that the pilots are linear in the unknown channel segments and derive least-squares and linear minimum-mean-square-error estimators, an identifiability condition and an exact error decomposition for the reactance training schedule, and a gradient-based schedule design. Cascade-based estimation floors above $0$~dB normalized error at practical layer spacings and collapses the sum rate below that of the bare feed, whereas the proposed estimators retain about $80\%$ of the perfect-channel-knowledge sum rate.

papers.title: CompSkill: Compiling Execution Experience for Skill Retrieval
papers.abstract: LLM agents increasingly rely on skill documents, yet most retrievers rank them by description alone and ignore what earlier executions revealed, even though a relevant skill can hurt execution. We present CompSkill, which indexes skills with learned 512-d keys and compiles matched same-task comparisons into skill offsets and capped key residuals (KeyOpt), so experience changes which document the executor receives, never its text. Under a logistic outcome model with unknown task difficulty, matched comparisons cancel that difficulty and only discordant ones carry information; on support executions, predictions improve with each discordant task. An experience hypergraph keeps each comparison with its executor and document versions, recalls missed skills and grounds a cited review. Compact keys raise SkillRet NDCG@10 from 64.0 to 70.9 at one eighth of the dimension. With one document, CompSkill completes 256 and 260 of 332 ToolQA tasks with GPT-5.6-luna and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, respectively, more than every baseline, and stays on par with the strongest baselines on AppWorld and ALFWorld. On 332 newly generated ToolQA tasks, it completes 256 with GPT-5.6-luna, significantly more than BM25, SkillRet-8B, Tool2Vec and RankGPT; over all 844 ToolQA tasks, it completes 24 more than the strongest baseline. Selection matters beyond relevance: pairing the right guide with a same-database sibling instead of another database's guide costs 8 of 96 tasks. Code, models and support data: https://github.com/satoshinji2992/CompSkill

papers.title: Zero-Gated Cross-Attention
papers.abstract: Injecting non-text modalities into frozen language models often introduces early optimization instability, making it difficult to separate architectural gains from transient training dynamics. We introduce Inductively Gated Cross-Attention (IGCA), a zero-initialized cross-attention bridge that preserves pretrained model behavior at initialization while enabling gradual multimodal conditioning. Integrated across six decoder layers of frozen Falcon-40B, open_llama_30b, and Bloom-7b1 backbones (with 40,404,961,288 trainable adapter parameters used during training), IGCA acts as an exact algebraic no-op at initialization with a maximum output discrepancy of 0.00e+00. Over 59,500 training steps on Falcon-40B, the training loss decreases from 3.9403 to 0.0007 (with final ten step losses of [0.0001, 0.0003, 0.0005, 0.0002, 0.0005, 0.0011, 0.0005, 0.0006, 0.0005, 0.0007]). On held-out evaluation, the best gate-on checkpoint achieves a loss of 2.2201 compared to 4.3469 for the gate-off baseline -- a 48.9% reduction (2.1268 nats) -- while average held-out loss improves from 4.3423 to 2.2498 (1.9075 nats) with a mean gate magnitude of $\vert{}\tanh(α)\vert{} = 0.0713$.

papers.title: LH$μ$C Concept: Energy-Frontier Antimuon-Proton Collisions at CERN
papers.abstract: The concept of the LH$μ$C, an energy-frontier antimuon-proton collider based on the HL-LHC, is presented. After recalling why energy-frontier lepton-hadron colliders are indispensable as QCD explorers and reviewing the history of muon-proton collider proposals, two ways of realising $μp$ collisions at the LHC are compared: with muon-collider beams and with ultra-cold $μ^+$ beams as proposed for $μ$TRISTAN. For the latter, a $μ$TRISTAN-type booster and the re-use of the LHeC energy-recovery-linac tunnel are discussed; colliding 1 TeV antimuons with 7 TeV protons gives $\sqrt{s}=5.3$ TeV and peak luminosities of $8.8\times10^{33}$ and $7.2\times10^{33}$ cm$^{-2}$s$^{-1}$, respectively. The detector concept and the physics potential, including searches for colour-octet muons and R-parity-violating squarks, are discussed together with the main challenges.

papers.title: Direct imaging of the Ni $e_g$ hole orbitals in the bilayer nickelate La$_2$SmNi$_2$O$_7$
papers.abstract: Models of unconventional superconductivity in cuprates and nickelates depend sensitively on the distribution of valence electrons among the $d$ orbitals. But accurately determining the orbital electron or hole occupations in these systems remains a difficult and unresolved task. Here, using $s$-core-level non-resonant inelastic x-ray scattering at the Ni $M_1$ edge, we determine the angular distribution of the Ni $3d$ holes in a single crystal of La$_2$SmNi$_2$O$_7$. Our results demonstrate that the hole occupation ratio $\hz/\hx = 0.94\pm0.06$, thus significantly above the expected value of $2/3$ for a filled $d_{z^2}$ orbitals models and close to value expected in a Hund's-coupling picture. Our results support superconductivity scenarios in which both $e_g$ orbitals contribute to the electron-pairing mechanism in La$_2$SmNi$_2$O$_7$.

papers.title: Nonlinear Physics and Self-Organized Criticality in Astrophysics
papers.abstract: The definition of self-organized criticality (SOC) is ambiguous and controversial. Here we discuss the nonlinear physics of six basic SOC definitions, such as: phase transitions, fractal structures, power laws, SOC contingency, exponential growth, and diffusive decay. Statistics of SOC events or avalanche processes can be inferred from their size distributions, or from their spatio-temporal evolution.

papers.title: StreamDuo: A Live Commentator and a Research Agent for Unseen Games
papers.abstract: Streaming video LLMs can now commentate live gameplay, but they are trained and tested on the same games. We study cross-game streaming commentary, in which a model trained on one game commentates games it has never seen, and find that current commentators transfer their timing but not their knowledge of the game world. We propose StreamDuo, which pairs a trainable commentator with a frozen research agent that reads the wiki of the game being played. When the commentator sees something it cannot name, it sends the current frames, and the research agent returns a few wiki entries two seconds later while the stream continues. We train only the commentator, on a single game, in two stages. Information-gain labels teach it to ask only where an answer would help it say what the human caster said, and on-policy self-distillation from a copy of itself that sees the ideal answer teaches it to use noisy answers. Trained on Baldur's Gate 3 and tested on ten unseen games, StreamDuo raises entity recall from 0.082 to 0.116 over Proact-VL trained on the same data, cuts source-game leakage from 9.9% to 1.0%, and achieves the best timing and the highest judged liveliness and overall quality among streaming models.

papers.title: Non-backtracking Laplacian for hypergraphs
papers.abstract: We extend the non-backtracking Laplacian for graphs, introduced by Jost, Mulas and Torres, to hypergraphs. The operator is defined on the permutations of the edges and is normalized by the number of edges through which a non-backtracking walk can continue. We show that it satisfies a symmetry that generalizes the graph case, and that it can be obtained from the random walk Laplacian of a directed graph by rescaling if and only if all edges have the same cardinality. Moreover, we show that, up to copies of the eigenvalue $1$, its spectrum can be computed from a much smaller matrix indexed by the incidences of the hypergraph, and we use this reduction to bound the remaining eigenvalues away from $1$.

papers.title: 3D Gaussian Splatting: A New Paradigm for Wireless Environment Representation
papers.abstract: Wireless channels are shaped by the surrounding propagation environment, making explicit environment representation an effective approach for characterizing channels. By combining explicit environment modeling with learnable radio frequency characteristics, 3D Gaussian splatting (3DGS) emerges as a new paradigm for wireless environment representation. This article establishes a systematic perspective on 3DGS-enabled wireless communications in terms of environment representation. We first clarify the rationale for extending 3DGS from visual scene modeling to wireless communications and formulate a unified framework for wireless environment representation. Building on this framework, we further investigate the applicability of 3DGS-based representations to a broad range of communication and sensing tasks, and characterize key considerations for practical deployment. Finally, emerging directions are highlighted, including cross-scene generalization, near-field channel modeling, real-world data collection, and lifecycle management.

papers.title: Do Earnings Calls Help Predict Financial Restatements? Evaluating Text Beyond Public Firm Information
papers.abstract: Financial restatements correct errors in previously published financial reports. Could managers' language in earnings calls warn of them in advance? Comparing 109 calls that precede restatements with 218 matched control calls, we find that the text predicts restatements but adds no detectable ranking gain beyond public firm information. A text classifier beats chance, largely because of restatements tied to special-purpose acquisition companies, but a model using only public information scores slightly higher. With refitting, the 95% interval for the gain from adding text (-0.05 to 0.11 AUROC) still leaves room for a meaningful benefit. A large language model scores higher, but we show that it names the exact ticker in 66% of masked transcripts, and it was released after the restatements occurred. Our results suggest that finding new warning signs in call text requires a public-information baseline and a check of what a language model already knows.

papers.title: Magnetic norm inflation below the velocity regularity threshold for viscous non-resistive MHD
papers.abstract: We study viscous, non-resistive magnetohydrodynamics on $\mathbb R^d$, $d\in\{2,3\}$. For every fixed magnetic exponent $s>d/2$ and every velocity exponent $q<s-1$, we prove norm inflation at the origin in $H^q\times H^s$. Arbitrarily small divergence-free Schwartz data generate classical solutions whose magnetic $H^s$ norm becomes arbitrarily large at arbitrarily small positive times, while the velocity remains arbitrarily small in $H^q$ throughout the observation interval. Together with endpoint local well-posedness, this identifies $q=s-1$ as the sharp lower velocity threshold for fixed $s>d/2$. The construction uses a symmetric pair of high-frequency velocity packets and a fixed low-frequency magnetic profile. A Fourier component of their stretching interaction has a fixed sign and gains the power $K^{s-1-q}$ on a short diffusive time scale. Subtracting an exact reference flow and using endpoint Besov estimates controls the full nonlinear remainder. Quantitative higher-order estimates ensure existence through the observation time and yield the uniform smallness of the velocity in the target norm.

papers.title: What Does a Safety Label Measure? Auditing Situational-Safety Benchmarks for Multimodal LLMs
papers.abstract: Situational-safety benchmarks label each scene SAFE or UNSAFE and score a multimodal large language model (MLLM) against that label, usually by judging its free-form answer, and these scores guide deployment. We ask what such a label measures. A label score can come from the scene, the request or the benchmark's own files. We propose the Benchmark Card, seven measured fields that tell them apart, and fill it for six benchmarks. Only MSSBench chat leaks the label through its image files: image size alone reaches 82.3% accuracy, matching or beating six of seven commercial models. Elsewhere the signal outside the scene comes from design. In MOSSBench the item partition fixes the label, and on HoliSafe the request alone ranks pairs about as well as the scene. On our corrected chat split, the size rule falls to chance. We then introduce the Spot-Stop decomposition, which compares ranking with labelling on pairs of a safe and an unsafe scene. It splits the gap above a label-swap null into three parts: a threshold part, overlap between safe and unsafe scores, and order that holds only within a pair. Most of fourteen open MLLMs rank better than they label, beyond what their AUROC predicts. On chat, one shared threshold repairs a third to a half of the excess, and label-free recentering recovers it on balanced batches. Recentering on unlabelled scenes of the same situation improves ranking on VSCBench for 13 of 14 models.

papers.title: Do GEO Gains Survive the Live Web? Evaluating In-the-Wild Visibility Gains of Generative Engine Optimization via LIVE-GEO
papers.abstract: Generative engine optimization (GEO) rewrites web content so that LLM-based search systems, also termed generative engines (GEs), rank it higher in their answers and recommendations. However, existing GEO evaluations typically rely on directly supplied text or controlled retrieval pipelines, and whether GEO gains survive the live Web remains unclear, leaving a gap in understanding how GEO strategies affect the visibility of live webpages when accessed and ranked by GEs. To address this gap, we introduce LIVE-GEO, a benchmark for Live, In-the-wild Visibility Evaluation for GEO. LIVE-GEO publishes GEO-rewritten products as live webpages. We use LIVE-GEO to evaluate five existing GEO strategies (CORE, C-SEO, E-GEO, AgenticGEO, and Statistics Addition), applying them to the product descriptions and reviews of 80 fictional brands across 18 product families. We run experiments on three GEs (ChatGPT with GPT-6, Gemini 3.6 Thinking, and Grok in Expert mode), four direct-text API evaluators (GPT-4o, DeepSeek, Kimi, and Claude), and a direct-text local evaluator (Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct). With frozen $\pm0.2\%$ prices, most direct-text evaluators and GEs receiving product URLs give CORE the highest Top-1 rate, reaching 66.3%-76.3% on the GEs, yet other strategies vary in relative performance, and the GEs select the same top product for only 48.8%-66.3% of brands. We also find that ChatGPT is sensitive to the order of candidate URLs: CORE's Top-1 rate is 73.8% and 93.8% under two opposite fixed orders, and the randomized order used by LIVE-GEO yields 82.5%, between the two. In the numerical-faithfulness check, the JEV verifier agrees with the reference labels on 90.7% of 194 numerical benchmark cases and with human judgments on all 50 sampled descriptions, and it flags 86 of the 400 rewritten descriptions, including all 80 Statistics Addition descriptions.

papers.title: What Must Be Done Here? Using a Bounded Application-Security Ontology at the Point of Change
papers.abstract: The security guidance that bears on code is real but scattered. It lives across secure-development frameworks, verification standards, controls catalogues, threat taxonomies, and, increasingly, normative regimes such as the EU's NIS2 -- and most of it is written for readers other than the engineer, or the AI assistant, at a point of change. Existing cybersecurity ontologies largely model attacks, indicators, and risk for detection and analysis, not the engineering-practice substance one must act on. This paper presents a use case for an existing bounded application-security ontology, AppSec Core, whose construction and validation are reported separately. We show how it is used. It makes the engineering-actionable fraction of those authorities addressable as a typed working set: the control objectives that apply, the practices that realize them, the mechanisms that implement them, and the evidence artifacts they expect, each traceable to the sources that justify it. We reach that working set from two entry points that recur in practice. Forward, from a code change: a change to authentication middleware scopes to its governing domain slice and returns the obligations the change must satisfy. Inverse, from a normative obligation: "make this NIS2-compliant" resolves a generic legal duty into the concrete engineering obligations it implies across slices, surfacing precisely the fraction of a mostly-governance regulation that lands in code. The same working set is what a human engineer reads and what an LLM-grounded assistant is handed as grounding. The use turns "read every applicable authority" into "satisfy this typed working set", for a code change or a compliance duty alike. The contribution is the demonstrated use; the artefact, its validation, and its governance are companion work.

papers.title: Some Characterisations of the Strichartz Fourier Transform on the Heisenberg Group
papers.abstract: Recently, Thangavelu introduced the Strichartz Fourier transform on the Heisenberg group. Around the same time, Krukowski characterised the classical Fourier transform on various settings, assuming a priori that the map is an integral transform, based on structural properties and a normalisation. In this paper, we obtain analogous results for the Strichartz Fourier transform, without assuming the characterised map is an integral transform. The spectral property is formulated jointly for the sublaplacian and central vector field, and the translation property uses a twisted form of left translation. The joint spectral property, the twisted translation property and a normalisation at one explicit test function, together characterise the transform on each ray of the Heisenberg fan. The twisted translation property, paired with a Dirac delta property, gives another characterisation. We characterise the radial kernel on each ray by a Laguerre-type differential equation. This gives a characterisation of the Hankel transform.

papers.title: HiGenTrans: Hierarchical LLM Knowledge Transfer for Generative Recommendation
papers.abstract: Generative recommendation promises to simplify conventional multi-stage recommender systems by generating item Semantic IDs (SIDs) autoregressively. However, two obstacles limit its effective- ness in industrial settings: interaction-only supervision underuses the semantic knowledge encoded in pretrained language models, while beam-search likelihood ranks token sequences rather than directly estimating item relevance. To address these limitations, we propose HiGenTrans, a three-level framework that introduces LLM knowledge at the input, representation, and decision levels. First, Global Semantic Priming (GSP) adds an LLM-derived user representation to the beginning-of-sequence embedding, provid- ing a semantic prior before SID generation. Second, Hierarchi- cal Representation Transfer (HRT) aligns intermediate LLM representations with depth-matched GenRec layers through mean- centered projections and gated residual connections. Finally, Multi- Signal Decision Calibration (MDC) uses a lightweight mixture- of-experts calibrator to combine semantic relevance, generation confidence, and candidate-set context when reranking beam-search outputs. All semantic features are computed only from the observ- able interaction prefix, preventing target leakage, and can be cached offline. Experiments on three public benchmarks show that HiGen- Trans improves Recall@10 by up to 12.9% and NDCG@10 by up to 33.7% over the strongest baselines. These results demonstrate the value of transferring LLM knowledge at complementary stages of the generative recommendation pipeline.

papers.title: Local and global conservation laws of partial differential equations on moving domains in three dimensions
papers.abstract: For PDE systems in three spatial dimensions, firstly, a review of the various types of global conservation laws --- volumetric, surface-flux, circulatory --- is given using vector calculus, and their corresponding local forms --- divergence, curl, gradient --- are explained. Secondly, an extension of each type of conservation law to moving domains is presented, where the domain --- volume, surface, curve --- is transported by a prescribed velocity field. This provides a generalization of Reynolds' transport theorem known for material domains in which the velocity field is the fluid velocity. The main results are illustrated by numerous physical examples taken from gas dynamics, fluid flow, nonlinear acoustics, chemotaxis, plasma dynamics, and also Maxwell's equations, which do not involve any physically specified velocity field. As an additional main result, an extension of the multiplier method for finding local conservation laws of divergence-type is presented for local curl-type and gradient-type conservation laws on both static and moving domains.

papers.title: Extended Onsager's variational principle for nonlinear chemical reaction kinetics in active matter
papers.abstract: Onsager's variational principle (OVP) constructs dissipative dynamics from free energy, dissipation, and input power, but deterministic rate laws alone do not identify fluctuations or chemical fuel consumption. We examine these distinctions for nonlinear reaction kinetics in active matter. Comparing Gaussian diffusion and Poisson reaction events clarifies when statistical fluctuations match a physical Rayleighian: the reaction dissipation potential must be consistent with counting statistics, local detailed balance links rate bias to chemical affinity, and kinetic scales remain constitutive inputs. Under these conditions, the normalized Rayleighian excess gives the leading rate-fluctuation cost in the frozen-state, many-event regime. Three models illustrate the consequences. Spatially uniform reactions exhibit protocol-dependent nonreciprocal response compatible with fixed-state OVP; different Rayleighian representations can select the same rate without specifying the same fluctuations. In an active emulsion, a finite fuel pool accounts for free-energy transfer and dissolution of a chemically maintained domain after replenishment stops. In a membrane-cytosol model, distinct reaction-channel realizations yield identical protein-density trajectories but different chemical input power. Under a separate kinetic assumption, an exact total-density equation still requires an initial rate and does not determine chemical work or fluctuations. These results clarify the physical and statistical inputs required for constructing reaction-transport models and interpreting their fluctuations.

papers.title: Acceptance and Responsibility Attribution Toward Autonomous Ambulances Across Driving Conditions: A Preliminary Survey of Fire Service Personnel
papers.abstract: Traffic incidents involving ambulances and fire engines during emergency-response driving can have serious consequences. Although autonomous driving technologies may reduce workload and improve safety, their introduction into emergency services requires consideration of first responders' trust, willingness to ride (WTR), and perceptions of responsibility. We surveyed 34 fire service personnel from a single fire station in Himeji, Japan, to examine their evaluations of autonomous ambulances and responsibility attribution under non-emergency and emergency driving conditions. Emergency driving was associated with lower perceived usefulness for improving safety, trust, and WTR, as well as greater anxiety. In contrast, responsibility attribution remained largely stable, with 30 participants ($88.2\%$) selecting the same primary responsible party across conditions and the onboard crew most frequently selected in both. Among these 30 participants, 26 ($86.7\%$) also assigned the same responsibility share. Open-ended responses revealed concerns about system reliability, the complexity of emergency driving, and the need for human judgment, as well as considerations regarding operator and organizational responsibility. These findings suggest that acceptance of autonomous ambulances is sensitive to driving conditions, while responsibility judgments may also reflect perceived professional roles and responsibilities.

papers.title: Rethinking LLM Pruning via Test-Time Scaling
papers.abstract: Structured pruning reduces the size of large language models, often at the cost of lower accuracy. Whether this decline reflects diminished reasoning capacity or greater difficulty in sampling correct solutions is less clear. We examine this question across expert, FFN and layer pruning on four mathematical and coding benchmarks, comparing original and pruned models through pass@k at matched sampling budgets. Even after substantial pruning, some models match or exceed the original model's reasoning coverage despite lower pass@1, and solve problems left unsolved in the original samples. Retaining broad coverage, however, does not mean that correct solutions remain easy to obtain. Under severe pruning, diverse generated chain-of-thought (CoT) traces can coexist with increased repetition and less reliable generation. As correct answers become harder to sample, the additional attempts can sharply increase total token use even when individual responses become shorter. This separation between coverage and sampling efficiency also clarifies expert-selection gains, as methods with markedly different pass@1 can solve the same problems at large budgets yet require different numbers of attempts to reach a common coverage target. Pruning should therefore be assessed by both the range of problems a model can still solve and the sampling cost of obtaining correct solutions.

papers.title: Selective inference for pruned interaction trees with known unequal variances in randomized trials
papers.abstract: Interaction trees reuse outcomes to discover treatment-effect heterogeneity, complicating inference after growth and pruning. We develop selective inference for generalized least-squares (GLS) interaction trees with a common covariate basis and known unequal variances. Under a conditional Gaussian model with positive diagonal covariance, weighted orthogonality reduces survival under additive fixed-penalty pruning to one quadratic inequality supplementing the growth event. This yields exact finite-sample conditional tests and confidence intervals, with retained-path and complete-tree inference agreeing on compatible sections. Under causal identification and a correct reference prognosis, the pruning-invariant GLS target is a signed finite-design weighted contrast of conditional average treatment effects. Simulations at $n=100,200,400,800$ and maximum depths one to three search all adjacent-observation midpoints, support calibration and demonstrate over-rejection when pruning survival is omitted. Compared with a 50:50 honest procedure, full-data learning improves reference-split recovery in some small-sample settings. Root-level median intervals can be shorter, while deep-node intervals and upper tails can be much wider; these comparisons concern each procedure's selected targets. Estimating a common scale with the variance ratio fixed produces modest changes in Selective coverage in the settings examined, without extending the exact guarantee. An exploratory ACTG 175 analysis provides a working-model illustration with estimated arm variances.

papers.title: Compile as Hypothesis: A Headroom Typology for Prompt Optimization on Real Reasoning Models
papers.abstract: Automated prompt compilers search for or rewrite prompts under the implicit assumption that optimization consistently improves downstream task performance. We evaluate this assumption on frontier reasoning models through rigorous paired, same-day measurements. Across four optimizer families (genome search, profile-guided mutation, GEPA, and ESPO) and eight tasks, structured search yields no statistically significant accuracy gains on strong reasoners. However, a discrete structural genome provides essential architectural stability, preventing catastrophic bimodal seed-collapse (where unconstrained search collapses toward the judge floor in 3/5 runs). Through 190-problem evaluations on knowledge-intensive benchmarks, we establish a three-dimensional headroom typology: prompt optimization cannot compensate for intrinsic knowledge deficits or physical token truncation, but successfully resolves protocol and formatting errors. On gpt-6, while free-text reflective search (GEPA) yields a +.14 gain on a task where structured search remains flat, qualitative ablation reveals that ~.035 stems from judge-rubric reconstruction while ~.105 reflects genuine instruction refinement. Our pre-registered AutoAPC-Select deployment gate matches the oracle policy in 5/7 groups and rescues seed-collapse arms with zero regret. Finally, we expose silent backend-mixing in commercial APIs during outage windows and provide automated per-call audit verification tools to ensure empirical evaluation fidelity.

papers.title: SIDRec: End-to-End Semantic ID Representation and Modeling for Recommendation
papers.abstract: Semantic IDs (SIDs) have emerged as a promising approach for discriminative recommendation by encoding continuous item rep- resentations into compact discrete identifiers. However, existing SID-based methods face two fundamental limitations: semantic mis- match between content semantics and collaborative preferences, and objective mismatch between SID construction and downstream recommendation optimization. To address these challenges, we propose SIDRec, an end-to-end recommendation-aware SID learn- ing framework that jointly models content and collaborative in- formation while aligning SID construction with recommendation objectives. Specifically, SIDRec introduces a self-updating fusion mechanism that explicitly integrates pretrained content represen- tations with collaborative embeddings initialized from a trained recommendation model, enabling preference-aware semantic mod- eling. Furthermore, SIDRec employs an MMoE-inspired joint opti- mization mechanism with shared experts and task-specific gates, allowing recommendation supervision to directly guide differen- tiable quantization and produce task-adaptive discrete representa- tions. Extensive experiments on three public benchmark datasets demonstrate that SIDRec consistently outperforms all competing methods across both AUC and GAUC, achieving up to 5.15% relative improvements over the strongest baselines. Further ablation stud- ies validate the effectiveness and complementarity of collaborative semantic modeling and end-to-end SID optimization.

papers.title: Local superderivations of Block Lie superalgebras $S(q)$
papers.abstract: We prove that every even or odd local superderivation of the Block Lie superalgebra $S(q)$ is a superderivation for every $q\in\mathbb{C}$, with both basis indices ranging over $\mathbb{Z}$. The superderivations used in the local condition have the same parity as the map. The proofs use the known description of homogeneous superderivations, bracket computations, and coefficient comparisons.

papers.title: Seshadri functions on surfaces
papers.abstract: We study the Seshadri function on the ample cone of a smooth complex projective surface at a fixed point. At a submaximal class, we show that the function is differentiable if and only if there is a unique Seshadri curve. At a maximal class $L$, differentiability is equivalent to every curve $C$ computing the Seshadri constant satisfying $\frac{[C]}{{\rm mult}_x C}=\frac{[L]}{\sqrt{L^{2}}}$. We also prove that the non-differentiability locus is nowhere dense. For the blow-up of $\mathbb P^{2}$ at $r\ge 9$ very general points, assuming the $(-1)$-curves conjecture for the blow-up at $r+1$ very general points, we construct a non-empty open subset of the ample cone on which the Seshadri function at a very general point equals $\sqrt{L^{2}}$. Consequently, this function is not piecewise linear. Under the assumption of the Strong SHGH conjecture, we obtain a common non-empty open subset on which maximality holds at every point when $r\ge36$.

papers.title: World Models Need Not Be Right to Rank Policies Right: Relative Bounds and Audit Limits
papers.abstract: Selecting a reinforcement-learning (RL) policy usually requires additional environment interaction, while learned world models offer cheap but potentially biased evaluations. This raises two distinct questions: can shared model errors preserve pairwise rankings despite poor absolute values, and do they make a small number of real audits more informative? We derive an exact pairwise simulation identity and a relative bound separating common-mode Bellman residuals from policy-specific error. The analysis motivates RAVEL (Relative Auditing of Value Errors in Learned models), a selective policy tournament whose eliminations use held-out real outcomes. We test 45 SAC, TD3, and PPO policies per task in DMC cheetah-run and walker-walk. At rollout horizon 500, model rankings remain strong (Kendall tau = 0.962 and 0.800), and same-run differential-error ratios are 0.674 and 0.106. Yet mean paired audit-error correlations are only 0.007 and 0.090, and pairing changes standard deviation by -2.5 percent and +1.9 percent. Simultaneous intervals attain 99.98 percent and 99.75 percent coverage, but certify only 13.2 percent and 0 percent of decisions at eight audits. RAVEL improves low-budget walker-walk regret, whereas real-only successive halving is better at the largest budget, rejecting the precommitted twofold efficiency target. Frozen-model optimization lowers real return without increasing predicted return on average. Thus ranking fidelity, useful audit covariance, and upward model exploitation are distinct properties, separated in part by closed-loop trajectory divergence.

papers.title: EMG-Hybrid: A Dual-Engine Elite Memory--Guided Adaptive Optimization Framework for High-Dimensional Feature Selection
papers.abstract: Feature selection in ultra-high-dimensional, noisy datasets remains a critical challenge due to exponential search space growth, where conventional binary metaheuristics often suffer from premature convergence. To address this, EMG-Hybrid is introduced as a novel three-level hierarchical optimization architecture designed around decoupled operational planes, feedback-driven scheduling, and isolated state refinement. At Level 1, a Dual-Engine Controller monitors population Shannon entropy and empirical fitness velocity, functioning as an architectural master-switch that dynamically routes execution between global exploration and local intensification. This control loop conditions the Level 2 active optimization plane, where an Adaptive Black Hole Gravity (ABHG) execution layer performs aggressive feature manifold pruning via a distance-decoupled penalty kernel driven by fitness similarities and Hamming metrics. To structurally isolate macro-exploration from micro-exploitation, Level 3 encapsulates an autonomous Elite Memory Archive that preserves high-fidelity sub-schemas and hosts a discrete bitwise Differential Evolution (DE) micro-refinement sandbox for resolving complex parameter epistasis. Theoretically, uniform combinatorial bounds derived via Vapnik--Chervonenkis (VC) dimension criteria demonstrate that this multi-level restriction mitigates high-dimensional overfitting. Empirical results across manifolds scaling up to $d > 100{,}000$ features, complemented by high-performance computing (HPC) profiling under lock-free atomic Compare-and-Swap (CAS) primitives, indicate strong performance gains over state-of-the-art baselines. The framework exhibits near-linear parallel speedups, sub-quadratic runtime scaling, and substantial dimensionality reduction, offering a scalable and structurally innovative paradigm for large-scale data mining.

papers.title: GESTALT: Fast, Generalizable Histopathology Image Synthesis from Gene Expression with Pretrained Pathology Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics measures gene expression while preserving where each cell sits in the tissue. The inverse, what a given transcriptomic state looks like, is less explored but equally useful: it lets researchers visualize the morphological consequence of a molecular state and interpret a spatial assay's molecular calls against real tissue structure. GeneFlow, the current state of the art on the Xenium gene expression-to-image benchmark, trains a model from scratch, incurring a high cost on every new target dataset it is applied to. We instead propose GESTALT, which reformulates gene expression-to-image synthesis as predicting a pathology foundation model's image embedding. A lightweight gene-token transformer predicts this embedding from multi-cell gene expression, and a frozen or LoRA-adapted diffusion decoder (PixCell) renders it as an image. Because this visual knowledge is reused rather than relearned, GESTALT trains in a fraction of the time. In both multi-cell and single-cell settings, our method outperforms the SoTA on perceptual metrics across all three Xenium datasets. Beyond improved image quality, GESTALT natively synthesizes at 1024 x 1024, and is evaluated in three generalization settings: zero-shot transfer across gene panels and datasets, held-out patients and disease states, and transfer across studies and tissue sources. Coupled with a statistical model of spatial expression, GESTALT also provides, to our knowledge, the first paired synthesis of cell-resolved transcriptomic fields and tissue images with explicit control over cell type, density, and composition. Code is available at https://github.com/trongnhandev1011/Gestalt.

papers.title: A Game of Scales
papers.abstract: These notes cover the material of two courses given at SISSA, Trieste, in the academic years 2023-2024 and 2025-2026, together with some material from courses taught in other recent years. The original idea behind these courses emerged from conversations with Andrea Causin and Margherita Solci about the somewhat elusive notion of `multiscale behaviour', which arises in the study of variational problems involving one or more small parameters. Two main mechanisms govern their asymptotic behaviour: concentration and oscillations. Their description is often associated with the emergence of a characteristic `scale', quantifying either the speed of concentration or the period of an optimal oscillation. These mechanisms may originate from different variational principles and may occur separately, coexist, compete, or interact, thus providing a natural interpretation of the term `multiscale'. This perspective inspired the informal title of the courses, which also became the title of these notes. The natural framework for these analyses is $Γ$-convergence. However, these notes are not intended as a general introduction to this now well-established theory. We provide only a brief account of the techniques relevant to our purposes, referring the reader to the author's book chapter {\em A Handbook of $Γ$-convergence}. For a broader introduction to $Γ$-convergence, and in particular to its topological properties, the standard reference is Dal Maso's monograph {\em An Introduction to $Γ$-convergence}.

papers.title: GSLM2: Multi-Stream Speech Representation Learning and Generative Spoken Language Modeling
papers.abstract: Generative spoken language models (SLMs) offer a route to learning linguistic structure purely from speech, yet they lag far behind text-based models in both capability and data scaling efficiency. We identify two bottlenecks underlying this gap: the limited linguistic quality of existing speech units and the reliance on a single stream of discrete units to represent speech. Multiple codebooks are widely used to encode acoustic features but rarely to represent speech semantics. We present GSLM2, which learns and models complementary properties of speech at multiple levels of abstraction. Its encoder, SpidR 2.0, uses self-supervised learning with differentiable prediction heads to induce high-quality discrete units at multiple levels. A multi-stream SLM then jointly models these units using a shared temporal backbone, stream-specific predictors, and an autoregressive head that captures cross-stream dependencies. Across training data sizes and model scales, up to 6M hours and 6.5B parameters, GSLM2 consistently improves linguistic competence while scaling more efficiently with data. As a result, it substantially narrows the gap between spoken and text-based LMs; across read and conversational speech domains, we shrink the gap by about two orders of magnitude on sWuggy, sBLIMP, and tSC, while also outperforming competitive speech-text systems on all three tasks. We open-source the training code and model checkpoints at https://github.com/facebookresearch/gslm2.

papers.title: Side-Channel Attack Prevention for Post Quantum Cryptography Algorithms: A 3D-Shield Approach
papers.abstract: Despite their theoretical quantum attack resistance, practical implementations of post-quantum cryptography (PQC) algorithms remain susceptible to side-channel attacks. This includes all standard algorithms selected the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) such as Kyber/ML-KEM, Dilithium/ML-DSA, Falcon/FN-DSA and SPHINCS+/SLH-DSA. This paper proposes an alternative defense for side-channel resilience based on 3D integration that uses 3D hardware to shield the underlying cryptographic activity by introducing decoy keys and physical shielding through stacking. The proposed approach can complement other security measures (such as masking and shuffling) on protecting Number Theoretic Transform (NTT) that move computation to dedicated NTT chips. We outline the construction of our approach and validate the effectiveness on a generic attack targeting intermediate computation inside an NTT butterfly.

papers.title: CivicBench: A Benchmark and Memory Framework for Web-Based Civic Data Analytics
papers.abstract: Municipalities publish service requests, geographic boundaries, weather observations, demographic estimates, and operational guidance through independently maintained Web portals. Civic analysis must combine these sources while preserving their schemas, source links, spatial and temporal scopes, and interpretive limits. Tool-using language agents can perform this integration, but existing task benchmarks rarely test whether a computed claim remains supported by the records used. We present CivicBench, a 400-task benchmark over four cities and two years that materializes civic Web data into frozen bundles for reproducible evaluation. Executable contracts score computation, source linkage, coverage, scope, qualified answers, and refusal when the requested conclusion is not supported. We also introduce Task-State Memory (TSM), which compiles tool observations into typed assertions, reconciles records only within compatible scopes, and retrieves a bounded state organized around unresolved constraints. Across nine completed model pairs, eight yield positive mean-score differences with 95\% semantic-contract-cluster bootstrap intervals excluding zero; the ninth interval crosses zero. The benchmark and memory framework make the records behind a claim inspectable at the point of decision.

papers.title: A polynomial-size logical twin for neural networks
papers.abstract: A logical twin of a neural network is a logical representation that mimics the computation of the network through logical formulas. We revisit two earlier proposals for constructing logical twins of feedforward neural networks in Łukasiewicz logic, both of which are susceptible to exponential blow-up in running time and representation size. Building on ideas from both approaches, we present a new construction that directly yields logical twins in Łukasiewicz logic. We show that this construction can be computed in polynomial time and produces polynomial-size logical twins. Finally, we report an empirical evaluation of the three methods, showing that the new proposal substantially outperforms the other two.

papers.title: Rel2Traj: Inter-Source Relation-Aware Trajectory Generation for Text-To-Spatial-Audio
papers.abstract: "A car drives from front left to front right while a dog follows it." Such a description specifies no particular trajectory, yet imposes a constraint on the joint motion of both sources that must hold at every frame. Existing text-to-spatial-audio methods can position and move each sound source according to its description, but none of them ensures or verifies that such inter-source relations hold. We therefore propose Rel2Traj, which parses the description into sources, relations, and anchors, jointly generates the trajectories of all sources using a relation-conditioned diffusion model, and finally renders sounds from a pretrained text-to-audio model along these trajectories to produce binaural audio. For training and evaluation, we construct a synthetic dataset from a controlled language of source motions and inter-source relations. A single frame-wise relational geometry defines both our evaluation metric, the Relation Satisfaction Rate (RSR), and an auxiliary training loss. On motion-relation combinations held out from training, Rel2Traj maintains all relation types, whereas every baseline fails on at least one. A listening test further confirms that listeners recognize the described relations. To our knowledge, this is the first text-to-spatial-audio work to model relations among moving sources as explicit geometric constraints.

papers.title: Enumeration of plane hypermaps with a mixed boundary II
papers.abstract: A plane hypermap with a boundary is a connected graph embedded in the plane with a distinguished face, and whose inner faces are properly face-bicolored. We say that such hypermaps are k-alternating if the colors of the faces adjacent to the distinguished face alternate at most 2k times when going counterclockwise. Eynard and Orantin, in [EO2005], have found a universal expression for the generating functions of k-alternating hypermaps as a surprisingly simple function of the generating function of 1-alternating hypermaps. In this article, we will provide combinatorial formulas for k-alternating hypermaps using specific subclasses of hypermaps in which each vertex can either be connected to a previously marked vertex, called accessible, or connected to all other vertices in what we call a blob. In particular, this method will allow us to derive the results from [EO2005] from a combinatorial perspective, and we anticipate that it will lead to the computation of asymptotics for hypermaps in future work. This article is naturally a sequel to, and most importantly a generalization of, the results in [BEL26], which deals essentially with the case of 1- and 2-alternating hypermaps.

papers.title: Functions of $\boldsymbol{S}_p$-almost commuting unitary operators and contractions. An extension of the Carey--Pincus trace formula
papers.abstract: In this paper we study functions of pairs of unitary operators and pairs of contractions with commutators in the Schatten-von Neumann class $\boldsymbol{S}_p$. We obtain commutator estimates and prove that our functional calculus is multiplicative modulo $\boldsymbol{S}_p$. On the other hand, we show that our commutator estimates do not extend to the case $p>2$. We also obtain an extension of the Carey--Pincus trace formula. The main tool of this paper is a technique of triple operator integrals.

papers.title: Enhancing Edge AI System Security with a Stacked Hardware Security Controller for Robust and Energy-Efficient Anomaly Detectio
papers.abstract: In recent years, the growing adoption of Edge AI systems has been accompanied by a surge in security threats. Edge AI deployments face an rapidly evolving spectrum of security threats, from side-channel information leakage to ad- versarial model manipulation and physical device tampering. Conventional security mechanisms such as malware scanners and resource-intensive firewall solutions are unsuitable due to edge AIs typically limited computational resources, strict energy budgets and thermal constraints especially in battery-powered and field-deployed environments. This paper proposes a stacked, hardware-based security mechanism that enables low-overhead, continuous detection of anomalous execution patterns. Anomaly detection utilizing hard- ware performance counters and physical sensors outperforms software-based alternatives by providing key capabilities such as tamper-resistant root-of-trust isolation, negligible runtime overhead, and resilience against compromised operating systems. Experimental analysis shows that adversarial or malicious ap- plications produce observable deviations in sensor and thermal readings on Edge AI systems and hardware-based anomaly detection provides effective and low-overhead anomaly detection.

papers.title: Robust Optimization in Stochastic Games
papers.abstract: A player's impatient valuation of an infinite stream of stage payoffs is a weighted average with nonincreasing weights. Such valuations generalize geometric discounting and allow imprecise or heterogeneous time preferences. For a stochastic game \(Γ\) and a profile \(u\) of impatient valuations, let \(Γ_u\) be the induced game. We ask when approximately optimal or equilibrium behavior can be chosen to vary continuously and stably with \(u\).
